(Section)
Since stumbling has two kinds, the stumbling of the foot and the stumbling of the tongue, the one is placed alongside the other in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [al-Furqan: 63].

He described them as upright in their utterances and in their steps, just as He combined glances and passing thoughts in His saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.﴾ [Ghafir: 19].

All of this we have mentioned as an introduction before the prohibition of indecency and the obligation of guarding the private parts. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The most common thing that causes people to enter the Fire is the mouth and the private part."

In the two Sahihs, from him (ﷺ): "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in one of three cases: the married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community." This hadith, in linking fornication with disbelief and killing a soul, is a parallel to the verse in al-Furqan and a parallel to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began with what is most frequent in occurrence, and then what follows it: fornication is more frequent than killing a soul, and killing a soul is more frequent than apostasy. Moreover, he moved from the greater to what is greater than it. The corruption of fornication contradicts the wellbeing of the world, for when a woman commits fornication she brings shame upon her family, her husband and her relatives, and she causes their heads to be bowed among the people. If she becomes pregnant from fornication and then kills her child, she has combined fornication and killing; and if she attributes the child to the husband, she introduces into his family and her family a stranger who is not of them, so that he inherits from them though he is not of them, sees them and is alone with them, and attributes himself to them though he is not of them, along with other corruptions of her fornication.

As for a man's fornication, it also necessitates the confusion of lineages, the corruption of a chaste woman, and exposing her to ruin and corruption. In this great sin is the ruin of both the world and the religion, and even if it populates the graves in the barzakh and the Fire in the Hereafter, how much in fornication is there of making lawful what is sacred, the loss of rights, and the commission of injustices?

Among its distinctive characteristics: it causes poverty, shortens life, clothes its doer with blackness of face and the garment of hatred among people.

Among its distinctive characteristics also: it scatters the heart and sickens it, if it does not kill it; it brings worry, grief and fear; it distances its doer from the angel and brings him near to Satan. There is no corruption greater than the corruption of killing after it, and for this reason the punishment for it was prescribed in the most abominable, most vile and most severe manner. Were a servant to learn that his wife or his womenfolk had been killed, it would be easier for him than to learn that she had committed fornication.

Sa'd ibn Ubadah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword, not turning it aside." This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Do you marvel at Sa'd's jealousy? By Allah, I am more jealous than he, and Allah is more jealous than I; and because of Allah's jealousy He forbade indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden." Agreed upon.

In the two Sahihs also, from him (ﷺ): "Allah is jealous, and the believer is jealous, and the jealousy of Allah is when a servant does what Allah has forbidden him."

In the two Sahihs, from him (ﷺ): "There is none more jealous than Allah; for this reason He forbade indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. And there is none more fond of excuse than Allah; for this reason He sent the Messengers as bearers of good news and warners. And there is none more fond of praise than Allah; for this reason He praised Himself."

In the two Sahihs, in his (ﷺ) sermon at the eclipse prayer, he said: "O community of Muhammad, by Allah, there is none more jealous than Allah that His servant should commit fornication or His female servant should commit fornication. O community of Muhammad, by Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, have I conveyed?"

In mentioning this particular great sin right after the eclipse prayer there is a wonderful secret for whoever reflects upon it, and the appearance of fornication is among the signs of the ruin of the world and among the portents of the Hour, as in the two Sahihs from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "I shall narrate to you a hadith that no one will narrate to you after me; I heard it from the Prophet (ﷺ) saying: Among the portents of the Hour is that knowledge will be raised, ignorance will appear, wine will be drunk, fornication will appear, men will become few and women many, until for fifty women there will be one guardian."

The sunnah of Allah, glorified is He, in His creation has been that when fornication appears, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, becomes angry and His anger intensifies, so His anger must have an effect upon the earth as a punishment.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "Usury and fornication do not appear in a town except that Allah permits its destruction."

One of the rabbis of the Children of Israel saw his son touching a woman, and said: "Gently, my son." The father was thrown from his couch, his spinal cord was severed, and his wife miscarried. It was said to him: "Is this how your anger is for Me? There will never be any good in your kind."

Glorified is He, among the hudud, singled out the hadd of fornication with three distinctive features:

The first: killing is in it by the most abominable kinds of killing; and where He lightened it, He combined in it punishment upon the body by flogging and upon the heart by exile from one's homeland for a year.

The second: He forbade His servants to let compassion for the fornicators prevent them from establishing the hadd upon them in His religion, so that they would not be prevented from carrying it out. For He, glorified is He, out of His tenderness toward them and His mercy for them, prescribed this punishment; so He is more merciful to you, and His mercy did not prevent Him from commanding this punishment. So let not the compassion that stirs in your hearts prevent you from carrying out His command.

This, although it is general across all the hudud, was mentioned specifically in the hadd of fornication because of the great need to mention it, for people do not find in their hearts toward the fornicator the harshness and severity that they find toward the thief, the slanderer, and the drinker of wine. Their hearts show more mercy to the fornicator than to others among the perpetrators of crimes, and reality bears witness to this. So they were forbidden to let this compassion take hold of them and lead them to suspend Allah's hadd.

The reason for this mercy is that this is a sin that occurs among the nobles, the middling and the lowly; the strongest motives toward it are in souls, many share in it, and most of its causes are passionate love. Hearts are naturally inclined to show mercy to the lover, and many people regard assisting him as obedience and a means of drawing near to Allah, even if the beloved is forbidden to him, and do not find this matter strange. It is established among the kinds of cattle that Allah wills, and many of the weak-minded, such as servants and women, have related to us a great deal of this.

Also, this sin usually occurs with mutual consent from both sides, and there is not in it the aggression, injustice and rape that repel souls.

Souls have an overwhelming desire for it, and so it presents this to them, and mercy arises within them that prevents the establishment of the hadd. All of this is from weakness of faith. The perfection of faith is that there arise in it strength by which one establishes the command of Allah, and mercy by which one shows mercy to the one being punished; thus one agrees with one's Lord, may He be exalted, in His command and His mercy.

The third: He, glorified is He, commanded that their punishment be carried out in the presence of a group of believers, so that it is not done in seclusion where no one sees them, and this is more effective for the interest of the hadd, since its wisdom is deterrence. The hadd of the married fornicator derives from Allah's punishment of the people of Lut by casting stones, because fornication and sodomy are shared in indecency, and in each of them is a corruption that contradicts Allah's wisdom in His creation and His command. In sodomy there are corruptions that exceed count and enumeration, and it is better for the one who is penetrated to be killed than to be penetrated, for he is corrupted with a corruption after which no righteousness is hoped for him ever again, all his goodness is lost, the earth sucks the water of modesty from his face, so that thereafter he is not shy before Allah or before His creation, and the seed of the doer works in his heart and spirit as poison works in the body.

[The wisdom in the hadd of fornication and its variation]

As for the fornicator, he commits fornication with his whole body, and the enjoyment of fulfilling his desire pervades the body; and most of the time his act occurs with the consent of the one fornicated with, so he is not fearful of what the thief fears of pursuit. Therefore he is punished with what pervades his body: flogging once, and stoning to death once. And since fornication is among the mothers of crimes and the greatest of sins, because of the confusion of lineages in it, through which acquaintance and mutual support for reviving the religion are nullified, and because in it is the destruction of tillage and offspring, it resembles in its meanings, or in most of them, killing, which entails the destruction of these, so it is restrained by retaliation, so that whoever intends to do the like is deterred. Thus this returns to the building up of the world and the wellbeing of the world, which leads to the establishment of worships that lead to the bliss of the Hereafter.

Then the fornicator has two states:

The first: that he is muhsan (married), who has married, and so he knows what chastity from forbidden private parts achieves, and he is made independent of them by it, and he protects himself from exposing himself to the hadd of fornication. So his excuse is removed in every respect in overstepping that to engaging in what is forbidden.

The second: that he is a virgin (bikr), who has not known what the muhsan knew and has not done what the muhsan did; so there is granted to him from the excuse some of what made the lightening of the punishment necessary. Thus his blood is preserved, and he is deterred by inflicting pain upon his whole body with the highest kind of flogging, as a restraint against returning to enjoyment of what is forbidden, and as an incitement for him to be content with what Allah has provided him of what is lawful.

This is in the utmost wisdom and interest, combining leniency in its place and severity in its place.

And where is this from cutting off the tongue of the reviler and the slanderer, and what is in it of excess and aggression?

Moreover, cutting off the private part of the fornicator involves the cessation of offspring, and cutting it is the opposite of the Lord's purpose, may He be exalted, in multiplying progeny and their descendants through the wives He has made for them. In it are corruptions many times over what is imagined as an interest of deterrence. In it is also the leaving of the whole body free of punishment, though the crime of fornication has occurred with all its parts; so it is part of justice that the punishment should encompass it all. Furthermore, it is inconceivable in the case of a woman, and both are fornicators; so they must be equal in punishment. Thus the legislation of Allah, glorified is He, is more perfect than the proposals of those who propose.

[Section: Sins are a path to destruction]

Among their punishments: they draw in the material causes of the servant's destruction in his world and his Hereafter. For sins are sicknesses; when they become entrenched they kill, without fail. Just as the body is not sound except with nourishment that preserves its strength, and with purging that expels the corrupt matters and the bad humors, which when they predominate corrupt it, and with a regimen by which it guards against what harms it and fears its damage, so too the heart's life is not complete except with nourishment of faith and righteous deeds that preserve its strength, and with purging by sincere repentance that expels the corrupt matters and bad humors from it, and with a regimen that makes necessary the preservation of health and the avoidance of what opposes it, and this is the expression for employing what is contrary to health.

Piety is a term that encompasses these three matters, so whatever of them is lost, piety is lost to the same measure.

When this is made clear, sins oppose these three matters, for they draw in harmful matter, necessitate the excess that opposes the regimen, and prevent the purging by sincere repentance.

Look at a sick body in which sick humors and matter of disease have accumulated, which neither purges them nor observes a regimen for them: how could its health and survival be? The poet has said well:

"You have guarded your body with a regimen, out of fear of a sudden pain,
And it would have been more fitting for you to fear, from sins, the fear of the Creator."

So whoever preserves strength by complying with the commands, practices the regimen by avoiding the prohibitions, and purges the excess by sincere repentance, will leave no good unsought and no evil unfled. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

[Section: The legal punishments for sins]

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 24, verse 2 (part 2 of 3):**

If these punishments do not deter you and you find no effect of them on your heart, then bring before yourself the legal punishments (*'uqubat shar'iyya*) that Allah and His Messenger prescribed for crimes. He cut off the hand for the theft of three dirhams. He cut off the hand and the foot for highway robbery against a person's protected property and life. He lashed the skin with the whip for a word of slander (*qadhf*) cast against a *muhsan* (a chaste, married person), or for a drop of wine that a person puts into his stomach. He stoned to death, in the most grievous manner of execution, the one who inserts the glans into a forbidden private part. He lightened this punishment for the one upon whom the blessing of *ihsan* (marriage) has not been completed, to one hundred lashes and a year of exile from his homeland and his town to a land of estrangement. He separated the head of a slave from his body when he had intercourse with a woman within his prohibited degrees of kinship. He (ordered punishment for) one who abandons the obligatory prayer, or who speaks a word of disbelief. He ordered the killing of the one who has intercourse with a male like himself, and the killing of the one to whom it is done. He ordered the killing of the one who has intercourse with an animal, and the killing of the animal along with him. He resolved to burn the houses of those who stay away from congregational prayer. And there are other punishments that Allah established for crimes, which He, in His wisdom, made proportionate to the motives that lead to those crimes and to the strength of the restraint against them.

Whatever restraint against a act is natural (*tabi'i*), and there is no inclination in human nature toward it, is enforced only by prohibition together with discretionary punishment (*ta'zir*), and no prescribed punishment (*hadd*) is assigned to it, such as eating excrement, drinking blood, and eating carrion.

Whatever has an inclination in human nature toward it, He assigned a punishment proportionate to its corruption and to the strength of the natural inclination toward it.

For this reason, since the natural motive toward fornication (*zina*) is among the strongest motives, its greatest punishment is among the most grievous and most severe forms of killing, and its lesser punishment is the highest type of flogging, together with additional exile.

And since the crime of sodomy (*liwat*) combines both matters (i.e., it is both a strong motive and a grave corruption), its prescribed punishment is killing in every case. And since the motive for theft is strong and its corruption likewise, He ordered the cutting off of the hand for it.

Reflect on His wisdom in corrupting the limb with which the crime was committed. Just as He corrupted for the highway robber his hand and foot, which are the instruments of his crime, He did not corrupt for the slanderer his tongue with which he committed the offence, because the corruption (of cutting out the tongue) would exceed the corruption of the offence and would not reach it (in proportion). So He sufficed, in that case, with inflicting pain upon the whole body through flogging.

If it is said: Why did He not corrupt the fornicator's private part with which he committed the disobedience?

It is answered: For several reasons.

First: the corruption of that would exceed the corruption of the crime, since in it is the cutting off of progeny and exposing them to destruction.

Second: the private part is a concealed organ, and by cutting it the intended purpose of the *hadd*, namely deterrence and restraint for others like the offenders, is not achieved, unlike cutting off the hand.

Third: if he has his hand cut off, a second hand remains for him to compensate for it, unlike the private part.

Fourth: the pleasure of fornication pervades the whole body, so it is more fitting that the punishment pervade the whole body, and that is more appropriate than restricting it to a part of him.

Thus the punishments of the Lawgiver came in the most complete forms, the most agreeable to reason, and the most upright in terms of public benefit.

The point is that sins are followed by punishments, either legal (*shar'iyya*), or divine-decreed (*qadariyya*), or Allah gathers both for the servant. He may remove them from one who repents and does good.

If it is said: Do you say that Allah, glorified is He, is the one who made the two fornicators commit fornication, and who brought them together in the act and drove one of them to the other?

It is answered: The source of most people's trials comes from general, ambiguous terms that contain both truth and falsehood. One who wants their truth uses them, and one who wants their falsehood denies them, and then someone who wants their truth responds to him. This is a matter which, when a clever and perceptive person contemplates it, he sees wonders from it, and it saves him from the pitfalls into which most sects have fallen. The "making" (*ja'l*) attributed to Allah, glorified is He, may refer to the making that He loves and is pleased with, and the making that He decreed and determined. Allah says: ﴿Allah did not institute any *bahira*, *sa'iba*, *wasila*, or *ham* (pre-Islamic practices of animal consecration)﴾ [5:103]. This is a negation of His legislated, religious making: that is, He did not legislate that, nor command it, nor love it or approve of it. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire﴾ [28:41]. This is a universal, decreed making: that is, We decreed that and determined it.

Making the servant an imam who calls to the Fire is more emphatic than making him one who commits fornication, steals, and kills. Likewise, the making (of the servant to commit sin) is also an ambiguous term, which may mean that He compelled him, forced him, and constrained him to it. This is impossible with respect to the Lord, exalted is He, and His sacred perfection refuses it, and the attributes of His perfection prevent it, as has already been explained. It may also mean that He empowered him to do that and enabled him to do it, without compelling him to it, forcing him, or coercing him. This is the truth.

If it is said: All this is a deviation from the point. Whoever brings a sin into existence, originates it, and brings it from non-existence into existence?

It is answered: The doer of it is the one who originated it, created it, and brought it from non-existence into existence, by Allah's decree that enabled him to do that and empowered him to it, without forcing him and without his being compelled to commit it.

If it is said: Then who created it?

It is answered: Who, then, did it? If you say that the Lord, glorified is He, is the doer of immorality and disobedience, then reason, natural disposition, the revealed books of Allah, the consensus of His messengers, and the affirmation of His praise and the attributes of His perfection refute you. For His action, glorified is He, is all good, and He is exalted above doing evil in any way whatsoever. Evil is not attributed to Him, and good is what is attributed to Him. He does only good, wills only good. If He willed, He would have done otherwise, but He is exalted above doing what is not fitting, and above His will and volition in that, just as He is exalted above being described by it or named by it.

And if you say that the servant himself did it by means of the will and volition that Allah created in him?

It is answered: Then Allah, glorified is He, is the creator of all the actions of the servants in this sense. And if the determinist (*jabri*) followed this path with the libertarian (*qadari*), he would find rest with it and bring rest to him, and likewise the libertarian with him. But the two groups deviated from the even path, as the poet said:

*She traveled to the east, and I traveled to the west,*
*How vast is the distance between east and west!*

**[Section: The punishments for sins are legal and decreed]**

When the legal punishments are carried out, the decreed punishment is lifted and lightened. The Lord, exalted is He, does not nearly combine both punishments upon the servant unless one of them does not fulfil the removal of the requirement of the sin, and does not suffice for the eradication of its disease. When the legal punishments are suspended, they turn into decreed punishments, which may be more severe than legal punishments, and may be less severe than them, but they are general, whereas legal punishments are particular. For the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, does not legally punish anyone except one who committed the crime directly or was a cause of it.

As for decreed punishment, it occurs both generally and specifically. When a sin is concealed, it harms only its doer. When it is made public, it harms the particular and the general alike. When people see the wrong and leave off denouncing it, Allah is about to encompass them all with His punishment.

It has already been stated that the legal punishment was prescribed by Allah, glorified is He, according to the degree of the corruption of the sin and the demand of human nature for it. He made it of three types: killing, cutting, and flogging. He made killing correspond to disbelief and what is next to it and near to it, namely fornication and sodomy, for these corrupt religions, and those corrupt lineages and the human species.

Imam Ahmad said: "I know of no sin greater than fornication after killing." He cited the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the greatest sin?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that he will share your food." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then Allah revealed its confirmation: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery﴾ [25:68].

The Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned from each type its highest form, so that his answer would correspond to the questioner's question. For he asked him about the greatest sin, and he answered him with what included mention of the greatest of its types, and what is the greatest of each type.

So the greatest type of *shirk* is that the servant sets up a rival to Allah.

And the greatest type of killing is that one kills his child out of fear that he will share his food and drink.

And the greatest type of fornication is that one commits it with his neighbour's wife, for the corruption of fornication multiplies in proportion to the multiplication of the right that he violates.

So fornication with a woman who has a husband is greater in sin and punishment than with one who has no husband, since in it is the violation of the husband's sanctity, the corruption of his bed, the attaching of a lineage to him that was not his, and other kinds of harm to him. Therefore it is greater in sin and crime than fornication with one who has no husband.

Fornication with a hundred unmarried women is easier in Allah's sight than fornication with a neighbour's wife. If her husband is a neighbour to him, bad neighbourliness is added to that, and harm to his neighbour in the highest forms of harm, and that is among the greatest calamities.

It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "One whose neighbour is not safe from his calamities will not enter Paradise." (Agreed upon.) There is no calamity greater than fornication with a neighbour's wife.

If the neighbour is his brother or one of his close relatives, the severing of kinship is added to that, so the sin multiplies for him. If the neighbour is absent in obedience to Allah, such as in prayer, seeking knowledge, or jihad, the sin is multiplied for him, to the extent that the one who commits fornication with the wife of one fighting in the path of Allah will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: "Take from his good deeds whatever you wish."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What do you think?" That is, what do you think, that he leaves good deeds for him? It has been decided that he may take from them whatever he wishes, given the great need for even one good deed, since a father does not leave to his son, nor a friend to his friend, a right that is due upon him. If it happens that the woman is a close relative of his, the severing of her kinship is added to that. If the fornicator happens to be married, the sin is greater. If he is an old man, the sin is even greater, and he is one of the three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify, and for whom there is a painful punishment. If in addition to that it occurs in a sacred month, a sacred land, or a time held in honour by Allah, such as the times of prayer and times of answered supplication, the sin is multiplied.

On this basis, consider the corruptions of sins and the multiplication of their ranks in sin and punishment. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

**[Section: The decreed punishments]**

As for decreed punishments, they are of two kinds: one kind upon the hearts and souls, and one kind upon the bodies and wealth.

Those upon the hearts are of two kinds:

The first: existential pains with which the heart is struck.

The second: the cutting off of the sustenance by which its life and well-being are maintained.

When these are cut off from it, their opposites occur to it. The punishment of the hearts is the more severe of the two punishments, and it is the root of the punishment of the bodies.

This punishment grows stronger and increases until it spreads from the heart to the body, just as the pain of the body spreads to the heart. When the soul departs from the body, the judgment attaches to it, and the punishment of the heart then appears, and becomes manifest and apparent. This is called the punishment of the grave, and its relation to the *barzakh* (the intermediate realm) is like the relation of the punishment of bodies to this world.

**[Section: Decreed punishments upon the bodies]**

Those upon the bodies are also of two kinds:

One kind in this world, and one kind in the Hereafter.

Their severity and their duration are according to the corruptions of what they are assigned for, in intensity and in nature. There is no evil at all in this world and the Hereafter except sins and their punishments. So "evil" is a name for all of that, and its root is from the evil of the self and the evil deeds, and these are the two roots from which the Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge in his sermon when he said: "We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from the evil consequences of our deeds."

The evil deeds are among the evils of the soul, so all evil returns to the evil of the soul, for the evil deeds are among its branches and fruits.

There has been disagreement about the meaning of his words: "and from the evil consequences of our deeds." Is it that the meaning is: the evil of our deeds, in which case it is an instance of attributing a genus to its species? Or is the *min* (translated as "from") explanatory? It has also been said that the meaning is: from the punishments of our deeds that cause us harm, so that the reckoning would be: and from the punishments of our deeds which harm us. What favours this view is that the seeking of refuge then includes all evil. For the evils of the souls entail evil deeds, and these entail evil punishments. So he drew attention, by the evils of the souls, to what they require of ugly deeds, and was content with mentioning them. Or the evils of the soul are its root, then he mentioned the ultimate goal and end of evil, namely the evil consequences that harm the servant from his deed, of punishments and pains. Thus this seeking of refuge includes the root of evil, its branches, its ultimate goal, and its requirement.

And from the supplication of the angels for the believers is their saying: ﴿And protect them from the evil consequences; and whoever is protected from evil consequences on that Day, You have truly had mercy on him﴾ [40:9].

This includes the request for their protection from the evil deeds and their punishments that harm their doer. For whenever He, glorified is He, protects them from doing evil, He protects them from the recompense of evil. Although His saying: ﴿And whoever is protected from evil consequences on that Day, You have truly had mercy on him﴾ is more manifest regarding the punishments of deeds, from which protection is sought on that Day.

If it is said: they asked Him, glorified be He, to protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire, and this is the protection from evil punishments. This indicates that the "evil" (sayyi'ah) they asked to be protected from means evil deeds, so what the angels asked for is similar to what the Prophet (ﷺ) sought refuge from.

And this is not refuted by His saying "on that day," for what is sought is protection from the evils of deeds on that day, and those are evils in themselves.

It is said: protection from evil deeds is of two kinds.

The first: protection from committing them through divine enablement (tawfiq), so that they do not proceed from him.

The second: protection from their consequence through forgiveness, so that he is not punished for them. The verse thus includes asking for both matters, and the adverbial phrase qualifies the conditional clause, not the imperative clause.

Reflect on what this report about the angels contains of praise for them: faith, righteous deeds, and kindness toward the believers by seeking forgiveness for them. Before their seeking forgiveness, they made a means (tawassul) to Allah through His vast knowledge and His vast mercy. His vast knowledge includes His knowledge of their sins and their causes, their weakness in preserving themselves from sin, the dominion of their enemy, their souls, their desires and natures, and what the world and its adornment were made attractive to them; His knowledge of them when He created them from the earth, and when they were embryos in their mothers' wombs; His foreknowledge that they would certainly disobey Him, and that He loves pardon and forgiveness; and other aspects of His vast knowledge which no one besides Him encompasses.

His vast mercy includes that none of the believers who affirm His oneness (tawhid) and love Him will perish, for He is of vast mercy and excludes from the circle of His mercy none but the wretched. No one is more wretched than the one whom His mercy, which encompasses everything, does not embrace. Then they asked Him to forgive those who repent and follow His path (sabil), which is His straight way (sirat) leading to Him, which is knowledge of Him, love of Him, and obedience to Him. So they repented from what He dislikes and followed the way He loves. Then they asked Him to protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire, and to admit them, and the believers among their fathers, their offspring, and their spouses, into the Gardens of Eden which He promised them. He, glorified be He, does not break His promise; yet He promised them these through means, and among these means is the supplication of His angels for them that He admit them into it, by His mercy, which includes that He enabled them to do their deeds and set His angels to supplicate for them.

Then Allah, glorified be He, informed of His angels that they said after this supplication: ﴿Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [Ghafir: 8].

That is: the source, cause, and end of all this proceeds from the perfection of Your power and the perfection of Your knowledge. For might (al-'izzah) is the perfection of power, and wisdom (al-hikmah) is the perfection of knowledge. By these two attributes, glorified and exalted be He, He decrees what He wills, commands and forbids, rewards and punishes. These two attributes are thus the source of creation and command.

The point is that the punishments for evil deeds are of various kinds: legislative punishments (shar'iyyah), predestined punishments (qadariyyah), which are either in the heart, in the body, or in both; punishments in the intermediate realm (al-barzakh) after death; and punishments on the day the bodies are returned. Sin is never free from punishment at all, but because of the servant's ignorance he does not perceive the punishment within it, for he is like one who is intoxicated, drugged, or asleep, who does not feel pain.

The consequences of sins following upon sins is like the burning following upon fire, breaking following upon being broken, drowning following upon water, the corruption of the body following upon poisons, and diseases following upon their causes. Harm may coincide with the sin, or may follow it, either shortly or after a period, just as sickness may lag behind its cause. Often the servant errs in this matter: he commits a sin and does not see its effect immediately, nor does he realize that he is gradually working his own ruin little by little, just as poisons and harmful things act precisely step by step. If the servant does not rescue himself with remedies, purging, and regimen, he is heading toward destruction. This is so for a single sin he has not countered by what removes its effect; how much more so for sin upon sin, every day and every hour?

And Allah is the One sought for help.

The correct view is that this verse is *muhkam* (firm, in the sense of not abrogated) and remains in effect, not abrogated by anything. It contains both an informative statement (*khabar*) and a prohibition (*tahrim*). No one who claimed it was abrogated has produced any proof at all. What was unclear to many people about it is, praise be to God, clear. They were puzzled by His words: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾.

Is this an informative statement, a prohibition, or a permission? If it is an informative statement, we see many adulterers marrying chaste women. If it is a prohibition, it would mean that the adulterer is forbidden to marry anyone except an adulteress or a polytheist, which would be a prohibition on marrying chaste believing women and a permission to marry polytheists and adulteresses. Certainly God, glorified is He, did not intend that. When this puzzled them, they sought an interpretation of the verse that could be sustained.

Some of them said: the intended meaning of "marriage" (*nikah*) is sexual intercourse (*wat'*) and fornication, so it is as if He said: the adulterer only commits adultery with an adulteress or a polytheist.

This is corrupt, for it has no benefit, and the speech of God must be protected from being interpreted in such a way. It is known that the adulterer only commits adultery with an adulteress, so what is the benefit in informing of this?

When the majority saw the corruption of this interpretation, they turned away from it.

Then a group said: this is general in wording but specific in meaning. It refers to one man and one woman, namely 'Anaq, the prostitute, and her companion, who became Muslim and asked the Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, for permission to marry her, and then this verse was revealed.

This too is corrupt. Even though this specific case was the cause of revelation (*sabab al-nuzul*), the Qur'an is not restricted to the occasions of its revelation. If it were so, its use as evidence for other cases would be invalidated.

Another group said: rather, the verse is abrogated by His words: ﴿And marry off the unmarried among you﴾ (an-Nur 24:32).

This is the most corrupt of all, for there is no conflict between these two verses, and neither one contradicts the other. Rather, He, glorified is He, commanded the marrying off of the unmarried and forbade marriage to an adulteress, just as He forbade marrying a woman in her waiting period (*'iddah*), a woman in the state of ihram, and those within the forbidden degrees of kinship. Where, then, is the abrogating and the abrogated in this?

If it is said: then what is the meaning of the verse?

It is said: its meaning, and God knows best, is that the one who marries is commanded to marry a chaste, virtuous woman. Marriage to a woman was permitted only on this condition, as He mentioned in the chapters of an-Nisa' and al-Ma'idah. A conditional ruling ceases to apply when its condition is absent, and permission has been made conditional on the condition of *ihsan* (chastity). So when *ihsan* is absent, the permission conditional on it is also absent. The one who marries either commits to the law of God and His legislation, which He enacted through His Messenger, or does not commit to it. If he does not commit to it, he is a polytheist who will not accept marriage except with one who is a polytheist like himself. If he commits to it, but then opposes it and marries what is forbidden to him, the marriage is not valid, and he is therefore an adulterer. Thus the meaning of His words is manifest: ﴿does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾ (an-Nur 24:3), and this is made entirely clear. The same applies to the woman.

Just as this ruling is the implication and explicit meaning of the Qur'an, it is also the implication of the natural disposition (*fitrah*) and what reason requires. God, glorified is He, forbade His servant to be a *qarnan* (a cuckold) or *dayyuth* (one who tolerates immorality in his family), or the husband of a prostitute. God created people with a disposition that finds this ugly and abhorrent. This is why, when people wish to insult a man to the utmost, they say: "husband of a whore." So God forbade the Muslim to be like that.

Thus the wisdom of the prohibition becomes apparent and the meaning of the verse is clear. And God is the Granter of success.

Among what clarifies the prohibition, and shows that it is what befits this perfect law: this offence by the woman leads to the corruption of the husband's bed and the corruption of lineage, which God made among people for the completion of their interests, and counted among His blessings upon them. Fornication leads to the mixing of waters and confusion of lineages. So among the excellences of the law is the prohibition of marrying an adulteress until she repents and is cleansed (*istibra'*).

Also, the adulteress is wicked (*khabithah*), as has been explained earlier. God, glorified is He, made marriage a cause of affection, mercy, love and pure devotion. How then can a wicked woman be loved by a good man as his wife? The word *zawj* (spouse) is named from *izdiwaj* (pairing), which means resemblance: the two spouses are alike. Repulsion is established between the good and the wicked, both by law and by decree, so pairing, mercy and affection cannot be realised with it. How excellently does the one who adopted this view act, and how well he prevented a man from being the husband of a whore.

How far is this from the view of one who permits him to marry her and have intercourse with her tonight, though an adulterer had intercourse with her yesterday, and who says: "The semen of an adulterer has no sanctity." Grant that this is so, yet the semen of the husband has sanctity. How then can it be permissible for it to mingle with the semen of an adulterer in one womb?

The point is that God, glorified is He, called adulterers and adulteresses wicked (*khabithin* and *khabithat*). The category of this act is one for which purification is prescribed, even though intercourse within marriage is lawful. He called the one who performs it *junub* (in a state of major ritual impurity), because he is distanced from reciting the Qur'an, from prayer and from the mosques, and he is forbidden all of this until he purifies himself with water.

Likewise, when it is forbidden, it distances the heart from God, glorified is He, and from the Last Abode. Rather, it comes between him and faith, until he attains a complete purification through repentance and purifies his body with water.

[Section: The Prohibition of Marrying an Adulteress]

As for marrying an adulteress, God, glorified and exalted is He, has explicitly prohibited it in the chapter of an-Nur. He informed that whoever marries her is either an adulterer or a polytheist. For he either commits to His ruling, believes it to be obligatory upon him, or does not. If he does not commit to it and does not believe in it, he is a polytheist. If he commits to it and believes it to be obligatory, but opposes it, he is an adulterer. Then He explicitly stated its prohibition, saying: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾ (an-Nur 24:3).

It is not hidden that the claim that the verse was abrogated by His words: ﴿And marry off the unmarried among you﴾ (an-Nur 24:32) is among the weakest things that can be said. Even weaker than it is interpreting "marriage" as "fornication," for then the meaning of the verse becomes: "The adulterer does not commit adultery except with an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not committed with except by an adulterer or a polytheist." The speech of God must be protected from such a thing.

Likewise, interpreting the verse as referring to a polytheist prostitute is extremely remote from its wording and context. How could that be, when He, glorified is He, only permitted marriage to free women and slave women on the condition of *ihsan*, which is chastity, saying: ﴿So marry them with the permission of their guardians, and give them their bridal gifts according to what is reasonable, as chaste women, not fornicators nor those who take secret lovers﴾ (an-Nisa' 4:25). He permitted marrying her only in this state and not otherwise. This is not a matter of the implication of a statement (*dalalat al-mafhum*), for the private parts are originally under prohibition, so permission for them is limited to what the law has stated. Anything beyond that remains under the original prohibition.

Also, He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men are for wicked women﴾ (an-Nur 24:26).

The wicked women (*khabithat*) are prostitutes. This implies that whoever marries them is wicked like them.

Also, among the most abhorrent of abominations is that a man should be the husband of a prostitute. The ugliness of this is fixed in the natural dispositions of creation, and among them it is considered the greatest of insults.

Also: the prostitute cannot be trusted not to corrupt the man's bed and attribute to him children from another. The prohibition is established even without this.

Also: the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, separated a man from a woman whom he found to be pregnant from fornication.

Also, Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi asked the Prophet, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, for permission to marry 'Anaq, and she was a prostitute. The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, recited to him the verse of an-Nur and said: "Do not marry her."

[Section: The wisdom of prescribing the hadd (prescribed penalty) for qadhf (false accusation) of unlawful sexual intercourse rather than of disbelief]

As for prescribing the hadd for slander (*firyah*) against one who accuses another of unlawful sexual intercourse (*zina*), rather than of disbelief (*kufr*), it is entirely fitting. The one who accuses another of *zina* has no way for people to know that he is lying. So the hadd for slander was made a means of refuting him, of clearing the honour of the one accused, and of magnifying the gravity of this grave sin, for whoever slanders a Muslim with it is flogged. As for one who accuses another of disbelief, the observed condition of the Muslim and the knowledge of the Muslims about it is sufficient to refute him. The shame that befalls him for lying about the Muslim in that matter does not match the shame that befalls him for lying about him in the accusation of an immoral act, especially if the one accused is a woman. The disgrace and blame that falls upon her among her family, the scattering of people's suspicions, and their division between one who believes and one who denies, does not befall a similar person through an accusation of disbelief.

[Section: The wisdom of requiring two witnesses for homicide but four for zina]

As for his requiring two witnesses for homicide but not for *zina*, it is in complete wisdom and benefit. The Lawgiver was cautious regarding retaliation (*qisas*) and blood, and he was also cautious regarding the hadd for *zina*. If he had accepted only four witnesses for homicide, blood would have been lost, the transgressors would have pounced, and they would have become bold in killing. As for *zina*, he went to great lengths to conceal it, just as Allah decreed its concealment. Thus the legislation of Allah and His decree combined to conceal it. So he accepted only four witnesses for it, who describe the act as direct observation, in which all possibility of doubt is eliminated. Likewise in confession: he did not suffice with less than four times, out of eagerness to conceal what Allah decreed to be concealed, and he disliked its disclosure and speaking of it. He threatened with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter whoever loves to spread it among the believers.

[Section: The wisdom of flogging the slanderer of a free person but not of a slave]

As for flogging the slanderer of a free person but not of a slave, it is a differentiation in His legislation between what Allah differentiated between by His decree. Allah, glorified is He, did not make the slave like the free person in every respect, neither by decree nor by law. Allah, glorified is He, has struck for His servants parables in which He informed of the disparity between the free and the slave, and that they themselves would not be content for their slaves to be equal to them in their provisions. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, preferred some of His creation over others, and preferred the free over the slaves in ownership, its causes, and the capacity to dispose of property. He made the slave one owned and the free one an owner, and the owner and the owned are not equal.

As for making them equal in the rulings of reward and punishment, that would necessitate justice and goodness. On the Day of Recompense there will be no slave and free, nor owner and owned.

(Benefit)
For *zina* four witnesses were required, and for *ihsan* (the condition of chastity and marriage) two were required, because *zina* is a cause and an effective reason (*'illah*), while *ihsan* is a condition (*shart*). The statement of conditions falls short of causes and reasons, because conditions validate but do not necessitate. For this reason, confession once is not sufficient according to us, and according to the Hanafis.

[Section: The flogging and its requirement]

As for flogging, He made it the punishment for offences against honour, against the intellect, and against sexual chastity. These offences do not reach the level that requires execution or the loss of a limb, except the offence against chastity, whose corruption has indeed become a cause for the most heinous killings. However, in the case of a virgin, what opposes it is the strength of the motive and the absence of a substitute, and this opposing factor became a cause for dropping the death penalty. Flogging alone was not sufficient for deterrence, so it was made more severe with exile and banishment, so that he would taste the pain of estrangement, separation from his homeland, and removal from family and close companions, which would deter him from repetition. As for offences against the intellect through intoxication, their corruption generally did not extend beyond the intoxicated person. For this reason intoxication was not forbidden at the beginning of Islam, whereas fornication, injustice, and transgression were forbidden in every religion and on the tongue of every prophet. The punishment for this offence was not specified by the Lawgiver. Rather, people were struck with hands, sandals, the ends of garments, and palm stalks, and forty lashes were struck for it. When people made light of its matter and kept committing it, the rightly-guided Caliph 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, whose Sunnah we were commanded to follow, and whose Sunnah is from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), made it more severe. He made it eighty lashes with the whip, exiled, and shaved the head. All of this is from the jurisprudence of the Sunnah. The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered the execution of the drinker in the fourth offence, and this was not abrogated, nor did he make it an unavoidable hadd. So it is a punishment that depends on the ruler's discretion regarding what is beneficial. Thus adding forty lashes, exile, and shaving the head is easier than execution.

[Section: Ta'zir (discretionary punishment) and its places]

As for ta'zir, it applies to every disobedience for which there is no hadd and no expiation (*kaffarah*). Acts of disobedience are of three kinds: a kind in which there is a hadd and no expiation; a kind in which there is expiation and no hadd; and a kind in which there is neither hadd nor expiation.

The first is like theft, drinking, *zina*, and slander.
The second is like sexual intercourse during the day in Ramadan and sexual intercourse while in ihram.
The third is like sexual intercourse with a jointly owned slave-girl, kissing a non-related woman, being alone with her, entering the bath without a loincloth, eating carrion, blood, pork, and the like.

As for the first kind, the hadd in it suffices and makes ta'zir unnecessary.

As for the second kind: is ta'zir required along with the expiation in it or not? There are two opinions on this, and both are in the school of Ahmad.

As for the third kind: ta'zir is required in it by unanimous agreement. But is it like the hadd, so that the ruler may not leave it, or is it left to the ruler's discretion in its implementation and its omission, just as it is left to his discretion regarding its extent? There are two opinions among the scholars. The second is the opinion of al-Shafi'i, and the first is the opinion of the majority.

Whatever disobedience is forbidden in its very nature, like injustice and immoral acts, the Lawgiver did not prescribe an expiation for it. For this reason there is no expiation for *zina*, drinking wine, slandering chaste women, or theft. The consistent application of this is that there is no expiation for intentional killing or for the deliberate false oath (*yamin al-ghamus*), as Ahmad, Abu Hanifah, and those who agree with them say. This is not a lightening of the burden on the one who commits them. Rather, expiation does not operate in this category of disobedience. It only operates in things that were permissible originally and were forbidden due to an external factor, like intercourse during fasting and ihram. The consistent application of this, which is the correct view, is that expiation is obligatory for intercourse during menstruation. This is what analogy necessitates even if the Sharia had not come with it. How much more so since it has come with it, both as a statement attributed to the Prophet and as one attributed to companions?

The reverse of this is anal intercourse, in which there is no expiation. Analogizing it to intercourse during menstruation is not valid, because this category was never permissible, and expiation does not operate in it. If expiation were obligatory in it, it would be obligatory in *zina* and sodomy by a stronger argument. This is the rule of the Lawgiver regarding expiations, and it is in complete accord with wisdom and benefit.

[Section: The testimony of one who has been flogged in a hadd for slander]

The statement of the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah be pleased with him, in his letter: "or one who has been flogged for a hadd," refers to the slanderer. If he is punished with the hadd for slander, his testimony is not accepted after that. This is agreed upon among the community before repentance, and the Qur'an is explicit about it. As for when he repents, there are two well-known opinions among the scholars:

The first: it is not accepted. This is the view of Abu Hanifah, his companions, and the people of Iraq.
The second: it is accepted. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Malik.

Ibn Jurayj said, from 'Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The testimony of a defiantly disobedient person is not permissible even if he repents." The judge Isma'il said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Qays narrated to us, from Salim, from Qays ibn 'Asim, who said: "Abu Bakrah, whenever a man came to him asking him to witness, would say: 'Call on someone other than me, for the Muslims have declared me defiantly disobedient.'" This is established from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Masruq, and al-Sha'bi, in one of the two narrations from them, and it is the view of Shurayh.

The proponents of this view argue that Allah, glorified is He, made the prohibition of accepting their testimony perpetual by His saying: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever﴾, and He judged them to be defiantly disobedient. Then He made an exception for those who repent from among the defiantly disobedient, and the prohibition on accepting testimony remained absolute and perpetual.

They also said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from Adam ibn Faid, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The testimony of a treacherous man or a treacherous woman is not permissible, nor that of one who has been subjected to a hadd in Islam, nor that of one who bears a grudge against his brother." There are chains to 'Amr.

Ibn Majah narrated it through the route of Hajjaj ibn Artah, from 'Amr, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it through the route of al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from 'Amr. They said: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Dimashqi narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The testimony of a treacherous man or treacherous woman is not permissible, nor that of one who has been flogged for a hadd, nor one who bears a grudge against his brother, nor one who is known for false testimony, nor one suspected in matters of clientage or kinship."

It was also narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (a report lacking a companion in its chain).

They said: The prohibition on accepting his testimony was made part of his punishment. For this reason, the prohibition is only applied after the hadd. If he slandered and was not flogged, his testimony would not be rejected. It is well known that the hadd only increases him in purity and lightens his sin of slander, or removes it. So after the hadd he is better than he was before. Nevertheless, his testimony is only rejected after the hadd, so rejecting it is part of his punishment. The hadd and its consequences do not fall away by repentance. For this reason, if the slanderer repents, his repentance does not prevent the hadd from being carried out upon him. Likewise his testimony.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "His repentance is accepted between him and Allah regarding the great punishment, but his testimony is not accepted." Shurayh said: "His testimony is never permissible, and his repentance is between him and his Lord."

The essence of the issue is that the rejection of his testimony was made a punishment for this sin, so it does not fall away by repentance, like the hadd.

The others said, and the wording is from al-Shafi'i: "The exception in the context of speech refers to the beginning and the end of the speech, in all that the people of jurisprudence hold, unless a report distinguishes between them." Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, saying: "I heard al-Zuhri saying: 'The people of Iraq claim that the testimony of one who has been subjected to a hadd is not permissible. And I testify that so-and-so informed me that 'Umar said to Abu Bakrah: "Repent, and I will accept your testimony."'" Sufyan said: "I forgot the name of the one who narrated to al-Zuhri. When we stood up, I asked those present, and 'Amr ibn Qays said to me: 'It is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.' So I said to Sufyan: 'Did you doubt what he told you?' He said: 'No, it is Sa'id, without any doubt.'" Al-Shafi'i said: "I often heard him narrating and naming Sa'id, and often heard him saying: 'From Sa'id, if Allah wills.' And someone I trust from the people of Madinah informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that when 'Umar flogged the three, he asked them to repent. Two of them returned, so he accepted their testimony, but Abu Bakrah refused to return, so he rejected his testimony." And Sulayman ibn Kathir narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Umar said to Abu Bakrah, Shibl, and Nafi': "Whoever of you repents, I will accept his testimony."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Umar said to those who testified against al-Mughirah: "Repent, and your testimony will be accepted." Two of them repented, and Abu Bakrah refused to repent, so 'Umar would not accept his testimony.

They said: "The exception returns to everything mentioned before it, except the hadd, for the Muslims are unanimous that the slanderer is not relieved of the hadd by repentance. And the leading scholars of the language have said that the exception returns to everything that precedes it entirely." Ibn 'Ubayd said in the Book of Judgment: "The community of the Hijaz and Mecca agree on accepting his testimony. As for the people of Iraq, they hold the first view, that it is never accepted. Both groups, as far as we see, interpreted the Qur'an accordingly." Those who do not accept it hold that the meaning is cut off at His saying: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever﴾, and then He began a new statement: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾.

So they made the exception apply only to defiant disobedience, not to testimony.

As for the others, they interpreted that the speech follows one part after another in a single sequence: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾.

The exception has come to govern everything that preceded it. Abu 'Ubayd said: "In my view this is the operative opinion, because more scholars hold it and it is sounder in reasoning. A position cannot be more widely held than the practice (of the Companions), and the Muslims do not disagree that the testimony of a flogged fornicator is accepted once he repents."

They (the proponents of acceptance) said: "As for what you have cited from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Shafi'i said: 'It has reached me from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to permit the testimony of the slanderer once he repents.'"

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from him (Ibn 'Abbas) regarding the words of the Most High, ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever﴾, then (the words), ﴿except those who repent﴾. So whoever repents and reforms, his testimony is accepted according to the Book of Allah.

Sharik related from Abu Husayn from al-Sha'bi: "Allah accepts his repentance, yet they do not accept his testimony?"

Mutarrif related from him: "When he has finished being flogged, and he retracts his accusation and recants his statement, his testimony is accepted."

They said: "As for those narrations you have related, they are weak. Adam ibn Fa'id is not well known, and his transmitters from 'Umar are of two kinds: trustworthy and weak. The trustworthy ones did not mention from them anyone's words, 'or flogged for a prescribed punishment (hadd)'. Only the weak ones mentioned it, such as al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, Adam and al-Hajjaj. The hadith of 'A'isha contains Yazid, who is weak. Even if the narrations were sound, they would be interpreted as referring to the one who has not repented, for the one who repents from a sin is like the one who has no sin. The testimony of 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas was accepted after repentance, and no opponent among the Companions is known for either of them."

They said: "The greatest impediments to testimony are disbelief, sorcery, killing a soul, disobedience to one's parents and fornication. If he repents from these things, his testimony is accepted by consensus. So the one who repents from slander (qadhf, false accusation of unchastity) is more deserving of acceptance. They said: 'Where is the crime of killing in comparison with his slander?' They said: 'The hadd (prescribed punishment) also removes from him the punishment of the Hereafter, and it is a purification for him, for the hudud are a purification for those upon whom they are imposed. How, then, is his testimony rejected when he has not been purified by the hadd, and yet he is to be rejected at his purest? For by the hadd and repentance he may attain complete purity.'"

They said: "The rejection of testimony due to slander is only based on the cause that Allah mentioned immediately after this ruling, namely fisq (grave moral transgression). Fisq has been removed by repentance, and it was the cause of the rejection, so the effect that followed from it, namely the prohibition, must be removed. They said: 'The slanderer is a fasiq (transgressor) by his slander, whether or not he was given the hadd. How, then, is his testimony accepted while he is in the state of fisq, and rejected after the fisq has ceased?' They said: 'We have no precedent in the Shari'ah of a single sin, from which one repents, while its consequential effect, the rejection of testimony, remains. Is this not contrary to what is known from it, and contrary to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The one who repents from sin is like the one who has no sin"?'"

At this point it is said: "His repentance from slander places him in the position of one who did not slander, so it is obligatory to accept his testimony," or as they stated.

Those who oppose (acceptance) said: "Slander includes an offence against the right of Allah and the right of a human being, and it is among the gravest of crimes. Therefore, it is fitting that the deterrent be severe, and the rejection of testimony is one of the most powerful means of deterrence, because of the pain it inflicts on the heart and the injury it causes to the self. For it is the removal of the authority of his tongue, with which he attacked the honour of his brother, and the nullification of that authority. Moreover, it is a punishment in the place of the offence, for the offence was committed by his tongue, so it is more fitting that the punishment be on it. We have seen that the Lawgiver took this into account when he cut off the hand of the thief, for it is a prescribed punishment in the place of the offence. This is not refuted by the fact that he did not make the punishment of the fornicator the cutting off of the organ with which he committed the offence, for several reasons:

"The first: it is a hidden organ, concealed and not visible to the eyes, so the intended lesson of the hadd is not achieved by cutting it off.

"The second: that would lead to the destruction of the organs of reproduction and the cessation of the human species.

"The third: the pleasure of the whole body in fornication is like the pleasure of that particular organ. Thus, what the whole body obtained of forbidden pleasure is like what the private parts obtained. For this reason, the hadd for wine-drinking is applied to the whole body.

"The fourth: cutting off this organ leads to death, and the offence of one who is not married (muhsan) does not warrant death, while the offence of the married person warrants the most grievous forms of killing, and cutting off some of his limbs is not proportionate to it. Thus the two are distinct."

They said: "As for the acceptance of his testimony before the hadd and its rejection after it, this is because it has been established that the rejection of testimony is made part of the hadd and its completion. So it is like an attribute and a complement of the hadd, and therefore it does not precede it. Moreover, the imposition of the hadd upon him diminishes him in the eyes of people and reduces his dignity, whereas before the hadd is imposed, his dignity remains intact and he has not violated it."

They said: "As for the one who repents from fornication, disbelief and killing, we accept his testimony because its rejection was a consequence of fisq, and that has ceased. This differs from our case, for we have shown that its rejection is part of the hadd, so the two are distinct."

Those who accept (his testimony) said: "The severity of deterrence has no defined measure. The purpose of deterrence has already been achieved through the hadd. Likewise, for all other crimes the Lawgiver made the achievement of deterrence through the hadd. Otherwise, his wives would not be divorced, his property would not be taken, he would not be removed from his post, and his narration (of hadith) would not be discarded, for that would be more severe in deterrence. Yet the Muslims have unanimously agreed to accept the narration of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The severity of deterrence is among the widespread attributes that cannot be pinned down. Moreover, the pain of the heart and body and the injury to the self have been achieved through the beating that was inflicted upon his back. Furthermore, the rejection of testimony does not deter most slanderers. Rather, it affects and deters only the notable people, and it is rare for slander to be found among them. It is found mostly among the rabble, the base, and those who do not care whether their testimony is rejected or accepted. Also, how many a slanderer has lived out his life without ever giving testimony before a judge? The purpose of deterrence is to restrain souls from what they need and what they frequently commit. Moreover, this consideration you have mentioned is opposed by something stronger: the rejection of testimony forever entails the mischief of losing the rights of others and the nullification of testimony in a place where it is needed. Such harm does not follow from acceptance, for there is no harm in it for others when the one who is a trustworthy (ʿadl) penitent has reformed what lies between himself and Allah. There is no doubt that taking into account a benefit that entails a harm is less preferable than taking into account a benefit that entails several harms for the witness, the one in whose favour the testimony is given, and the one against whom it is given. The Lawgiver aspires to preserving rights for their rightful owners by every means and to avoiding their loss. How, then, would he nullify a right to which a just, approved person, whose testimony is acceptable, has testified concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his religion, in narration and in legal opinion?"

As for your statement, "The punishment is in the place of the offence," this does not necessarily follow, because of the punishment of the drinker and the fornicator mentioned earlier. Allah, glory be to Him, made the punishment for this offence fall upon the whole body rather than the tongue. He made the punishment of the tongue dependent upon fisq, which is the locus of suspicion. So when fisq is removed by repentance, there is no basis for punishment after it.

As for your statement, "The rejection of testimony is part of the completion of the hadd," this is not so, for the hadd is completed by carrying out its number (of lashes), and its cause is the slander itself. As for the rejection of testimony, it is a separate ruling required by the fisq resulting from the slander, not by the hadd. Thus slander necessitated two rulings: the establishment of fisq and the imposition of the hadd, and these two are distinct.

[Section: The wisdom of prescribing the hadd (prescribed penalty) for qadhf (false accusation) of unlawful sexual intercourse rather than of disbelief]

As for prescribing the hadd for slander (*firyah*) against one who accuses another of unlawful sexual intercourse (*zina*), rather than of disbelief (*kufr*), it is entirely fitting. The one who accuses another of *zina* has no way for people to know that he is lying. So the hadd for slander was made a means of refuting him, of clearing the honour of the one accused, and of magnifying the gravity of this grave sin, for whoever slanders a Muslim with it is flogged. As for one who accuses another of disbelief, the observed condition of the Muslim and the knowledge of the Muslims about it is sufficient to refute him. The shame that befalls him for lying about the Muslim in that matter does not match the shame that befalls him for lying about him in the accusation of an immoral act, especially if the one accused is a woman. The disgrace and blame that falls upon her among her family, the scattering of people's suspicions, and their division between one who believes and one who denies, does not befall a similar person through an accusation of disbelief.

[Section: The wisdom of requiring two witnesses for homicide but four for zina]

As for his requiring two witnesses for homicide but not for *zina*, it is in complete wisdom and benefit. The Lawgiver was cautious regarding retaliation (*qisas*) and blood, and he was also cautious regarding the hadd for *zina*. If he had accepted only four witnesses for homicide, blood would have been lost, the transgressors would have pounced, and they would have become bold in killing. As for *zina*, he went to great lengths to conceal it, just as Allah decreed its concealment. Thus the legislation of Allah and His decree combined to conceal it. So he accepted only four witnesses for it, who describe the act as direct observation, in which all possibility of doubt is eliminated. Likewise in confession: he did not suffice with less than four times, out of eagerness to conceal what Allah decreed to be concealed, and he disliked its disclosure and speaking of it. He threatened with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter whoever loves to spread it among the believers.

[Section: The wisdom of flogging the slanderer of a free person but not of a slave]

As for flogging the slanderer of a free person but not of a slave, it is a differentiation in His legislation between what Allah differentiated between by His decree. Allah, glorified is He, did not make the slave like the free person in every respect, neither by decree nor by law. Allah, glorified is He, has struck for His servants parables in which He informed of the disparity between the free and the slave, and that they themselves would not be content for their slaves to be equal to them in their provisions. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, preferred some of His creation over others, and preferred the free over the slaves in ownership, its causes, and the capacity to dispose of property. He made the slave one owned and the free one an owner, and the owner and the owned are not equal.

As for making them equal in the rulings of reward and punishment, that would necessitate justice and goodness. On the Day of Recompense there will be no slave and free, nor owner and owned.

(Benefit)
For *zina* four witnesses were required, and for *ihsan* (the condition of chastity and marriage) two were required, because *zina* is a cause and an effective reason (*'illah*), while *ihsan* is a condition (*shart*). The statement of conditions falls short of causes and reasons, because conditions validate but do not necessitate. For this reason, confession once is not sufficient according to us, and according to the Hanafis.

[Section: The flogging and its requirement]

As for flogging, He made it the punishment for offences against honour, against the intellect, and against sexual chastity. These offences do not reach the level that requires execution or the loss of a limb, except the offence against chastity, whose corruption has indeed become a cause for the most heinous killings. However, in the case of a virgin, what opposes it is the strength of the motive and the absence of a substitute, and this opposing factor became a cause for dropping the death penalty. Flogging alone was not sufficient for deterrence, so it was made more severe with exile and banishment, so that he would taste the pain of estrangement, separation from his homeland, and removal from family and close companions, which would deter him from repetition. As for offences against the intellect through intoxication, their corruption generally did not extend beyond the intoxicated person. For this reason intoxication was not forbidden at the beginning of Islam, whereas fornication, injustice, and transgression were forbidden in every religion and on the tongue of every prophet. The punishment for this offence was not specified by the Lawgiver. Rather, people were struck with hands, sandals, the ends of garments, and palm stalks, and forty lashes were struck for it. When people made light of its matter and kept committing it, the rightly-guided Caliph 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, whose Sunnah we were commanded to follow, and whose Sunnah is from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), made it more severe. He made it eighty lashes with the whip, exiled, and shaved the head. All of this is from the jurisprudence of the Sunnah. The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered the execution of the drinker in the fourth offence, and this was not abrogated, nor did he make it an unavoidable hadd. So it is a punishment that depends on the ruler's discretion regarding what is beneficial. Thus adding forty lashes, exile, and shaving the head is easier than execution.

[Section: Ta'zir (discretionary punishment) and its places]

As for ta'zir, it applies to every disobedience for which there is no hadd and no expiation (*kaffarah*). Acts of disobedience are of three kinds: a kind in which there is a hadd and no expiation; a kind in which there is expiation and no hadd; and a kind in which there is neither hadd nor expiation.

The first is like theft, drinking, *zina*, and slander.
The second is like sexual intercourse during the day in Ramadan and sexual intercourse while in ihram.
The third is like sexual intercourse with a jointly owned slave-girl, kissing a non-related woman, being alone with her, entering the bath without a loincloth, eating carrion, blood, pork, and the like.

As for the first kind, the hadd in it suffices and makes ta'zir unnecessary.

As for the second kind: is ta'zir required along with the expiation in it or not? There are two opinions on this, and both are in the school of Ahmad.

As for the third kind: ta'zir is required in it by unanimous agreement. But is it like the hadd, so that the ruler may not leave it, or is it left to the ruler's discretion in its implementation and its omission, just as it is left to his discretion regarding its extent? There are two opinions among the scholars. The second is the opinion of al-Shafi'i, and the first is the opinion of the majority.

Whatever disobedience is forbidden in its very nature, like injustice and immoral acts, the Lawgiver did not prescribe an expiation for it. For this reason there is no expiation for *zina*, drinking wine, slandering chaste women, or theft. The consistent application of this is that there is no expiation for intentional killing or for the deliberate false oath (*yamin al-ghamus*), as Ahmad, Abu Hanifah, and those who agree with them say. This is not a lightening of the burden on the one who commits them. Rather, expiation does not operate in this category of disobedience. It only operates in things that were permissible originally and were forbidden due to an external factor, like intercourse during fasting and ihram. The consistent application of this, which is the correct view, is that expiation is obligatory for intercourse during menstruation. This is what analogy necessitates even if the Sharia had not come with it. How much more so since it has come with it, both as a statement attributed to the Prophet and as one attributed to companions?

The reverse of this is anal intercourse, in which there is no expiation. Analogizing it to intercourse during menstruation is not valid, because this category was never permissible, and expiation does not operate in it. If expiation were obligatory in it, it would be obligatory in *zina* and sodomy by a stronger argument. This is the rule of the Lawgiver regarding expiations, and it is in complete accord with wisdom and benefit.

[Section: The testimony of one who has been flogged in a hadd for slander]

The statement of the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah be pleased with him, in his letter: "or one who has been flogged for a hadd," refers to the slanderer. If he is punished with the hadd for slander, his testimony is not accepted after that. This is agreed upon among the community before repentance, and the Qur'an is explicit about it. As for when he repents, there are two well-known opinions among the scholars:

The first: it is not accepted. This is the view of Abu Hanifah, his companions, and the people of Iraq.
The second: it is accepted. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Malik.

Ibn Jurayj said, from 'Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The testimony of a defiantly disobedient person is not permissible even if he repents."
