The judge Isma'il said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Qays narrated to us, from Salim, from Qays ibn 'Asim, who said: "Abu Bakrah, whenever a man came to him asking him to witness, would say: 'Call on someone other than me, for the Muslims have declared me defiantly disobedient.'" This is established from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Masruq, and al-Sha'bi, in one of the two narrations from them, and it is the view of Shurayh.

The proponents of this view argue that Allah, glorified is He, made the prohibition of accepting their testimony perpetual by His saying: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever﴾, and He judged them to be defiantly disobedient. Then He made an exception for those who repent from among the defiantly disobedient, and the prohibition on accepting testimony remained absolute and perpetual.

They also said: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from Adam ibn Faid, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The testimony of a treacherous man or a treacherous woman is not permissible, nor that of one who has been subjected to a hadd in Islam, nor that of one who bears a grudge against his brother." There are chains to 'Amr.

Ibn Majah narrated it through the route of Hajjaj ibn Artah, from 'Amr, and al-Bayhaqi narrated it through the route of al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from 'Amr. They said: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Dimashqi narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The testimony of a treacherous man or treacherous woman is not permissible, nor that of one who has been flogged for a hadd, nor one who bears a grudge against his brother, nor one who is known for false testimony, nor one suspected in matters of clientage or kinship."

It was also narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (a report lacking a companion in its chain).

They said: The prohibition on accepting his testimony was made part of his punishment. For this reason, the prohibition is only applied after the hadd. If he slandered and was not flogged, his testimony would not be rejected. It is well known that the hadd only increases him in purity and lightens his sin of slander, or removes it. So after the hadd he is better than he was before. Nevertheless, his testimony is only rejected after the hadd, so rejecting it is part of his punishment. The hadd and its consequences do not fall away by repentance. For this reason, if the slanderer repents, his repentance does not prevent the hadd from being carried out upon him. Likewise his testimony.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "His repentance is accepted between him and Allah regarding the great punishment, but his testimony is not accepted." Shurayh said: "His testimony is never permissible, and his repentance is between him and his Lord."

The essence of the issue is that the rejection of his testimony was made a punishment for this sin, so it does not fall away by repentance, like the hadd.

The others said, and the wording is from al-Shafi'i: "The exception in the context of speech refers to the beginning and the end of the speech, in all that the people of jurisprudence hold, unless a report distinguishes between them." Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, saying: "I heard al-Zuhri saying: 'The people of Iraq claim that the testimony of one who has been subjected to a hadd is not permissible. And I testify that so-and-so informed me that 'Umar said to Abu Bakrah: "Repent, and I will accept your testimony."'" Sufyan said: "I forgot the name of the one who narrated to al-Zuhri. When we stood up, I asked those present, and 'Amr ibn Qays said to me: 'It is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.' So I said to Sufyan: 'Did you doubt what he told you?' He said: 'No, it is Sa'id, without any doubt.'" Al-Shafi'i said: "I often heard him narrating and naming Sa'id, and often heard him saying: 'From Sa'id, if Allah wills.' And someone I trust from the people of Madinah informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that when 'Umar flogged the three, he asked them to repent. Two of them returned, so he accepted their testimony, but Abu Bakrah refused to return, so he rejected his testimony." And Sulayman ibn Kathir narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Umar said to Abu Bakrah, Shibl, and Nafi': "Whoever of you repents, I will accept his testimony."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Umar said to those who testified against al-Mughirah: "Repent, and your testimony will be accepted." Two of them repented, and Abu Bakrah refused to repent, so 'Umar would not accept his testimony.

They said: "The exception returns to everything mentioned before it, except the hadd, for the Muslims are unanimous that the slanderer is not relieved of the hadd by repentance. And the leading scholars of the language have said that the exception returns to everything that precedes it entirely." Ibn 'Ubayd said in the Book of Judgment: "The community of the Hijaz and Mecca agree on accepting his testimony. As for the people of Iraq, they hold the first view, that it is never accepted. Both groups, as far as we see, interpreted the Qur'an accordingly." Those who do not accept it hold that the meaning is cut off at His saying: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever﴾, and then He began a new statement: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾.

So they made the exception apply only to defiant disobedience, not to testimony.

As for the others, they interpreted that the speech follows one part after another in a single sequence: ﴿and never accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ ﴿except those who repent﴾.

The exception has come to govern everything that preceded it. Abu 'Ubayd said: "In my view this is the operative opinion, because more scholars hold it and it is sounder in reasoning. A position cannot be more widely held than the practice (of the Companions), and the Muslims do not disagree that the testimony of a flogged fornicator is accepted once he repents."

They (the proponents of acceptance) said: "As for what you have cited from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Shafi'i said: 'It has reached me from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to permit the testimony of the slanderer once he repents.'"

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from him (Ibn 'Abbas) regarding the words of the Most High, ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever﴾, then (the words), ﴿except those who repent﴾. So whoever repents and reforms, his testimony is accepted according to the Book of Allah.

Sharik related from Abu Husayn from al-Sha'bi: "Allah accepts his repentance, yet they do not accept his testimony?"

Mutarrif related from him: "When he has finished being flogged, and he retracts his accusation and recants his statement, his testimony is accepted."

They said: "As for those narrations you have related, they are weak. Adam ibn Fa'id is not well known, and his transmitters from 'Umar are of two kinds: trustworthy and weak. The trustworthy ones did not mention from them anyone's words, 'or flogged for a prescribed punishment (hadd)'. Only the weak ones mentioned it, such as al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, Adam and al-Hajjaj. The hadith of 'A'isha contains Yazid, who is weak. Even if the narrations were sound, they would be interpreted as referring to the one who has not repented, for the one who repents from a sin is like the one who has no sin. The testimony of 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas was accepted after repentance, and no opponent among the Companions is known for either of them."

They said: "The greatest impediments to testimony are disbelief, sorcery, killing a soul, disobedience to one's parents and fornication. If he repents from these things, his testimony is accepted by consensus. So the one who repents from slander (qadhf, false accusation of unchastity) is more deserving of acceptance. They said: 'Where is the crime of killing in comparison with his slander?' They said: 'The hadd (prescribed punishment) also removes from him the punishment of the Hereafter, and it is a purification for him, for the hudud are a purification for those upon whom they are imposed. How, then, is his testimony rejected when he has not been purified by the hadd, and yet he is to be rejected at his purest? For by the hadd and repentance he may attain complete purity.'"

They said: "The rejection of testimony due to slander is only based on the cause that Allah mentioned immediately after this ruling, namely fisq (grave moral transgression). Fisq has been removed by repentance, and it was the cause of the rejection, so the effect that followed from it, namely the prohibition, must be removed. They said: 'The slanderer is a fasiq (transgressor) by his slander, whether or not he was given the hadd. How, then, is his testimony accepted while he is in the state of fisq, and rejected after the fisq has ceased?' They said: 'We have no precedent in the Shari'ah of a single sin, from which one repents, while its consequential effect, the rejection of testimony, remains. Is this not contrary to what is known from it, and contrary to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The one who repents from sin is like the one who has no sin"?'"

At this point it is said: "His repentance from slander places him in the position of one who did not slander, so it is obligatory to accept his testimony," or as they stated.

Those who oppose (acceptance) said: "Slander includes an offence against the right of Allah and the right of a human being, and it is among the gravest of crimes. Therefore, it is fitting that the deterrent be severe, and the rejection of testimony is one of the most powerful means of deterrence, because of the pain it inflicts on the heart and the injury it causes to the self. For it is the removal of the authority of his tongue, with which he attacked the honour of his brother, and the nullification of that authority. Moreover, it is a punishment in the place of the offence, for the offence was committed by his tongue, so it is more fitting that the punishment be on it. We have seen that the Lawgiver took this into account when he cut off the hand of the thief, for it is a prescribed punishment in the place of the offence. This is not refuted by the fact that he did not make the punishment of the fornicator the cutting off of the organ with which he committed the offence, for several reasons:

"The first: it is a hidden organ, concealed and not visible to the eyes, so the intended lesson of the hadd is not achieved by cutting it off.

"The second: that would lead to the destruction of the organs of reproduction and the cessation of the human species.

"The third: the pleasure of the whole body in fornication is like the pleasure of that particular organ. Thus, what the whole body obtained of forbidden pleasure is like what the private parts obtained. For this reason, the hadd for wine-drinking is applied to the whole body.

"The fourth: cutting off this organ leads to death, and the offence of one who is not married (muhsan) does not warrant death, while the offence of the married person warrants the most grievous forms of killing, and cutting off some of his limbs is not proportionate to it. Thus the two are distinct."

They said: "As for the acceptance of his testimony before the hadd and its rejection after it, this is because it has been established that the rejection of testimony is made part of the hadd and its completion. So it is like an attribute and a complement of the hadd, and therefore it does not precede it. Moreover, the imposition of the hadd upon him diminishes him in the eyes of people and reduces his dignity, whereas before the hadd is imposed, his dignity remains intact and he has not violated it."

They said: "As for the one who repents from fornication, disbelief and killing, we accept his testimony because its rejection was a consequence of fisq, and that has ceased. This differs from our case, for we have shown that its rejection is part of the hadd, so the two are distinct."

Those who accept (his testimony) said: "The severity of deterrence has no defined measure. The purpose of deterrence has already been achieved through the hadd. Likewise, for all other crimes the Lawgiver made the achievement of deterrence through the hadd. Otherwise, his wives would not be divorced, his property would not be taken, he would not be removed from his post, and his narration (of hadith) would not be discarded, for that would be more severe in deterrence. Yet the Muslims have unanimously agreed to accept the narration of Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him. The severity of deterrence is among the widespread attributes that cannot be pinned down. Moreover, the pain of the heart and body and the injury to the self have been achieved through the beating that was inflicted upon his back. Furthermore, the rejection of testimony does not deter most slanderers. Rather, it affects and deters only the notable people, and it is rare for slander to be found among them. It is found mostly among the rabble, the base, and those who do not care whether their testimony is rejected or accepted. Also, how many a slanderer has lived out his life without ever giving testimony before a judge? The purpose of deterrence is to restrain souls from what they need and what they frequently commit. Moreover, this consideration you have mentioned is opposed by something stronger: the rejection of testimony forever entails the mischief of losing the rights of others and the nullification of testimony in a place where it is needed. Such harm does not follow from acceptance, for there is no harm in it for others when the one who is a trustworthy (ʿadl) penitent has reformed what lies between himself and Allah. There is no doubt that taking into account a benefit that entails a harm is less preferable than taking into account a benefit that entails several harms for the witness, the one in whose favour the testimony is given, and the one against whom it is given. The Lawgiver aspires to preserving rights for their rightful owners by every means and to avoiding their loss. How, then, would he nullify a right to which a just, approved person, whose testimony is acceptable, has testified concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his religion, in narration and in legal opinion?"

As for your statement, "The punishment is in the place of the offence," this does not necessarily follow, because of the punishment of the drinker and the fornicator mentioned earlier. Allah, glory be to Him, made the punishment for this offence fall upon the whole body rather than the tongue. He made the punishment of the tongue dependent upon fisq, which is the locus of suspicion. So when fisq is removed by repentance, there is no basis for punishment after it.

As for your statement, "The rejection of testimony is part of the completion of the hadd," this is not so, for the hadd is completed by carrying out its number (of lashes), and its cause is the slander itself. As for the rejection of testimony, it is a separate ruling required by the fisq resulting from the slander, not by the hadd. Thus slander necessitated two rulings: the establishment of fisq and the imposition of the hadd, and these two are distinct.

(Section)

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife Shurayk ibn Sahma' before the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned the hadith of li'an (mutual imprecation).

And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Look at her. If she gives birth to a child with dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'. And if she gives birth to one of such-and-such description, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya." She gave birth to one with the disliked description, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Had it not been for what has preceded from the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her."

He means, and Allah and His Messenger know best, by the Book of Allah, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah﴾.

By "the matter," Allah knows best, he means that he would have punished her by the hadd because of the child's resemblance to the man she was accused of. But the Book of Allah settled the judgment in detail and set aside every opinion that came after it, and there was no longer any room for ijtihad (independent reasoning) after it.

(A Benefit)

Allah, glorified is He, made the oaths of li'an come first from the husband's side. If the woman refuses to counter his oaths with her own oaths, the punishment becomes obligatory upon her by the hadd. This is the punishment mentioned in His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾.

For the claimant, when his side is strengthened by a single witness, the oath is prescribed on his side. Likewise, the heirs of the blood, when their side is strengthened by lawth (presumptive evidence), the oath is prescribed on their side and is reinforced by number, to magnify the gravity of a human life. Similarly, in li'an the husband's side is definitely stronger than the woman's, for his proceeding to destroy his marriage bed, to accuse her of indecency in front of witnesses, to expose himself to the punishment of this world and the Hereafter, and to disgrace his family and himself before witnesses, is something the nature of sensible people refuses and their souls shrink from. Were it not that the wife compelled him by what he saw and was certain of from her, he would not do so. Therefore his side is definitely stronger than the woman's, and so the oath is prescribed on his side. For this reason, qasama and li'an both involve execution, and this is the view of the people of Madina. As for the jurists of Iraq, they do not execute either by this or by that. Ahmad executes by qasama but not by li'an, while al-Shafi'i executes by li'an but not by qasama.

Nothing in any of this contradicts the authentic hadith, which is his saying ﷺ: "If people were given according to their claims, people would claim the blood and property of others. But the oath is upon the one who denies."

For this applies when the claimant has nothing but a bare claim. In that case, judgment is not given to him on the bare claim. But when his side is strengthened by a witness, or lawth, or something else, judgment is not given to him on his bare claim alone, but on the witness combined with the strengthening of his side and the oath. Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, ruled for one of the two women concerning the child, because her side was strengthened by compassion for the child and her preference for its life, while the other was content to have it killed, and he did not turn to the other's acknowledgment that it was hers.

And his saying: "He is her son." For this reason, among the chapter headings of the imams on this hadith is: "The latitude for a judge to say to a thing he does not do: 'I will do it,' in order to make the truth clear." Then he gave another heading, better than this and more profound, saying: "A ruling contrary to what the one in whose favor it is given acknowledges, when it becomes clear to the judge that the truth is other than what he acknowledged." Thus is the understanding of the imams of the texts and the deduction of rulings that intellects and natural dispositions bear witness to. By the life of Allah, this beneficial knowledge is not the guessing of opinions and the conjecture of assumptions.

And he said in (al-Turuq al-Hukmiyya):

A judge does not rule against the woman in li'an merely on her refusal without the husband's oath. If the husband swears and she refuses to swear, the judge rules against her either by imprisonment until she confesses or is subjected to li'an, as Ahmad and Abu Hanifa say, or by the hadd, as al-Shafi'i and Malik say.

And this is the stronger view, because Allah, glorified and exalted, only averts the punishment from her by her testimony of four testimonies. The punishment averted from her by her li'an is the punishment mentioned in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

It is the punishment of the hadd. For this reason He mentioned it in the definite form, the lam being that of reference (al-'ahd), so it is known that the punishment is the one previously mentioned. For this reason, the husband's oaths were begun with first, because of the strength of his side, and the woman was empowered to counter his oath with hers. If she refuses, there is nothing left to counter his oath, so he has done his part, and the woman's refusal strengthens him, and the judgment is rendered against her by his oath and her refusal. If it is said: it would have been possible to begin with her oaths, and if she refused, the husband would swear and she would be punished by the hadd, just as when someone claims a right from another and he refuses to swear, the oath is returned to the claimant and judgment is given for him. Why was li'an not prescribed in this way, since the woman is the defendant? Rather, the oath was prescribed on the claimant's side first, and this has no parallel in claims.

It is said: since the husband is the one who accuses her, the consequence of his accusation is that he should be punished by the hadd on her behalf. So he was empowered to ward off the hadd from himself by his li'an. Then she was required afterwards to either confess or swear li'an. If she confesses, she is punished by the hadd, and if she denies and swears li'an, she averts the hadd from herself by her li'an, just as he can avert the hadd from himself by his li'an.

The beginning with him was more appropriate, because he is the claimant, and his oaths stand in place of evidence. But since they are below four witnesses in strength, the woman was empowered to repel them with her oaths. If she refuses to repel them, his side is strengthened and the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. She is not punished by the mere li'an of the husband, nor by the mere refusal of the woman, but by the combination of the two matters. The oaths were reinforced by being four in number, just as the oaths of the claimants in qasama were reinforced by being fifty, so that the oaths might stand in place of witnesses.

There is a third view on this question, which is that judgment is not given by refusal or by returning the oath, but the defendant is imprisoned until he answers with a confession or a denial, with an oath accompanying it. This is a view in the school of Ahmad, and one of the two opinions of the followers of al-Shafi'i. It is also the view of Ibn Abi Layla, for he said: "I will not leave him until he confesses or swears."

[The ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning li'an]

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful. And the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾.

And it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, that "'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani said to 'Asim ibn 'Adi: 'What do you say if a man finds another man with his wife? Will he kill him, and will you kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me.' So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked the questions and criticized them, until what 'Asim heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily upon him. Then 'Uwaymir himself asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: 'Indeed, it has been revealed concerning you and your companion. Go and bring her.' So they performed li'an in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they finished, he said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him."

Al-Zuhri said: "That became the sunnah for those who perform li'an."

Sahl said: "She was pregnant, and her son was ascribed to his mother. Then the sunnah established that he would inherit from her and she would inherit from him what Allah had prescribed for her."

In another wording: "They performed li'an in the mosque, and he separated from her in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is the separation between every two who perform li'an.'"

Sahl's saying, "She was pregnant," to the end, is, in al-Bukhari, a statement of al-Zuhri. In al-Bukhari also: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Look. If she gives birth to a child with black hair, large dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except truthfully about her. And if she gives birth to a child that is reddish, like a lizard, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except falsely about her.'" She gave birth to him in the description by which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had described him, confirming 'Uwaymir.

In another wording: "She was pregnant, and he denied her pregnancy." In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, that "a certain man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you say if one of us finds his wife committing an indecency? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he keeps silent, he keeps silent over such a thing?' The Prophet ﷺ was silent and did not answer him. Then, after that, the man came to him and said: 'Indeed the matter I asked you about has befallen me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses in Surat al-Nur: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ [al-Nur: 6]. He recited them to him, admonished him, reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I did not lie against her.' Then he called her, admonished her, reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, he is surely a liar.' So he began with the man, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, and the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the liars, and the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was of the truthful. Then he separated between them."

In the two Sahihs, from him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the two who performed li'an: 'Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is a liar. There is no way for you over her.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?' He said: 'You have no property. If you were truthful about her, then it is for what you made lawful from her private part, and if you were false about her, then it is further from you than she is.'"

In another wording of the two: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated between the two who performed li'an and said: 'By Allah, one of you is surely a liar. Is there among you one who will repent?'"

And in both of them from him: "A man performed li'an in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them and attached the child to its mother."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the two who performed li'an: "The man testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, then he invoked the curse upon himself for the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then she went to invoke the curse, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: 'Stop.' But she refused and invoked the curse. When he turned away, he said: 'Perhaps she will bring forth a child who is black and curly-haired.' And she brought forth a child who was black and curly-haired."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, that "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife of adultery with Shurayk ibn Sahma', who was the maternal brother of al-Bara' ibn Malik, and he was the first man to perform li'an in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Look at her. If she gives birth to a child who is white, straight-haired, and with a squint in the eyes, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya. And if she gives birth to a child who is dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'.' He said: 'I was informed that she gave birth to one who was dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved.'"

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, a similar story: a man said to him: "Is she the woman about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If I were to stone anyone without evidence, I would have stoned this woman'?"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "No, that was a woman who used to show evil in Islam."

In Abu Dawud, in this hadith, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them, and decreed that her child should not be claimed for a father, nor should she be accused, nor her child accused. Whoever accuses her or her child, upon him is the hadd. And he decreed that she should have neither lodging nor maintenance from him, because they separated without divorce and without her being widowed."

And in the story, 'Ikrima said: "After that he became governor of Egypt, and he was not called by a father's name."

Al-Bukhari also mentioned: "That Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man upon his wife, does he go off to seek evidence?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept saying: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I am surely truthful, and Allah will surely send down what will clear my back from the hadd.' Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came down and revealed to him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ [al-Nur: 6] ... the verses. The Prophet ﷺ turned to her, and Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet ﷺ was saying:"

[Section: The wisdom of prescribing li'an (mutual oath-swearing, a sworn procedure between spouses accusing each other) only for a wife, and not for others]

As for his words, "and He made it so that the accuser may avoid the prescribed punishment (hadd) through li'an (mutual oath-swearing) with a wife, but not with a stranger, though both have brought shame upon them," this is among the greatest of the excellences of the Sharia. The one who accuses a stranger has no need to accuse her at all; her adultery does not harm him in any way, does not corrupt his marital bed, and does not attach to him children from another man. Accusing her is pure transgression and harm to a chaste, unaware, believing woman, so the prescribed punishment (hadd) is imposed on him as a deterrent and a penalty.

As for the husband, the adultery of his wife brings upon him shame and disgrace, the corruption of his bed, the attribution to him of another man's child, and the turning of her heart away from him toward someone else. So he needs to accuse her, to deny a corrupt lineage from himself, and to free himself from disgrace and shame, since he is the husband of a lewd, immoral woman. Proof of her adultery is usually impossible to establish, and she does not confess to it, and the husband's word against her is not accepted. Nothing remains except that they swear to each other with the most emphatic oaths: he invokes the curse upon himself, and she invokes the wrath upon herself, if they are both lying.

Then the marriage is dissolved between them, since neither of them can ever be content with the other. This is the best ruling by which the matter is settled between them in this world, and there is nothing after it more just, more wise, or more beneficial. Even if the minds of all the worlds were gathered together, they would not reach it. Blessed is He who has made clear His lordship, His oneness, His wisdom and His knowledge in His law and His creation.

[Section: Beginning with the man in li'an]

Among its features is that the man begins the li'an, just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger began with him. If the woman had begun, her li'an would not be counted according to the majority (jumhur) of scholars, though Abu Hanifa counted it. Allah, glorified is He, began the prescribed punishment (hadd) by mentioning the woman, saying: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

In li'an He mentioned the husband first. This is most appropriate, because adultery by a woman is more abominable than by a man, since she adds to the violation of Allah's right the corruption of her husband's bed, attributing to him the lineage of another, disgracing her family and relatives, offending the husband's purely personal right, betraying him in it, removing his honor before people, causing him to be reproached for keeping a lewd woman, and other corruptions of her adultery. Therefore beginning with her in the prescribed punishment was more important. As for li'an, it is the husband who accused her and exposed her to li'an, violated her honor, charged her with a grave matter, and disgraced her before her people and family. For this reason the husband is obligated to suffer the prescribed punishment if he does not perform li'an, so beginning with him in li'an is more fitting than beginning with her.

[Section: Neither of them is accepted with fewer than five repetitions]

Among its features is that the man's li'an is not accepted with fewer than five repetitions, nor is the woman's. It is not accepted from him to substitute the curse with wrath, distancing or anger, nor from her to substitute wrath with curse, distancing or anger. Rather, each of them brings what Allah has prescribed for him or her of these, both in law and by decree. This is the more correct of the two opinions in the school of Ahmad, Malik and others.

Among its features is that it does not require adding anything to the wording mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Indeed, it is not recommended to do so. He does not need to say: "I testify by Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, who knows the secret as He knows the open," or the like. Rather, it is sufficient for him to say: "I testify by Allah that I am truly among the truthful," and she says: "I testify by Allah that he is truly among the liars." He does not need to say: "concerning what I have accused her of, adultery," nor should she say: "he is truly among the liars concerning what he accused me of, adultery." It is not required that, if he claims to have seen it, he says: "I saw her committing adultery like the kohl stick in the kohl pot." There is no basis for this in the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger. Allah, glorified is He, in His knowledge and wisdom, has sufficed us with what He has legislated for us and commanded us, without the burden of adding to it.

(Section)

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife Shurayk ibn Sahma' before the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned the hadith of li'an (mutual imprecation).

And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Look at her. If she gives birth to a child with dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'. And if she gives birth to one of such-and-such description, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya." She gave birth to one with the disliked description, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Had it not been for what has preceded from the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her."

He means, and Allah and His Messenger know best, by the Book of Allah, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah﴾.

By "the matter," Allah knows best, he means that he would have punished her by the hadd because of the child's resemblance to the man she was accused of. But the Book of Allah settled the judgment in detail and set aside every opinion that came after it, and there was no longer any room for ijtihad (independent reasoning) after it.

(A Benefit)

Allah, glorified is He, made the oaths of li'an come first from the husband's side. If the woman refuses to counter his oaths with her own oaths, the punishment becomes obligatory upon her by the hadd. This is the punishment mentioned in His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾.

For the claimant, when his side is strengthened by a single witness, the oath is prescribed on his side. Likewise, the heirs of the blood, when their side is strengthened by lawth (presumptive evidence), the oath is prescribed on their side and is reinforced by number, to magnify the gravity of a human life. Similarly, in li'an the husband's side is definitely stronger than the woman's, for his proceeding to destroy his marriage bed, to accuse her of indecency in front of witnesses, to expose himself to the punishment of this world and the Hereafter, and to disgrace his family and himself before witnesses, is something the nature of sensible people refuses and their souls shrink from. Were it not that the wife compelled him by what he saw and was certain of from her, he would not do so. Therefore his side is definitely stronger than the woman's, and so the oath is prescribed on his side. For this reason, qasama and li'an both involve execution, and this is the view of the people of Madina. As for the jurists of Iraq, they do not execute either by this or by that. Ahmad executes by qasama but not by li'an, while al-Shafi'i executes by li'an but not by qasama.

Nothing in any of this contradicts the authentic hadith, which is his saying ﷺ: "If people were given according to their claims, people would claim the blood and property of others. But the oath is upon the one who denies."

For this applies when the claimant has nothing but a bare claim. In that case, judgment is not given to him on the bare claim. But when his side is strengthened by a witness, or lawth, or something else, judgment is not given to him on his bare claim alone, but on the witness combined with the strengthening of his side and the oath. Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, ruled for one of the two women concerning the child, because her side was strengthened by compassion for the child and her preference for its life, while the other was content to have it killed, and he did not turn to the other's acknowledgment that it was hers.

And his saying: "He is her son." For this reason, among the chapter headings of the imams on this hadith is: "The latitude for a judge to say to a thing he does not do: 'I will do it,' in order to make the truth clear." Then he gave another heading, better than this and more profound, saying: "A ruling contrary to what the one in whose favor it is given acknowledges, when it becomes clear to the judge that the truth is other than what he acknowledged." Thus is the understanding of the imams of the texts and the deduction of rulings that intellects and natural dispositions bear witness to. By the life of Allah, this beneficial knowledge is not the guessing of opinions and the conjecture of assumptions.

And he said in (al-Turuq al-Hukmiyya):

A judge does not rule against the woman in li'an merely on her refusal without the husband's oath. If the husband swears and she refuses to swear, the judge rules against her either by imprisonment until she confesses or is subjected to li'an, as Ahmad and Abu Hanifa say, or by the hadd, as al-Shafi'i and Malik say.

And this is the stronger view, because Allah, glorified and exalted, only averts the punishment from her by her testimony of four testimonies. The punishment averted from her by her li'an is the punishment mentioned in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

It is the punishment of the hadd. For this reason He mentioned it in the definite form, the lam being that of reference (al-'ahd), so it is known that the punishment is the one previously mentioned. For this reason, the husband's oaths were begun with first, because of the strength of his side, and the woman was empowered to counter his oath with hers. If she refuses, there is nothing left to counter his oath, so he has done his part, and the woman's refusal strengthens him, and the judgment is rendered against her by his oath and her refusal. If it is said: it would have been possible to begin with her oaths, and if she refused, the husband would swear and she would be punished by the hadd, just as when someone claims a right from another and he refuses to swear, the oath is returned to the claimant and judgment is given for him. Why was li'an not prescribed in this way, since the woman is the defendant? Rather, the oath was prescribed on the claimant's side first, and this has no parallel in claims.

It is said: since the husband is the one who accuses her, the consequence of his accusation is that he should be punished by the hadd on her behalf. So he was empowered to ward off the hadd from himself by his li'an. Then she was required afterwards to either confess or swear li'an. If she confesses, she is punished by the hadd, and if she denies and swears li'an, she averts the hadd from herself by her li'an, just as he can avert the hadd from himself by his li'an.

The beginning with him was more appropriate, because he is the claimant, and his oaths stand in place of evidence. But since they are below four witnesses in strength, the woman was empowered to repel them with her oaths. If she refuses to repel them, his side is strengthened and the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. She is not punished by the mere li'an of the husband, nor by the mere refusal of the woman, but by the combination of the two matters. The oaths were reinforced by being four in number, just as the oaths of the claimants in qasama were reinforced by being fifty, so that the oaths might stand in place of witnesses.

There is a third view on this question, which is that judgment is not given by refusal or by returning the oath, but the defendant is imprisoned until he answers with a confession or a denial, with an oath accompanying it. This is a view in the school of Ahmad, and one of the two opinions of the followers of al-Shafi'i. It is also the view of Ibn Abi Layla, for he said: "I will not leave him until he confesses or swears."

[The ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning li'an]

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful. And the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾.

And it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, that "'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani said to 'Asim ibn 'Adi: 'What do you say if a man finds another man with his wife? Will he kill him, and will you kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me.' So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked the questions and criticized them, until what 'Asim heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily upon him. Then 'Uwaymir himself asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: 'Indeed, it has been revealed concerning you and your companion. Go and bring her.' So they performed li'an in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they finished, he said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him."

Al-Zuhri said: "That became the sunnah for those who perform li'an."

Sahl said: "She was pregnant, and her son was ascribed to his mother. Then the sunnah established that he would inherit from her and she would inherit from him what Allah had prescribed for her."

In another wording: "They performed li'an in the mosque, and he separated from her in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is the separation between every two who perform li'an.'"

Sahl's saying, "She was pregnant," to the end, is, in al-Bukhari, a statement of al-Zuhri. In al-Bukhari also: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Look. If she gives birth to a child with black hair, large dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except truthfully about her. And if she gives birth to a child that is reddish, like a lizard, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except falsely about her.'" In another wording: "She was pregnant, and he denied her pregnancy." In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, that "a certain man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you say if one of us finds his wife committing an indecency? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he keeps silent, he keeps silent over such a thing?' The Prophet ﷺ was silent and did not answer him. Then, after that, the man came to him and said: 'Indeed the matter I asked you about has befallen me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses in Surat al-Nur: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ [al-Nur: 6]. He recited them to him, admonished him, reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I did not lie against her.' Then he called her, admonished her, reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, he is surely a liar.' So he began with the man, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, and the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the liars, and the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was of the truthful. Then he separated between them."

In the two Sahihs, from him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the two who performed li'an: 'Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is a liar. There is no way for you over her.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?' He said: 'You have no property. If you were truthful about her, then it is for what you made lawful from her private part, and if you were false about her, then it is further from you than she is.'"

In another wording of the two: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated between the two who performed li'an and said: 'By Allah, one of you is surely a liar. Is there among you one who will repent?'"

And in both of them from him: "A man performed li'an in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them and attached the child to its mother."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the two who performed li'an: "The man testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, then he invoked the curse upon himself for the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then she went to invoke the curse, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: 'Stop.' But she refused and invoked the curse. When he turned away, he said: 'Perhaps she will bring forth a child who is black and curly-haired.' And she brought forth a child who was black and curly-haired."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, that "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife of adultery with Shurayk ibn Sahma', who was the maternal brother of al-Bara' ibn Malik, and he was the first man to perform li'an in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Look at her. If she gives birth to a child who is white, straight-haired, and with a squint in the eyes, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya. And if she gives birth to a child who is dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'.' He said: 'I was informed that she gave birth to one who was dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved.'"

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, a similar story: a man said to him: "Is she the woman about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If I were to stone anyone without evidence, I would have stoned this woman'?"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "No, that was a woman who used to show evil in Islam."

In Abu Dawud, in this hadith, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them, and decreed that her child should not be claimed for a father, nor should she be accused, nor her child accused. Whoever accuses her or her child, upon him is the hadd. And he decreed that she should have neither lodging nor maintenance from him, because they separated without divorce and without her being widowed."

And in the story, 'Ikrima said: "After that he became governor of Egypt, and he was not called by a father's name."

Al-Bukhari also mentioned: "That Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man upon his wife, does he go off to seek evidence?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept saying: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I am surely truthful, and Allah will surely send down what will clear my back from the hadd.' Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came down and revealed to him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ [al-Nur: 6] ... the verses. The Prophet ﷺ turned to her, and Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet ﷺ was saying:"

[Section: The wisdom of prescribing li'an (mutual oath-swearing, a sworn procedure between spouses accusing each other) only for a wife, and not for others]

As for his words, "and He made it so that the accuser may avoid the prescribed punishment (hadd) through li'an (mutual oath-swearing) with a wife, but not with a stranger, though both have brought shame upon them," this is among the greatest of the excellences of the Sharia. The one who accuses a stranger has no need to accuse her at all; her adultery does not harm him in any way, does not corrupt his marital bed, and does not attach to him children from another man. Accusing her is pure transgression and harm to a chaste, unaware, believing woman, so the prescribed punishment (hadd) is imposed on him as a deterrent and a penalty.

As for the husband, the adultery of his wife brings upon him shame and disgrace, the corruption of his bed, the attribution to him of another man's child, and the turning of her heart away from him toward someone else. So he needs to accuse her, to deny a corrupt lineage from himself, and to free himself from disgrace and shame, since he is the husband of a lewd, immoral woman. Proof of her adultery is usually impossible to establish, and she does not confess to it, and the husband's word against her is not accepted. Nothing remains except that they swear to each other with the most emphatic oaths: he invokes the curse upon himself, and she invokes the wrath upon herself, if they are both lying.

Then the marriage is dissolved between them, since neither of them can ever be content with the other. This is the best ruling by which the matter is settled between them in this world, and there is nothing after it more just, more wise, or more beneficial. Even if the minds of all the worlds were gathered together, they would not reach it. Blessed is He who has made clear His lordship, His oneness, His wisdom and His knowledge in His law and His creation.

[Section: Beginning with the man in li'an]

Among its features is that the man begins the li'an, just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger began with him. If the woman had begun, her li'an would not be counted according to the majority (jumhur) of scholars, though Abu Hanifa counted it. Allah, glorified is He, began the prescribed punishment (hadd) by mentioning the woman, saying: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

In li'an He mentioned the husband first. This is most appropriate, because adultery by a woman is more abominable than by a man, since she adds to the violation of Allah's right the corruption of her husband's bed, attributing to him the lineage of another, disgracing her family and relatives, offending the husband's purely personal right, betraying him in it, removing his honor before people, causing him to be reproached for keeping a lewd woman, and other corruptions of her adultery. Therefore beginning with her in the prescribed punishment was more important. As for li'an, it is the husband who accused her and exposed her to li'an, violated her honor, charged her with a grave matter, and disgraced her before her people and family. For this reason the husband is obligated to suffer the prescribed punishment if he does not perform li'an, so beginning with him in li'an is more fitting than beginning with her.

[Section: Neither of them is accepted with fewer than five repetitions]

Among its features is that the man's li'an is not accepted with fewer than five repetitions, nor is the woman's. It is not accepted from him to substitute the curse with wrath, distancing or anger, nor from her to substitute wrath with curse, distancing or anger. Rather, each of them brings what Allah has prescribed for him or her of these, both in law and by decree. This is the more correct of the two opinions in the school of Ahmad, Malik and others.

Among its features is that it does not require adding anything to the wording mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Indeed, it is not recommended to do so. He does not need to say: "I testify by Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, who knows the secret as He knows the open," or the like. Rather, it is sufficient for him to say: "I testify by Allah that I am truly among the truthful," and she says: "I testify by Allah that he is truly among the liars." He does not need to say: "concerning what I have accused her of, adultery," nor should she say: "he is truly among the liars concerning what he accused me of, adultery." It is not required that, if he claims to have seen it, he says: "I saw her committing adultery like the kohl stick in the kohl pot." There is no basis for this in the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger. Allah, glorified is He, in His knowledge and wisdom, has sufficed us with what He has legislated for us and commanded us, without the burden of adding to it.

(Section)

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife Shurayk ibn Sahma' before the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned the hadith of li'an (mutual imprecation).

And the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Look at her. If she gives birth to a child with dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'. And if she gives birth to one of such-and-such description, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya." She gave birth to one with the disliked description, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Had it not been for what has preceded from the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her."

He means, and Allah and His Messenger know best, by the Book of Allah, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah﴾.

By "the matter," Allah knows best, he means that he would have punished her by the hadd because of the child's resemblance to the man she was accused of. But the Book of Allah settled the judgment in detail and set aside every opinion that came after it, and there was no longer any room for ijtihad (independent reasoning) after it.

(A Benefit)

Allah, glorified is He, made the oaths of li'an come first from the husband's side. If the woman refuses to counter his oaths with her own oaths, the punishment becomes obligatory upon her by the hadd. This is the punishment mentioned in His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾.

For the claimant, when his side is strengthened by a single witness, the oath is prescribed on his side. But when his side is strengthened by a witness, or lawth, or something else, judgment is not given to him on his bare claim alone, but on the witness combined with the strengthening of his side and the oath. Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon him, ruled for one of the two women concerning the child, because her side was strengthened by compassion for the child and her preference for its life, while the other was content to have it killed, and he did not turn to the other's acknowledgment that it was hers.

And his saying: "He is her son." For this reason, among the chapter headings of the imams on this hadith is: "The latitude for a judge to say to a thing he does not do: 'I will do it,' in order to make the truth clear." Then he gave another heading, better than this and more profound, saying: "A ruling contrary to what the one in whose favor it is given acknowledges, when it becomes clear to the judge that the truth is other than what he acknowledged." And he said in (al-Turuq al-Hukmiyya):

A judge does not rule against the woman in li'an merely on her refusal without the husband's oath. If the husband swears and she refuses to swear, the judge rules against her either by imprisonment until she confesses or is subjected to li'an, as Ahmad and Abu Hanifa say, or by the hadd, as al-Shafi'i and Malik say.

And this is the stronger view, because Allah, glorified and exalted, only averts the punishment from her by her testimony of four testimonies. The punishment averted from her by her li'an is the punishment mentioned in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

It is the punishment of the hadd. For this reason He mentioned it in the definite form, the lam being that of reference (al-'ahd), so it is known that the punishment is the one previously mentioned. For this reason, the husband's oaths were begun with first, because of the strength of his side, and the woman was empowered to counter his oath with hers. If she refuses, there is nothing left to counter his oath, so he has done his part, and the woman's refusal strengthens him, and the judgment is rendered against her by his oath and her refusal. If it is said: it would have been possible to begin with her oaths, and if she refused, the husband would swear and she would be punished by the hadd, just as when someone claims a right from another and he refuses to swear, the oath is returned to the claimant and judgment is given for him. Why was li'an not prescribed in this way, since the woman is the defendant? Rather, the oath was prescribed on the claimant's side first, and this has no parallel in claims.

It is said: since the husband is the one who accuses her, the consequence of his accusation is that he should be punished by the hadd on her behalf. So he was empowered to ward off the hadd from himself by his li'an. Then she was required afterwards to either confess or swear li'an. If she confesses, she is punished by the hadd, and if she denies and swears li'an, she averts the hadd from herself by her li'an, just as he can avert the hadd from himself by his li'an.

The beginning with him was more appropriate, because he is the claimant, and his oaths stand in place of evidence. But since they are below four witnesses in strength, the woman was empowered to repel them with her oaths. If she refuses to repel them, his side is strengthened and the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. She is not punished by the mere li'an of the husband, nor by the mere refusal of the woman, but by the combination of the two matters. The oaths were reinforced by being four in number, just as the oaths of the claimants in qasama were reinforced by being fifty, so that the oaths might stand in place of witnesses.

There is a third view on this question, which is that judgment is not given by refusal or by returning the oath, but the defendant is imprisoned until he answers with a confession or a denial, with an oath accompanying it. This is a view in the school of Ahmad, and one of the two opinions of the followers of al-Shafi'i. It is also the view of Ibn Abi Layla, for he said: "I will not leave him until he confesses or swears."

[The ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning li'an]

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful. And the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾.

And it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, that "'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani said to 'Asim ibn 'Adi: 'What do you say if a man finds another man with his wife? Will he kill him, and will you kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me.' So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked the questions and criticized them, until what 'Asim heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily upon him. Then 'Uwaymir himself asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: 'Indeed, it has been revealed concerning you and your companion. Go and bring her.' So they performed li'an in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they finished, he said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him."

Al-Zuhri said: "That became the sunnah for those who perform li'an."

Sahl said: "She was pregnant, and her son was ascribed to his mother. Then the sunnah established that he would inherit from her and she would inherit from him what Allah had prescribed for her."

In another wording: "They performed li'an in the mosque, and he separated from her in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is the separation between every two who perform li'an.'"

Sahl's saying, "She was pregnant," to the end, is, in al-Bukhari, a statement of al-Zuhri. In al-Bukhari also: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Look. If she gives birth to a child with black hair, large dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except truthfully about her. And if she gives birth to a child that is reddish, like a lizard, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except falsely about her.'" She gave birth to him in the description by which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had described him, confirming 'Uwaymir.

In another wording: "She was pregnant, and he denied her pregnancy." In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, that "a certain man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you say if one of us finds his wife committing an indecency? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he keeps silent, he keeps silent over such a thing?' The Prophet ﷺ was silent and did not answer him. Then, after that, the man came to him and said: 'Indeed the matter I asked you about has befallen me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses in Surat al-Nur: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ [al-Nur: 6]. He recited them to him, admonished him, reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I did not lie against her.' Then he called her, admonished her, reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, he is surely a liar.' So he began with the man, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, and the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the liars, and the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was of the truthful. Then he separated between them."

In the two Sahihs, from him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the two who performed li'an: 'Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is a liar. There is no way for you over her.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?' He said: 'You have no property. If you were truthful about her, then it is for what you made lawful from her private part, and if you were false about her, then it is further from you than she is.'"

In another wording of the two: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated between the two who performed li'an and said: 'By Allah, one of you is surely a liar. Is there among you one who will repent?'"

And in both of them from him: "A man performed li'an in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them and attached the child to its mother."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the two who performed li'an: "The man testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, then he invoked the curse upon himself for the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then she went to invoke the curse, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: 'Stop.' But she refused and invoked the curse. When he turned away, he said: 'Perhaps she will bring forth a child who is black and curly-haired.' And she brought forth a child who was black and curly-haired."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, that "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife of adultery with Shurayk ibn Sahma', who was the maternal brother of al-Bara' ibn Malik, and he was the first man to perform li'an in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Look at her. If she gives birth to a child who is white, straight-haired, and with a squint in the eyes, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya. And if she gives birth to a child who is dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'.' He said: 'I was informed that she gave birth to one who was dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved.'"

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, a similar story: a man said to him: "Is she the woman about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If I were to stone anyone without evidence, I would have stoned this woman'?"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "No, that was a woman who used to show evil in Islam."

In Abu Dawud, in this hadith, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them, and decreed that her child should not be claimed for a father, nor should she be accused, nor her child accused. Whoever accuses her or her child, upon him is the hadd. And he decreed that she should have neither lodging nor maintenance from him, because they separated without divorce and without her being widowed."

And in the story, 'Ikrima said: "After that he became governor of Egypt, and he was not called by a father's name."

Al-Bukhari also mentioned: "That Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man upon his wife, does he go off to seek evidence?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept saying: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I am surely truthful, and Allah will surely send down what will clear my back from the hadd.' Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came down and revealed to him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ [al-Nur: 6] ... the verses. The Prophet ﷺ turned to her, and Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet ﷺ was saying:"

She is not punished by the mere li'an of the husband, nor by the mere refusal of the woman, but by the combination of the two matters. The oaths were reinforced by being four in number, just as the oaths of the claimants in qasama were reinforced by being fifty, so that the oaths might stand in place of witnesses.

There is a third view on this question, which is that judgment is not given by refusal or by returning the oath, but the defendant is imprisoned until he answers with a confession or a denial, with an oath accompanying it. This is a view in the school of Ahmad, and one of the two opinions of the followers of al-Shafi'i. It is also the view of Ibn Abi Layla, for he said: "I will not leave him until he confesses or swears."

[The ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning li'an]

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves, the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful. And the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. And it would avert the punishment from her if she bears witness four times by Allah that he is surely of the liars. And the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾.

And it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, that "'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani said to 'Asim ibn 'Adi: 'What do you say if a man finds another man with his wife? Will he kill him, and will you kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me.' So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked the questions and criticized them, until what 'Asim heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily upon him. Then 'Uwaymir himself asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: 'Indeed, it has been revealed concerning you and your companion. Go and bring her.' So they performed li'an in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they finished, he said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him."

Al-Zuhri said: "That became the sunnah for those who perform li'an."

Sahl said: "She was pregnant, and her son was ascribed to his mother. Then the sunnah established that he would inherit from her and she would inherit from him what Allah had prescribed for her."

In another wording: "They performed li'an in the mosque, and he separated from her in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is the separation between every two who perform li'an.'"

Sahl's saying, "She was pregnant," to the end, is, in al-Bukhari, a statement of al-Zuhri. In al-Bukhari also: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Look. If she gives birth to a child with black hair, large dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except truthfully about her. And if she gives birth to a child that is reddish, like a lizard, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has spoken except falsely about her.'" She gave birth to him in the description by which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had described him, confirming 'Uwaymir.

In another wording: "She was pregnant, and he denied her pregnancy." In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, that "a certain man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you say if one of us finds his wife committing an indecency? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he keeps silent, he keeps silent over such a thing?' The Prophet ﷺ was silent and did not answer him. Then, after that, the man came to him and said: 'Indeed the matter I asked you about has befallen me.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses in Surat al-Nur: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ [al-Nur: 6]. He recited them to him, admonished him, reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, I did not lie against her.' Then he called her, admonished her, reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'No, by the One who sent you with the truth, he is surely a liar.' So he began with the man, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, and the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the liars, and the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was of the truthful. Then he separated between them."

In the two Sahihs, from him: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the two who performed li'an: 'Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is a liar. There is no way for you over her.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?' He said: 'You have no property. If you were truthful about her, then it is for what you made lawful from her private part, and if you were false about her, then it is further from you than she is.'"

In another wording of the two: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated between the two who performed li'an and said: 'By Allah, one of you is surely a liar. Is there among you one who will repent?'"

And in both of them from him: "A man performed li'an in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them and attached the child to its mother."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of the two who performed li'an: "The man testified four testimonies by Allah that he was surely of the truthful, then he invoked the curse upon himself for the fifth, that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was of the liars. Then she went to invoke the curse, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: 'Stop.' But she refused and invoked the curse. When he turned away, he said: 'Perhaps she will bring forth a child who is black and curly-haired.' And she brought forth a child who was black and curly-haired."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, that "Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife of adultery with Shurayk ibn Sahma', who was the maternal brother of al-Bara' ibn Malik, and he was the first man to perform li'an in Islam. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Look at her. If she gives birth to a child who is white, straight-haired, and with a squint in the eyes, then it belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya. And if she gives birth to a child who is dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved, then it belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'.' He said: 'I was informed that she gave birth to one who was dark, curly-haired, and thin-calved.'"

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, a similar story: a man said to him: "Is she the woman about whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If I were to stone anyone without evidence, I would have stoned this woman'?"

Ibn 'Abbas said: "No, that was a woman who used to show evil in Islam."

In Abu Dawud, in this hadith, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated them, and decreed that her child should not be claimed for a father, nor should she be accused, nor her child accused. Whoever accuses her or her child, upon him is the hadd. And he decreed that she should have neither lodging nor maintenance from him, because they separated without divorce and without her being widowed."

And in the story, 'Ikrima said: "After that he became governor of Egypt, and he was not called by a father's name."

Al-Bukhari also mentioned: "That Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man upon his wife, does he go off to seek evidence?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept saying: 'Evidence, or the hadd on your back.' He said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I am surely truthful, and Allah will surely send down what will clear my back from the hadd.' Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came down and revealed to him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ [al-Nur: 6] ... the verses. The Prophet ﷺ turned to her, and Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet ﷺ was saying:"

[Section: The wisdom of prescribing li'an (mutual oath-swearing, a sworn procedure between spouses accusing each other) only for a wife, and not for others]

As for his words, "and He made it so that the accuser may avoid the prescribed punishment (hadd) through li'an (mutual oath-swearing) with a wife, but not with a stranger, though both have brought shame upon them," this is among the greatest of the excellences of the Sharia. The one who accuses a stranger has no need to accuse her at all; her adultery does not harm him in any way, does not corrupt his marital bed, and does not attach to him children from another man. Accusing her is pure transgression and harm to a chaste, unaware, believing woman, so the prescribed punishment (hadd) is imposed on him as a deterrent and a penalty.

As for the husband, the adultery of his wife brings upon him shame and disgrace, the corruption of his bed, the attribution to him of another man's child, and the turning of her heart away from him toward someone else. So he needs to accuse her, to deny a corrupt lineage from himself, and to free himself from disgrace and shame, since he is the husband of a lewd, immoral woman. Proof of her adultery is usually impossible to establish, and she does not confess to it, and the husband's word against her is not accepted. Nothing remains except that they swear to each other with the most emphatic oaths: he invokes the curse upon himself, and she invokes the wrath upon herself, if they are both lying.

Then the marriage is dissolved between them, since neither of them can ever be content with the other. This is the best ruling by which the matter is settled between them in this world, and there is nothing after it more just, more wise, or more beneficial. Even if the minds of all the worlds were gathered together, they would not reach it. Blessed is He who has made clear His lordship, His oneness, His wisdom and His knowledge in His law and His creation.

[Section: Beginning with the man in li'an]

Among its features is that the man begins the li'an, just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger began with him. If the woman had begun, her li'an would not be counted according to the majority (jumhur) of scholars, though Abu Hanifa counted it. Allah, glorified is He, began the prescribed punishment (hadd) by mentioning the woman, saying: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

In li'an He mentioned the husband first. This is most appropriate, because adultery by a woman is more abominable than by a man, since she adds to the violation of Allah's right the corruption of her husband's bed, attributing to him the lineage of another, disgracing her family and relatives, offending the husband's purely personal right, betraying him in it, removing his honor before people, causing him to be reproached for keeping a lewd woman, and other corruptions of her adultery. Therefore beginning with her in the prescribed punishment was more important. As for li'an, it is the husband who accused her and exposed her to li'an, violated her honor, charged her with a grave matter, and disgraced her before her people and family.
