And there is nothing more harmful to them than this. The angel is with the right side of the heart, and the Satan is with the left side of the heart. Wars are continuous; they do not lay down their burdens until their term in this world is fulfilled. All falsehood aligns itself with Satan and the commanding self (al-ammarah), and all truth aligns itself with the angel and the self at rest (al-mutma'innah). War consists of alternating turns and rounds, and victory is with patience. Whoever is patient, endures, stays steadfast on the frontier (rabata), and fears Allah, to him belongs the final outcome in this world and the Hereafter. Allah, exalted is He, has decreed a judgment that is never changed: that the final outcome is for taqwa, and the final outcome is for the muttaqin (the God-conscious).

The heart is a blank tablet, and thoughts are engravings inscribed upon it. How, then, is it fitting for an intelligent person that the engravings on his tablet should be between falsehood, delusion, deceit, vain wishes, and a mirage that has no reality? What wisdom, knowledge, or guidance can be engraved alongside these engravings? If he wishes that such engravings be inscribed on the tablet of his heart, he is like one who writes beneficial knowledge on a place occupied with writing what has no benefit in it. If he does not empty the heart of wicked thoughts, beneficial thoughts will not settle in it, for they settle only in an empty place, as it has been said:

"Her desire came to me before I knew desire, and it found an empty heart, so it took root."

Many of the people of the spiritual path (ahl al-suluk) built their path upon guarding their thoughts, and not allowing any thought to enter their hearts, until their hearts become empty, receptive to unveiling (al-kashf) and to the manifestation of the realities of the higher realm within them. These people guarded one thing and lost sight of other things, for they emptied the hearts of any thought passing through them, so they remained empty with nothing in them. Satan found them empty, and sowed falsehood in them in forms that made them think these were the highest and most noble of things, and he substituted these for the thoughts which are the material of knowledge and guidance. When the heart is empty of these thoughts, Satan comes and finds the place vacant, and he occupies it with what suits the state of its owner, since he could not occupy him with lowly thoughts. So he occupied him with the will for detachment (al-tajrid) and emptiness from will, though there is no righteousness for the servant nor success except that the will which dominates his heart be the will of Allah's religious and commanding purpose (muradihi al-dini al-amri), which He loves and is pleased with. The occupation and concern of the heart is with knowing this in detail, establishing it, implementing it among creation, pursuing it, and seeking the means to it by entering into the affairs of creation to implement it. Satan misguides them from this by calling them to abandon and neglect it, under the guise of asceticism (zuhd) regarding the thoughts and means of this world.

He also made them imagine that their perfection lies in that detachment and emptiness. But far, far is that! Perfection lies only in the heart being filled with thoughts, wills, and reflection on attaining the pleasure of the Lord, exalted is He, from the servant and from people, and reflection on the ways to that and reaching it. Thus the most perfect of people are those with the most thoughts, reflection, and wills directed toward this, just as the most deficient of people are those with the most thoughts, reflection, and wills directed toward their own portions and desires, wherever they may be. And Allah is the One sought for help.

And here is 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: thoughts concerning the pleasure of the Lord, exalted is He, crowded upon him, so he sometimes put them to use in his prayer. He would prepare his army while in prayer, thus combining jihad and prayer. This is from the door of the overlapping of acts of worship within a single act of worship, which is a rare and noble door, through which only one who is sincere, skilled in seeking, deeply versed in knowledge, and high in aspiration enters, such that he enters into one act of worship and attains through it many different acts of worship. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whomever He wills.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 24, verse 31 (part 1 of 3):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known.﴾

He forbade them from stamping their feet, even though it is permissible in itself, lest it become a cause for men to hear the sound of the anklet, which would stir up in them the impulses of desire towards them.

[Section: The Station of Repentance (tawbah)]

When this station is firmly established and the servant has descended into this station, he rises from it to the station of repentance, because through self-examination what is his has become distinct from what is upon him. So let him gather his resolve and determination to descend into it and to exert himself towards it until death.

The station of repentance is the first of the stations, its middle, and its last. The travelling servant does not part from it, and he remains in it until death. If he moves on to another station, he moves on with it, keeping it as his companion and dwelling in it. Repentance is the beginning of the servant and his end, and his need for it at the end is as necessary as his need for it at the beginning. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance all together, O believers, that you may succeed﴾ [al-Nur: 31]. This verse is in a Medinan surah, in which Allah addressed the people of faith and the best of His creation, commanding them to turn to Him in repentance after their faith, their patience, their emigration and their striving. Then He made success conditional upon repentance, as the effect is conditional upon its cause, and He used the particle la'alla (perhaps), which conveys hope, to indicate that when you repent you are on the hope of success, for only those who repent hope for success. May Allah make us among them.

He the Exalted has said: ﴿And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11]. He divided the servants into the repentant and the wrongdoer, and there is absolutely no third division. He applied the name "wrongdoer" to whoever does not repent, and there is no greater wrongdoer than him, due to his ignorance of his Lord and of His right, and of the defect of his own self and the afflictions of his deeds.

In the authentic collection it is related from him (ﷺ) that he said: "O people, repent to Allah, for by Allah I repent to Him more than seventy times a day." His companions would count for him, in a single sitting before he stood up, [the words]: "My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, for You are the Accepting of repentance, the Forgiving" one hundred times. And he never prayed a prayer after the revelation of ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory﴾ to its end, except that he would say in it: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me."

It is also authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: "None of you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon the one most knowing of Allah among creation, of His rights and His greatness, and of what His majesty deserves of servitude, and most knowing of servitude and its rights and most upright in them.

[Section: The Innermost Secrets of the Reality of Repentance]

The author of al-Manazil said: The innermost secrets of the reality of repentance are three things: distinguishing piety from honour, forgetting the offence, and repentance from repentance, because the penitent is included in all of it from His saying ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance all together, O believers, that you may succeed﴾ [al-Nur: 31], so He commanded the penitent to repent.

Distinguishing piety from honour means that the aim of repentance is the fear of Allah, which is His dread and awe, and the carrying out of His command and the avoidance of His prohibition. So he acts in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, hoping for Allah's reward, and he abandons disobedience to Allah upon a light from Allah, fearing Allah's punishment, and he does not intend by this the honour of obedience. For obedience and repentance have an honour, outward and inward, so his aim is not honour, even if he knows that it is obtained for him through obedience and repentance. Whoever repents for the sake of honour, his repentance is tainted. In some reports: Allah the Exalted revealed to a prophet of the prophets: "Say to such-and-such ascetic: as for your renunciation of the world, you have hastened its comfort for yourself; and as for your devotion to Me, you have gained honour thereby; but what have you done concerning what is due to Me from you?" He said: "My Lord, and what is Your due from me after this?" He said: "Have you befriended for My sake a friend, or been hostile for My sake to an enemy?"

This means that comfort and honour are your portion, and you have attained them through asceticism and worship; but where is the upholding of My right, which is loving for My sake and hating for My sake?

So the matter lies in distinguishing, in the commands, between your portion and the right of your Lord, both in knowledge and in state.

Many of the sincere may have the condition of their souls confused for them in this matter, and none distinguishes it except the people of insight among them, and they among the sincere are like the sincere among people.

As for forgetting the offence: this is a matter requiring detail, and the people of the path have differed concerning it.

Among them is one who sees that occupation away from remembering the sin and turning away from it entirely is better, for the clarity of the moment with Allah the Exalted is more fitting for the penitent and more beneficial to him. For this reason it was said: "Mentioning harshness in a time of clarity is harshness."

And among them is one who sees that the better course is that he should not forget his sin, but should continue to place it before his eyes, observing it at all times, so that this produces in him brokenness, humility and submission, which is more beneficial to him than his collectedness and the clarity of his time.

They said: For this reason Dawud (peace be upon him) engraved the sin on his palm, and he would look at it and weep.

They said: Whenever you lose your way on the path, return to your sin and you will find the path.

The meaning of this is that when you return to your sin you are broken and humbled, and you lower yourself before Allah the Mighty and Majestic, humble, fearful and lowly; and this is the way of servitude.

The correct position on this question is a detailed one, and it is to be said: when the servant perceives within himself, in the state of clarity, a cloud of pretension, a fine film of self-admiration and forgetting the favour, and his self snatches him away from the reality of his poverty and deficiency, then remembering the sin is more beneficial for him, even if he is in the state of witnessing Allah's favour upon him, his complete need for Him, his annihilation in Him, and his lack of independence from Him in the least of his atoms. And if the state of love, joy in Allah, intimacy with Him, longing for His meeting, and witnessing the vastness of His mercy, forbearance and pardon has mingled with his heart, and the lights of the Names and Attributes have shone upon his heart, then forgetting the offence and turning away from the sin is more fitting and more beneficial for him. For whenever he returns to remembering the offence, that [state] is veiled from him, and he descends from height to lowness, and from one state to another, between which there is a gap greater than that between heaven and earth. This is from the envy of Satan towards him: he wished to bring him down from his station, and he set his heart roaming in the fields of knowledge and love, and in longing for the loneliness of wrongdoing and the confinement of the offence.

The first is that his witnessing of his offence is a favour from Allah, by which He bestowed grace upon him, so that He may secure him thereby from the hatred of pretension and the veil of hidden pride of which he is unaware. So this is one kind, and that is another kind.

This place contains a matter beyond expression. And success is from Allah, and He is the One sought for help.

[Section: Repentance from Repentance]

As for repentance from repentance: it is among the ambiguous expressions by which a truth or a falsehood may be intended, and the speaker's meaning in it may be true, yet he expresses it without distinction.

For repentance is among the greatest of good deeds, and repentance from good deeds is among the greatest of evil deeds and the most hideous of offences; indeed, if taken at face value it is disbelief. And there is no difference between repentance from repentance and repentance from Islam or from faith. So is it permissible to say "repentance from faith"?

Rather, what they mean is that one repents from seeing repentance as one's own doing, for it has only come about for him by the favour and will of Allah, and had he been left to himself his soul would never have permitted it at all. So when he sees it and witnesses its issuing from him and its occurrence through him, and is heedless of Allah's favour upon him, he repents from this seeing and this heedlessness. But this seeing and this heedlessness are not repentance, nor a part of it, nor a condition for it; rather they are another offence that befell him after repentance, so he repents from this offence just as he repented from the first offence. For he repents only from a sin, at the beginning and at the end. So how can it be said: he repents from repentance?

This is an incoherent statement, nor is it correct in itself. Rather, repentance may have a defect, a deficiency, and a blight that prevents its perfection, and its bearer may perceive this or may not perceive it, so he repents from the deficiency of repentance and from failing to render it its due.

This too is not repentance itself, but rather repentance from the absence of repentance, for the portion of it that exists is obedience from which one does not repent, and the portion that is missing is what one needs to repent of.

Thus repentance from repentance is only conceivable in one of these two ways.

Yes, there is here a third aspect, very subtle: whoever has attained the station of intimacy with Allah, and whose time is clear with Allah, such that his turning to Allah and his occupation with the remembrance of His bounties, Names and Attributes is the most beneficial thing for him, until he descends from this state and occupies himself with repentance from a past offence from which he has already repented, and he gazes at the offence and occupies himself with it away from Allah; this is a deficiency for which he ought to repent to Allah, and it is repentance from this repentance, because it is a descent from clarity to harshness. And Allah knows best.

[Section: Subtle Secrets of Repentance]

The author of al-Manazil said: The subtle secrets of repentance are three things. The first of them: that one should look at the offence and the decree, and recognise what Allah intends in it, in that He left you and its commission. For Allah the Mighty and Majestic only left the servant and the sin for the sake of two meanings:

The first: that he should know His might in His decree, His goodness in His concealment, His forbearance in granting respite to the one who commits sin, His generosity in accepting the excuse from him, and His grace in His forgiveness.

The second: that He should establish against His servant the proof of His justice, so that He punishes him for his sin by His own proof.

Know that the person of insight, when a sin proceeds from him, has regard to five matters:

The first: that he looks at Allah's command and prohibition, and this produces in him the acknowledgement that it is a sin, and the confession of the sin against himself.

The second: that he looks at the promise and the warning, and this produces in him fear and dread, which carries him to repentance.

The third: that he looks at Allah's enabling him to commit it, His leaving him between himself and it, and His decreeing it upon him, and that had He willed He would have preserved him from it. This produces in him various kinds of knowledge of Allah, His Names, His Attributes, His wisdom, His mercy, His forgiveness and pardon, His forbearance and generosity. This knowledge makes binding upon him a servitude to these Names, which is not attained at all without its necessary consequences, and he knows the connection of creation and command, and of recompense and promise and warning, with His Names and Attributes, and that this is the requirement of the Names and Attributes and their effect in existence, and that every Name and Attribute necessitates its effect and its requirement, and is linked to it inescapably.

This vantage point reveals to him gardens of delightful knowledge and faith, and the secrets of decree and wisdom, for which the bounds of speech are too narrow to express.

Among some of them is what the Shaykh mentioned: that the servant should know His might in His decree. That is, He, glorified is He, is the Mighty who decrees what He wills, and that for the perfection of His might He has passed judgement upon the servant and decreed upon him, by turning his heart and directing his will as He wills, and placing a barrier between the servant and his heart, and making him will and desire what the Mighty, Wise One wills from him. This is of the perfection of might, for none is able to do this except Allah, whereas the utmost a created being can do is to act upon your body and your outward self. As for making you will and desire what He wills and desires from you, none is able to do this except the Possessor of overwhelming might.

So when the servant knows the might of his Master and is mindful of it in his heart, and this witnessing is firmly established in him, then occupation with it rather than with the humiliation of disobedience is more fitting for him and more beneficial to him, for he becomes with Allah and not with his own self.

Among knowing His might in His decree: that one knows that he is governed and subjugated, his forelock in the hand of another, having no protection except by His protection, and no success except by His help. So he is lowly and insignificant, in the grip of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.

And among the witnessings of His might in His decree is also that one witnesses that perfection, praise, complete self-sufficiency, and might belong entirely to Allah, while the servant himself is most deserving of shortcoming, blame, defect, wrongdoing, and need. Whenever one's witnessing (shuhud) of his own humiliation, deficiency, defect, and poverty increases, his witnessing of Allah's might, perfection, praise, and self-sufficiency increases as well, and vice versa. Thus the deficiency and humiliation of sin lead him to the station of might.

Among them: the servant does not desire his Master's disobedience as disobedience. When he witnesses the operation of the Decree, and that He makes him the doer of what he does not choose, and that he wills by His will, choice, and decree, then he is, as it were, one who chooses without choosing, wills without willing, and intends without intending. This witnessing reveals Allah's might, His greatness, and the perfection of His power.

Among them: that one recognizes His goodness (birr), glorified is He, in concealing him while he commits the sin, even though He fully sees him. Had He willed, He would have exposed him before His creation, so that they would have been wary of him. This is from the perfection of His goodness, and among His names is al-Barr (the Most Good). This goodness from his Lord, of which the perfection of His self-sufficiency and the perfection of the servant's need for Him are the cause, leads him to occupy himself with contemplating this favor and witnessing this goodness, generosity, and bounty. Thus he is distracted from remembering the sin, and he remains with Allah, glorified is He. This is more beneficial to him than being preoccupied with his offense and witnessing the humiliation of his disobedience, for occupation with Allah and heedlessness of all else is the highest aim and the most excellent goal.

This does not require forgetting the sin absolutely. Rather, in this state, when he loses it, let him return to contemplating the sin and remembering the offense, for every time and station has a servitude (ʿubudiyyah) that befits it.

Among them: witnessing the forbearance (ḥilm) of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in granting respite to the one who commits sin. Had He willed, He would have hastened punishment upon him, but He is al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing) who does not hasten. This produces in him knowledge of his Lord, glorified is He, through His name al-Ḥalīm, the witnessing of the attribute of forbearance, and devotion through this name. The wisdom and benefit that result from this, through the intermediary of the sin, are more beloved to Allah and more beneficial to the servant, and more useful than their loss. The existence of what is necessitated without its necessary consequence is impossible.

Among them: the servant's recognition of his Lord's generosity in accepting his excuse when he offers an apology to Him, in the manner mentioned earlier, not by appealing to the Decree, for that is contention and argumentation, as was mentioned before. He accepts his excuse by His generosity and bounty. This produces in him occupation with His remembrance and gratitude, and a love for Him that had not existed in him before. For your love for one who thanks you for your kindness and repays you with it, and then forgives your wrongdoing and does not hold you accountable for it, is many times greater than your love for him for thanking you for the kindness alone. Reality bears witness to this. Thus the servitude of repentance after sin is one hue, and this is another hue.

Among them: that one witnesses His grace (faḍl) in His forgiveness. Forgiveness is a grace from Allah, for if He took you to account by sheer right, He would be just and praiseworthy. His pardon is only by His grace, not by your deserving it. This also produces in you gratitude to Him, love, return to Him in repentance, joy and delight in Him, knowledge of Him through His name al-Ghaffār (the Ever-Forgiving), the witnessing of this attribute, and devotion according to its requirements. This is more perfect in servitude, love, and knowledge.

Among them: that He perfects for His servant the stations of humiliation, submission, brokenness before Him, and need for Him.

For the self has within it a likeness to Lordship, and had it been able, it would have said as Pharaoh said. But He had power and manifested it, while others were powerless and concealed it. What frees the self from this likeness is the humiliation of servitude, which has four stations:

The first station is shared among all creatures: the humiliation of need and poverty before Allah. All the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth are in need of Him, poor before Him, while He alone is free of them. All the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth ask Him, and He asks no one.

The second station is the humiliation of obedience and servitude, which is the humiliation of choice. This is specific to the people of His obedience, and it is the secret of servitude.

The third station is the humiliation of love, for the lover is humble by essence, and in proportion to his love for the beloved is his humiliation. Love is founded upon humility before the beloved, as it has been said:

"Submit and be humbled before the one you love, for in the rule of passion there is no pride that can be raised or held."

And another said:

"The poor people of love, even their graves, upon them is the dust of humiliation among the tombs."

The fourth station is the humiliation of disobedience and offense.

When these four stations are combined, humiliation before Allah and submission to Him become most perfect and complete, for one is humbled before Him out of fear and awe, love and return, obedience, and poverty and dependence.

The reality of this is the poverty that the Sufis (al-qawm) point to. This meaning is too exalted to be called poverty. Rather, it is the very core and secret of servitude. Its attainment is the most beneficial thing for the servant and the most beloved thing to Allah.

Thus one must determine its necessary requirements: the causes of weakness and need, the causes of servitude and obedience, the causes of love and return, and the causes of disobedience and transgression, for the existence of what is necessitated without its necessary consequence is impossible. The purpose of assuming the non-existence of this necessitated thing and its consequence is that the benefit of its existence is better than the benefit of its loss, and the harm of its loss is greater than the harm of its existence. Wisdom is founded upon repelling the greater of two harms by enduring the lesser, and achieving the greater of two benefits by forgoing the lesser. He has opened the door for you. If you are among the people of knowledge, then enter; otherwise, close the door and go back in peace.

Among them: His beautiful names, the effects of which require their consequences as complete causes require their effects. The name al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing) and al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing) require something heard and something seen. The name al-Razzāq (the Provider) requires someone provided for. The name al-Raḥīm (the Most Merciful) requires someone shown mercy. Likewise the names al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), al-ʿAfuww (the Pardoner), al-Tawwāb (the Acceptor of Repentance), and al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing) require one whom He forgives, accepts repentance from, pardons, and forbears with. It is impossible to nullify these names and attributes, for they are beautiful names, attributes of perfection, descriptions of majesty, and acts of wisdom, kindness, and generosity. Therefore their effects must manifest in the world. The one most knowing of Allah among creation, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, pointed to this when he said: "Had you not sinned, Allah would have taken you away and brought a people who sin, then seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them."

And if you suppose that all living beings were non-existent, then who would the Provider (al-Razzāq), glorified is He, provide for? And if you suppose that sin and wrongdoing were absent from the world, then whom would He forgive? Whom would He pardon? Upon whom would He accept repentance and forbear? And if you suppose that all needs had been cut off and the servants were all wealthy and free from affliction, then where would supplication, humble entreaty, and imploring be? Where would answering, witnessing of grace and favor, and singling out with blessing and honor be?

Glory be to the One who made Himself known to His creation by every kind of making-known, guided them to Himself by every kind of proof, opened for them all the paths to Him, then set up the straight path to Him, and made Himself known to them and guided them to Him: "So that whoever perishes may perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives may live upon clear evidence. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." [al-Anfāl: 42]

Among them: the greatest secret, which expression cannot penetrate, which allusion does not dare to approach, and which the caller of faith does not proclaim before the heads of witnesses. Rather, the hearts of the elite among the servants have witnessed it, and through it they have increased in knowledge of their Lord, love for Him, tranquility in Him, longing for Him, constant remembrance of Him, and witnessing of His goodness, gentleness, generosity, and kindness, and contemplation of the secret of servitude and a view over the reality of divinity. This is what is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from the hadith of Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant, when he turns back to Him, than one of you who was on a riding animal in a barren desert, and it ran away from him, carrying his food and drink. He despaired of it, then came to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of his mount. While he was in that state, behold, it was standing before him. He took hold of its halter, then said, from the intensity of his joy: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord,' he erred from the intensity of his joy." This is the wording of Muslim.

In the hadith is one of the principles of knowledge: that words which come from the servant's tongue by mistake, due to intense joy or intense anger or the like, are not held against him. For this reason, this man did not become a disbeliever by his saying: "You are my servant and I am your lord."

It is well known that the effect of anger on the absence of intention can reach this state or even greater than it. Therefore one should not hold the angry person accountable for what he says in the state of his intense anger, such as this kind of speech, nor does his divorce take effect by it, nor his apostasy. Imam Aḥmad explicitly interpreted the term ighlāq in His saying (ﷺ): "There is no divorce under ighlāq" as meaning anger. Many imams interpreted it this way, and others interpreted it as coercion and insanity.

Our shaykh said: It encompasses all of this, and it derives from ghalaq (being closed), because the speaker's intention is closed off, as if his heart was not opened to the meaning of what he said.

The point is that this joy has a matter that the servant should not neglect or turn away from, and only one who has a special knowledge of Allah, His names, His attributes, and what befits the might of His majesty comprehends it.

It would have been better for us to fold the discussion of it into what is suitable for the understanding of the people of this age, their knowledge, the limit of their steps in knowledge, and the weakness of their minds in bearing it.

Nevertheless, we know that Allah, mighty and majestic, will drive this merchandise to its merchants, and to one who knows its worth, even if it falls into the hands of one who does not know it on the way. For many a bearer of knowledge is not a jurist, and many a bearer of knowledge carries it to one who is more learned than himself.

Know that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, singled out the human species from among His creatures by honoring, favoring, and ennobling it, creating it for Himself, creating everything for its sake, and granting it from His knowledge, love, nearness, and honor what He did not give to anyone else. He subjected to it whatever is in His heavens, His earth, and between them. Even His angels, who are the people of His nearness, He made to serve it, and He appointed them as its guardians in its sleep and wakefulness, its travel and residence. He sent down His books to it and upon it, sent it as messengers and sent messengers to it, addressed it and spoke to it from Himself to it. From among them He took the intimate friend (Khalīl) and the one who spoke with Him (Kalīm), and the saints, the elite, and the scholars. He made them the mine of His secrets, the seat of His wisdom, and the locus of His love. He created Paradise and Hellfire for them. He created the command, and reward and punishment revolve around the human species, for it is the essence of creation, the one intended by the commands and prohibitions, and upon it fall reward and punishment.

Thus the human being has a status that the rest of created beings do not have. He created his father with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, made His angels prostrate to him, taught him the names of all things, and manifested his excellence over the angels and all creatures below them. He expelled Iblīs from His nearness and distanced him from His door, when he did not prostrate with the prostrators, and He took him as an enemy.

Therefore, the believer among the human species is the best of creation without qualification, and the chosen one of Allah among the worlds. He created him so that He might complete His favor upon him, so that His kindness to him might be continuous, and so that He might single him out with His honor and grace with what his wish had not reached, what had not occurred to his mind, and what he had not perceived. He asks Him for gifts and bounties, hidden and manifest, immediate and deferred, which are not attained except through His love, and His love is not attained except through obedience to Him and preferring Him over all else. So He took him as His beloved and prepared for him the best of what a loving, wealthy, capable, generous one prepares for his beloved when he comes to him. He made a covenant with him, in which He set forth His commands and prohibitions, and in that covenant He informed him of what brings him near to Him, increases his love and honor before Him, and what distances him from Him, incurs His wrath, and drops him from His eyes.

The beloved has an enemy, who is the most hateful of His creatures to Him. He has openly declared hostility, and He commanded His servants that their religion, obedience, and worship be directed to Him alone, rather than to their true Protector and Deity. He sought to lure away His servants and took from among them a party that supported him and allied with him against their Lord. They were enemies to Him along with this enemy. They call to what angers Him, they attack His lordship, divinity, and oneness, they revile and deny Him, they tempt His friends, and they harm them in every kind of way. They strive to eliminate them from existence, to establish their dominion, and to erase everything that Allah loves and is pleased with, replacing it with everything that displeases and angers Him. So He made him aware of this enemy, his methods, his deeds, and his fate, and He warned him against allying with them, entering their company, and being with them.

He informed him in His covenant that He is the most generous of the generous, the most noble of the noble, and the most merciful of the merciful; that His mercy precedes His wrath, His forbearance precedes His punishment, and His pardon precedes His taking to account; that He has showered His creatures with blessings and has prescribed mercy upon Himself; that He loves kindness, generosity, giving, and righteousness; that all bounty is in His hand, all good comes from Him, and all generosity belongs to Him. The thing He loves most is to bestow His generosity upon His servants, to extend bounty to them, to overwhelm them with kindness and generosity, to complete His favor upon them, to multiply His grace toward them, and to make Himself known to them through His attributes and names, and to draw them to Himself through His blessings and bounties.

He is the Generous by His very essence, and the generosity of every generous being is one that Allah created. And He will continue to create, forever, something less than an atom's weight compared to His generosity. Thus, the truly Generous in the absolute sense is none other than Him, and the generosity of every generous one is from His generosity. His love for generosity, giving, kindness, righteousness, and bounty, and for conferring favors and grace, is beyond what occurs to the minds of creatures or arises in their imaginations. His joy in His giving, His generosity, and His bounty is greater than the joy of the recipient in what he is given and takes. The more one is in need of something, the greater its worth, so when intense need combines with the great value of the gift and its benefit, what can be imagined of the joy of the giver? Thus the joy of the Giver, glorified is He, in His giving is more intense and greater than the joy of this one in what he receives. And to Allah belongs the highest likeness, for this is the nature of a generous person among creatures: he experiences joy, delight, happiness, and pleasure in his giving and generosity beyond what the recipient experiences. But the recipient is absorbed in the pleasure of receiving, oblivious to the joy and happiness of the giver. This is so even though he is in complete need of what is given, poor in relation to it, does not trust that someone like it will be given again, fears need of it when it is gone, and is exposed to the humiliation of seeking help from one like himself or one lower than himself, while his soul is naturally inclined to greed and miserliness.

So what can be imagined of the One who is exalted and far removed from all of that? Even if the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, the first and last of His creation, humans and jinn, the moist and the dry, were to stand in one plain and ask Him, and He gave each one what he asked for, it would not diminish what He has by the weight of an atom.

He is the Generous by His essence, just as He is the Living by His essence, the Knowing by His essence, the All-Hearing and All-Seeing by His essence. So His supreme generosity is one of the necessary consequences of His essence. Pardon is more beloved to Him than retribution, mercy is more beloved to Him than punishment, grace is more beloved to Him than justice, and giving is more beloved to Him than withholding.

When His servant, His beloved whom He created for Himself and prepared for all kinds of His honor and favor over others, who was made the place of His knowledge, to whom He sent down His Book and whom He sent His Messenger, whose affairs He attended to and did not neglect or leave purposeless, exposes himself to His anger, commits what angers Him and what He hates, runs away from Him, allies with His enemy and supports him against Him, and inclines toward him, severing the path of the blessings and kindness that He bestows upon him, which are the most beloved things to Him, and opens the path of punishment, anger, and retribution, then he has invited from the Generous, the Noble, the opposite of what He is described as: generosity, kindness, and righteousness. He has exposed himself to His being angered, displeased, and retaliating, and to His anger and displeasure being directed at what pleases Him, and His retribution and punishment being directed at the place of His generosity, righteousness, and giving. So by his disobedience he has invited from His acts something other than what He loves more, and the opposite of what is among the necessary consequences of His essence: generosity and kindness.

Then, this beloved, the one brought near and specially honored, suddenly turns away, runs off, rejects His honor, and turns aside from Him toward His enemy, even though he is in dire need of Him and cannot do without Him for the blink of an eye.

While that beloved is with the enemy, in his obedience and service, forgetful of his master, absorbed in agreeing with his enemy, having invited from his master the opposite of what he deserves, a thought occurs to him. He remembers his master's righteousness, compassion, generosity, and kindness, and he knows that he has no escape from Him, that his final destination is with Him, that he will be presented before Him, and that if he does not come to Him of his own accord, he will be brought to Him in the worst of circumstances. So he flees to his master from the land of his enemy, and strives hard in running toward Him until he reaches His door. He places his cheek on the threshold of His door and lays his head on the dust of His doorstep, humbled, supplicating, humble, weeping, grieving, flattering his master, asking Him for mercy, seeking His compassion, and apologizing to Him. He has thrown his hand toward Him, submitted to Him, given Him his reins, and cast his leash to Him. So his master knows what is in his heart, and in place of anger toward him, He returns to being pleased with him; in place of severity toward him, mercy for him; in place of punishment, pardon; in place of withholding, giving; and in place of taking to account, forbearance. Thus by repentance and returning, he has invited from his master what he deserves and what is required by His beautiful names and sublime attributes. So how will his master rejoice in him, when His beloved and friend has returned to Him willingly and by choice, and has resumed what his master loves from him by his own consent, and has opened the path of righteousness, kindness, and generosity, which are more beloved to his master than the path of anger, retribution, and punishment?

This is the place of the well-known story related about some of the gnostics (al-'arifin), that he once experienced wandering and fleeing from his master. He saw in one of the alleys a door that had been opened, and from it came out a boy, crying and calling for help, while his mother was behind him driving him away, until he came out. She closed the door in his face and went inside. The boy went a short distance, then stopped and reflected. He found no shelter except the house from which he had been expelled, and no one to take him in except his mother. So he returned, heartbroken and grieving, and found the door bolted. He lay down, placed his cheek on the threshold, and slept. His mother came out, and when she saw him in that state, she could not help but throw herself upon him, embracing him, kissing him, and weeping, saying: "My son, where are you going, away from me? Who will take you in besides me? Did I not tell you: Do not disobey me, and do not force me, by your disobedience toward me, to act contrary to what I am disposed to of mercy toward you, compassion for you, and my desire for good for you?" Then she took him and went inside.

So reflect on the mother's words: "Do not force me, by your disobedience toward me, to act contrary to what I am disposed to of mercy and compassion."

And reflect on his statement (ﷺ): "Allah is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child." Where does a mother's mercy stand in comparison to the mercy of Allah, which encompasses all things?

So when a servant angers Him by his disobedience, he has invited from Him the diversion of that mercy away from him. But when he repents to Him, he has invited from Him what He deserves and is more worthy of.

This is a brief summary that reveals to you the secret of Allah's joy at the repentance of His servant, greater than the joy of this man who found his riding beast in a desolate land after despairing of it.

Beyond this lies what expression falls short of, and what minds find too subtle to grasp.

Beware of the path of ta'til (denial of the divine attributes) and tamthil (likening Allah to creation), for each of them is a blameworthy station and a pasture that is, in its every state, unwholesome. Neither of them may find the scent of this matter, for the catarrh of ta'til and tamthil corrupts the sense of smell just as it corrupts the sense of taste, so one does not taste the flavor of faith nor find its fragrance. The most deprived of all the deprived is the one to whom wealth and good are offered but who does not accept them. There is no preventer of what Allah gives, and no giver of what He withholds. Bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of Great Bounty.

The meaning of "the righteous" (al-salihin) here is those who are fit for marriage (al-nikah). This is the more sound of the two interpretations. Some scholars held that it means those who are upright in faith (al-iman).

The first is more sound. Allah, glory be to Him, did not command them to marry off only the righteous and pious among their male and female slaves, just as He did not single them out for the obligation of maintaining them. Rather, it is obligatory for the master to provide for his male and female slave's chastity (if'af) just as it is obligatory for him to maintain them, for that is part of the completion of their welfare and their rights over their master. He stated the command to marry off female slaves in an unrestricted way, whether they were Muslims or disbelievers, and did not prohibit marrying a disbelieving slave-woman to a Muslim man.

(Question)

If it is said: Allah the Exalted has said, ﴿And marry off the single among you, and the righteous among your male and female slaves. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾

And He said in another verse, ﴿And let those who cannot find marriage keep chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾

He commanded them to seek chastity until the time of wealth, and commanded the marriage of those (slaves) despite their poverty, and informed that Allah the Exalted will enrich them. So what is the interpretation of each of the two verses?

The answer: His words, ﴿And let those who cannot find marriage keep chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾, concern free persons. Allah the Exalted commanded them to remain chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty, for if they marry while poor, they take on obligations they cannot meet, and they have no one to carry them out on their behalf.

As for His words, ﴿And marry off the single among you, and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾, in it He commanded them to marry off the single (al-ayama), meaning the women who have no husbands.

This is the common meaning of the word "ayyim" when used without qualification, though it is used for men when qualified, just as "a'zab" (unmarried) is used without qualification for men, though it is used for women.

Then He commanded them to marry off their male and female slaves when they are fit for marriage.

So the first verse concerns their marrying for themselves, and the second concerns their marrying them to others.

His words in this category, ﴿and your female slaves, if they are poor﴾, cover the three types mentioned in it, for the single woman is enriched by her husband's maintenance, and likewise the female slave.

As for the male slave, since he has no property, and his property belongs to his master, he is poor as long as he is a slave. Therefore a condition of wealth cannot be set for his marriage as long as he is a slave. Rather, his wealth comes only when he is freed and becomes self-sufficient through that manumission, while his need calls him to marriage while still enslaved. So Allah commanded that he be married off, and informed that He will enrich him from His bounty, either through his earnings or through his master's maintenance of him and his wife. Thus it was not possible to postpone his marriage until the wealth awaited for the marriage of a free man. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 24, verse 35 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) said, regarding the words of the Most High, ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾ [al-Anʿam: 103]:
He said: "That is His light, which is His light; when it manifests through Him, nothing can stand before it."

This light that appears to the sincere believer is the light of faith (nur al-iman), about which Allah informed in His words: ﴿The parable of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp﴾ [al-Nur: 35]. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: "The parable of His light in the heart of the believer." This light is attributed to the Lord, and it is said: "It is the light of Allah," just as Allah, glory be to Him, attributed it to Himself. What is meant is the light of faith, which Allah made for him as a creation and a bringing into being, as He said, the Most High: ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ [al-Nur: 40].

When this light takes firm root in the heart and shines within it, it overflows onto the limbs, so its effect is seen on the face and in the eyes, and it becomes apparent in speech and action. It may grow stronger until its possessor witnesses it directly, and that is due to the dominance of the rulings of the heart over him and the absence of the rulings of the self (nafs).

The eye is closely bound to the heart, revealing what is within it. So the material of light in the heart grows stronger, and its possessor becomes absorbed, through what is in his heart, away from the rulings of his senses, and even away from the rulings of knowledge, so he moves from the rulings of knowledge to the rulings of direct witnessing.

The secret of the matter: the rulings of nature and the self are one thing, the rulings of the heart are another, the rulings of the spirit (ruh) are another, the lights of acts of worship are another, the lights of the domination of the meanings of the Divine Attributes and Names over the heart are another, and the lights of the Holy Essence are a thing beyond all of that.

In this matter two kinds of people go astray: one of them is thick of veil and dense of nature; the other has little knowledge, and what is in the mind becomes confused for what is outside it, and the light of dealings becomes confused with the light of the Lord of the earth and the heavens. ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾.

(Section)
Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has presented the light in the heart of His servant as a parable that only those with knowledge understand, when He said, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The parable of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp; the lamp is in a glass; the glass is as if it were a dazzling star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides whom He wills to His light. And Allah presents parables for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: "The parable of His light in the heart of the Muslim."

This is the light that He deposited in his heart through knowledge of Him, love of Him, faith in Him and remembrance of Him. It is His light which He sent down to them, so He gave them life by it and made them walk by it among the people. Its root is in their hearts, then its material grows stronger and increases until it appears upon their faces, their limbs and their bodies, and even their garments and homes; one who is of their kind sees it, while all other creatures deny it.

When the Day of Resurrection comes, that light will manifest and, through their faith, will go before them in the darkness of the Bridge until they cross it. They will be in it according to the strength or weakness of their light in their hearts in this world. Some of them will have light like the sun, another like the moon, another like the stars, another like a lamp, and another will be given light on the tip of his big toe that flickers, shining once and extinguished another time. Since this is the state of his light in this world, he will be given on the Bridge according to that measure. Indeed, it is his very light made manifest to him directly. As for the hypocrite, since he has no steady light in this world, but his light was apparent and not inward, he is given an apparent light whose end is darkness and extinction.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has struck for this light, its place, its bearer and its material, a parable: the niche (mishkah), which is the recess in the wall, which is like the chest (sadr). In that niche is a glass of the purest glass, so much so that it is likened to a dazzling star in its whiteness and clarity; this is like the heart. It is likened to glass because it combines qualities that are in the heart of the believer: purity and tenderness. Through its purity he sees the truth and guidance, and through its tenderness mercy, compassion and kindness arise in him. He strives against the enemies of Allah, is harsh toward them, and is firm in the truth and steadfast in it through his firmness. No one quality of his cancels another or opposes it; rather, each supports and strengthens the other: ﴿Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾. And He, the Most High, said: ﴿It is by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them; and if you had been rude and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you﴾. And He, the Most High, said: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾.

In the impressions of hearts: they are the vessels of Allah the Most High on His earth; so the most beloved of them to Him are the most tender, the firmest, and the purest. Opposite this heart are two blameworthy hearts at opposite extremes:
The first: a stony, hard heart in which there is no mercy, no kindness, no piety; it has no purity by which to see the truth. Rather, it is tyrannical and ignorant: it has no knowledge of the truth and no mercy for creation.
Opposite it is a weak, watery heart with no strength and no firmness; it accepts every form, and has no power to retain those forms or to influence others, and whatever mixes with it leaves an impression on it, whether strong or weak, good or bad.

In the glass is a lamp, which is the light in the wick, and the wick is its bearer.

This light has a material: oil that has been pressed from an olive tree in the most balanced place, which the sun touches at the beginning and end of the day. Its oil is among the purest oils and farthest from turbidity, so much so that from its clarity it almost glows without fire. This is the material of the lamp's light.

Likewise, the material of the lamp's light that is in the believer's heart comes from the tree of revelation, which is the greatest of things in blessing and the furthest from deviation. Indeed, it is the middle course and the most balanced and the best of matters. It has not deviated like the deviation of Christianity nor the deviation of Judaism; rather, it is a middle path between the two blameworthy extremes in everything. This is the material of the lamp of faith in the believer's heart.

Since that oil has become so pure that it almost glows by itself, then it has mixed with fire, so its illumination is intensified by it and the material of the fire's light is strengthened by it, that is light upon light.

Likewise the believer's heart is luminous, almost recognizing the truth by its natural disposition (fitrah) and intellect, but it has no material from itself. Then the material of revelation comes, touches his heart and mixes with its brightness, so his light is increased by revelation upon the light with which Allah created him by nature. Thus the light of revelation and the light of nature are gathered in him: light upon light. He almost speaks the truth even before he hears any text; then he hears a text agreeing with what his nature has testified to, and it becomes light upon light. This is the condition of the believer: he perceives the truth by his nature in general terms, then he hears the text that brings it in detail, and so his faith arises from the testimony of both revelation and nature.

Let the discerning one reflect upon this great verse and its agreement with these noble meanings.

He, glory be to Him and exalted, mentioned His light in the heavens and the earth, and His light in the hearts of His believing servants: the intelligible light witnessed by insight and hearts, and the sensible light witnessed by eyes, by which the regions of the upper and lower worlds are illuminated. These are two great lights, one of them greater than the other. Just as, if either of them is absent from a place or position, no human or other creature can live there, because living beings come into being only where there is light, and places of darkness on which no light shines do not sustain life and never come to be, so too a nation in which the light of revelation and faith is absent is dead, and a heart from which this light is absent is dead without doubt, having no life at all, just as there is no life for living beings in a place without light.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, links life and light, as in His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and cannot emerge from it?﴾

Likewise His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was; but We made it a light, guiding by it whom We will of Our servants﴾.

[Section: On the mention of lights, containing noble benefits]
Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, named Himself Light, made His Book light, His Messenger ﷺ light, and His religion light; He veiled Himself from His creation by light, and made the abode of His friends a light that shines. Allah, the Most High, said: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The parable of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp; the lamp is in a glass; the glass is as if it were a dazzling star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides whom He wills to His light. And Allah presents parables for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Nur: 35].

It has been explained that ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth…﴾ means that He is the one who illuminates the heavens and the earth and the guide of the people of the heavens and the earth; by His light the people of the heavens and the earth are guided. This is merely His act; otherwise, the light, which is among His attributes, subsists in Him, and from it is derived His name "the Light," which is one of the Most Beautiful Names.

Light is attributed to Him, glory be to Him, in one of two ways: the attribution of a quality to what it qualifies, and the attribution of an effect to its agent. The first is like His words, the Most High: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord…﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], the verse; this shining will be on the Day of Resurrection by His light, the Most High, when He comes to judge. From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in the well-known supplication: "I seek refuge in the noble light of Your Face from that You should send me astray; there is no god but You." And in another narration: "I seek refuge in the light of Your Face by which the darknesses are illuminated." So he ﷺ informed that the darknesses shine by the light of His Face, just as Allah, the Most High, informed that the earth shines on the Day of Resurrection by His light.

In al-Tabarani's Mu'jam and his Sunnah, and the Kitab of Uthman al-Darimi, and others, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "With your Lord there is no night or day; the light of the heavens and the earth is from the light of His Face." What Ibn Mas'ud said is closer to the interpretation of the verse than the view of one who explained it as "the guide of the people of the heavens and the earth." As for one who explained it as "the illuminator of the heavens and the earth," there is no contradiction between that and the statement of Ibn Mas'ud. The truth is that He is the light of the heavens and the earth in all these senses.

In Sahih Muslim and others, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us and spoke five "words," saying: "Indeed Allah does not sleep, nor is it proper for Him to sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light; were He to uncover it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches."

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Did you see your Lord? He said: 'Light; how could I see Him?'" I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah say: its meaning is that there was light there, or that light prevented its seeing, so how could I see Him?

He said: What indicates this is that in some wordings of the Sahih, "Did you see your Lord? He said: I saw light." This hadith became a difficulty for many people, to the extent that some of them distorted it, saying: "Nurani ara-hu" (I see Him as luminous), treating it as the nisba ya', while the word is one word; this is an error both in wording and meaning. What caused them this confusion and error is that they believed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw his Lord, and his saying "how could I see Him?" seemed like a denial of seeing, so they were confused about the hadith, and some of them rejected it because of the instability of its wording. All of this is a departure from what the evidence requires.

Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, in his book "al-Radd," related the consensus of the Companions that he did not see his Lord on the night of the Mi'raj; some of them excepted Ibn Abbas from this. Our shaykh said: this is not a real disagreement, for Ibn Abbas did not say "he saw Him with the eyes of his head." Ahmad, in one of the two narrations, relied on this, where he said: "He saw Him, Mighty and Majestic, but did not say 'with the eyes of his head,'" and Ahmad's wording is like the wording of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. What confirms the correctness of what our shaykh said regarding the meaning of the hadith of Abu Dharr is the Prophet's ﷺ saying in the other hadith: "His veil is light." So this light is - and Allah knows best - the light mentioned in the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him: "I saw light."

[Section on the explanation of His words (The parable of His light…), the verse]
Section: On the explanation of His words, the Most High: ﴿The parable of His light…﴾ [al-Nur: 35], the verse.

His words, the Most High: ﴿The parable of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp…﴾ [al-Nur: 35] is a parable of His light in the heart of His believing servant, as Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and others said. There has been disagreement over the referent of the pronoun in "His light" (nurihi). It was said: it refers to the Prophet ﷺ, meaning the parable of the light of Muhammad ﷺ. It was said: its explanation is the believer, meaning the parable of the light of the believer. The correct view is that it refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the meaning is: the parable of the light of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, in the heart of His servant; and the greatest of His servants in share of this light is His Messenger ﷺ. This view, together with the return of the pronoun to the one mentioned, which is the apparent sense of the speech, encompasses all three possibilities, and it is the more complete in meaning and wording.

This light is attributed to Allah, the Most High, since He is the one who bestows it and gives it to His servant; and it is attributed to the servant, since he is its locus and receiver. So it is attributed to both the agent and the receiver. This light has an agent, a receiver, a locus, a bearer, and a material, and the verse includes mention of all these matters in detail.

The agent is Allah, the Most High, the one who pours out lights and guides by His light whom He wills. The receiver is the believing servant. The locus is his heart. The bearer is his resolve, determination and will. The material is his speech and his action. This wondrous similitude which the verse contains holds secrets and meanings, and shows the perfection of His blessing upon His believing servant by what He has bestowed upon him of His light, by which the eyes of its people are gladdened and their hearts delighted.

Regarding this simile, the scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) have two approaches. The first is the approach of the compound simile (al-tashbih al-murakkab). It is closer in its derivation and safer from artificiality. It consists of likening the whole sentence, in its entirety, to the light of the believer, without addressing the detail of each part of the comparandum (al-mushabbah) and matching it with a part of the comparison (al-mushabbah bih). Most of the similitudes of the Noble Qur'an follow this approach.

Reflect on the description of the niche (mishkah), which is a recess that does not pierce through, so that it gathers the light best. In it is placed a lamp, and that lamp is inside a glass (zujajah) that resembles a glittering star in its clarity and beauty. Its fuel is from the purest and most complete of oils, from the oil of a tree in the middle of an orchard (qara), neither eastern nor western, such that the sun strikes it at one of the two ends of the day. Rather, it is in the middle of the orchard, protected by its edges. The sun strikes it in the most balanced way, and afflictions are kept away from its edges. Because of the intensity of its illumination, and the purity and beauty of its oil, it nearly gives light even without fire touching it. This whole compound is the likeness of the light of Allah, the Exalted, which He placed in the heart of His believing servant and singled him out with.

The second approach is that of the detailed simile (al-tashbih al-mufassal). It is said: the niche is the chest (sadr) of the believer, and the glass is his heart. He likened his heart to the glass for its delicacy (riqqah), clarity (safa') and firmness (salabah). Likewise, the heart of the believer combines these three attributes: it is merciful, does good, is tender, and is compassionate towards creation through its delicacy.

Through its clarity, the images of truths and knowledge appear in it as they really are, and turbidity, filth and dirt are kept away in proportion to the clarity within it. Through its firmness, it becomes resolute in the command of Allah, the Exalted, stands firm for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, is stern towards the enemies of Allah, the Exalted, and establishes the truth for Allah, the Exalted. Allah, the Exalted, has made hearts like vessels, as one of the early pious predecessors (salaf) said: "Hearts are the vessels of Allah on His earth, and the most beloved of them to Him are the most delicate, the firmest and the purest."

The lamp is the light of faith in his heart. The blessed tree is the tree of revelation, which contains guidance and the religion of truth, and it is the material of the lamp from which it is kindled. "Light upon light" is the light of sound nature (fitrah) and sound perception, and the light of revelation and the Book. So one of the two lights is added to the other, and the servant increases in light upon light. For this reason, he nearly speaks the truth and wisdom before he hears what is in it by way of transmitted report (athar). Then the report reaches him in the same manner as what occurred in his heart and what he spoke, so that the witness of reason (aql), the Law (shar'), nature (fitrah) and revelation (wahy) agree with him. His reason, his nature and his taste show him that what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought is the truth. Reason and transmitted text do not in any way conflict in his view; rather, they confirm and agree with each other. This is the sign of light upon light, the opposite of the one in whose heart the waves of false doubts (shubah), corrupt imaginings and ignorant conjectures (zunun jahliyyat), which their adherents call "decisive rational proofs," crash together. These are in his chest, as Allah, the Exalted, said:

﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which are clouds: darknesses, some above others. When he extends his hand, he can barely see it. And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light.﴾ [al-Nur: 40]

Observe how these verses comprehensively include all the varieties of the children of Adam, with the most perfect arrangement, and encompass them in the most complete way.

(Section)

Whoever does not know himself, how will he know his Creator? Know that Allah, the Exalted, has created in your chest a house, which is the heart, and placed in its chest a throne for His knowledge, upon which sits the Most High Likeness (al-mathal al-a'la). He is established upon His throne in His essence, separate from His creation. The Most High Likeness, which is from His knowledge, love and monotheism, is established upon the couch of the heart. Upon the couch is a carpet of contentment. He placed on its right and left the attendants of His laws and commands. He opened to it a door from the Garden of His mercy, of intimacy with Him and longing for His meeting. He poured upon it from the torrent of His speech, which caused to grow in it varieties of fragrant plants and fruitful trees of various acts of obedience, glorification, praise, sanctification and exaltation. He placed in the middle of the garden a tree of knowledge (shajarat ma'rifah), which gives its fruit at all times by the permission of its Lord: love, turning in repentance, fear, joy in Him and delight in His nearness. He caused to flow to that tree what waters it from the governance of His speech, understanding of it, and acting upon His counsels. He hung in that house a lamp, which He lit with the light of His knowledge and faith in Him and His monotheism. It draws from a blessed tree, an olive tree, neither eastern nor western, whose oil nearly gives light even if no fire touches it. Then He surrounded it with a wall that prevents afflictions, corrupters and whoever harms the garden from entering, so that if they intend harm, it does not reach it. He stationed over it a guard of angels who protect it in its wakefulness and in its sleep. Then He informed the owner of the house and the garden of the one dwelling within it. So he is always concerned with improving the dwelling and mending its disorder, so that the dweller will be pleased with it as a residence. Whenever he senses the slightest disorder in the dwelling, he hastens to repair it and mend it, fearing the dweller's departure from it. So excellent is the dweller, and excellent is the dwelling.

Glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, how great is the difference between this house and a house over which ruin has taken hold, which has become a refuge for insects and vermin, and a place for the dumping of filth and foulness.

Whoever wishes to relieve himself and attend to his needs finds a ruin with no dweller in it and no guardian over it. It is prepared for relieving oneself, its corners dark, its smell foul, ruin has covered it and filth has filled it. No one feels at ease with it, and no one dwells in it except one suited to its habitation, from among insects, worms and vermin. Satan sits upon its couch, and upon the couch is a carpet of ignorance, in which desires flutter. On its right and left are the attendants of appetites. A door has been opened to it from the field of forsaking (al-khidhlan), loneliness, inclination to this world, contentment with it, and renunciation of the Hereafter. It has poured upon it from the torrent of ignorance, desire, polytheism and innovations (bida'). It has caused to grow in it varieties of thorns, colocynth, and fruitful trees bearing various sins and transgressions: additions, unsuitable embellishments, anecdotes, frivolities, things that provoke laughter, amorous poems and wine poems which stir up the committing of forbidden acts and discourage acts of obedience. In the middle of the field is a tree of ignorance of Him and turning away from Him. It gives its fruit at all times: wickedness, sins, heedlessness, play, licentiousness, going with every wind and following every desire. From its fruit come anxieties, griefs, sorrows and pains. But these are concealed by occupying the soul with its frivolity and play. When it awakens from its intoxication, it brings forth every worry, grief, sorrow, anxiety and constricted living. Into that tree flows what waters it: following desire, long hopes and delusion. Then He abandons that house and its darkness and the ruin of its walls, such that no corrupter, animal, harmful creature or filth is prevented from entering it.

Glory be to the Creator of this house and of that house.

Whoever knows his house, and appreciates the one who dwells in it, and appreciates what is in it of treasures, stores and instruments, benefits from his life and his soul. Whoever is ignorant of that has ignorance of himself and wastes his happiness.

And success is from Allah.

**[The Divisions of People in Relation to What Allah Sent His Messenger ﷺ With]**

People are of two kinds: the people of guidance and insight (*basa'ir*), who know that the truth lies in what the Messenger ﷺ brought from Allah, and that whatever opposes it consists of doubts (*shubuhat*, sing. *shubhah*). The matter of these doubts is obscure to those whose share of reason and revealed knowledge (*al-sam'*) is small, so they take them to be something real from which they benefit. These doubts are like: ﴿a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one takes for water, until when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, or ﴿like darkness in a deep sea, covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds: darkness upon darkness. When he stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he for whom Allah has not appointed light, has no light﴾ [al-Nur: 39–40].

These are the people of guidance and the religion of truth, the possessors of beneficial knowledge and righteous action, who affirmed the Messenger ﷺ in his reports and did not oppose them with doubts, and who obeyed him in his commands and did not neglect them for the sake of desires. They are neither among those who plunge into vain speculation (*al-khawd*), the conjecturers who are heedless in their confusion, nor among those who enjoy their share (*khalaq*) in this world, whose deeds have come to nothing in this world and the Hereafter. Those are the losers.

The light of clear revelation has shone upon them, and in its light they saw the people of darkness wandering in the darkness of their own opinions, going astray in their error, hesitating in their doubt, deceived by the outward appearance of the mirage, barren and dry (*mumhalin mujdibin*) with respect to what Allah the Exalted sent His Messenger ﷺ with of wisdom and decisive speech. What they possess is nothing but the dregs of thoughts and the refuse of minds, with which they are content and at rest, and which they have preferred over the Sunnah and the Qur'an. In their breasts there is nothing but arrogance, which they will never attain, caused for them by the pursuit of desire and the pride of Satan, and for its sake they dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority.

**[Section: The Second Division: The People of Ignorance and Wrongdoing]**

The second division: the people of ignorance and wrongdoing, who combined ignorance of what was brought with wrongdoing through following their own desires. Concerning them Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture and what the souls desire, though there has already come to them guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Najm: 23].

These are of two kinds:

The first: those who think they are upon knowledge and guidance, while they are in fact people of ignorance and misguidance. These are the people of compound ignorance (*al-jahl al-murakkab*), who are ignorant of the truth, oppose it, and oppose its people, and who support falsehood and befriend it and its people. They think they are upon something, but verily they are the liars. Because of their belief in something contrary to what it actually is, they are like the one who sees a mirage, which the thirsty one takes for water, until when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing. Likewise, their deeds and their knowledge are like a mirage that betrays its seeker at the moment he most needs it. It does not stop at mere disappointment and deprivation, as is the case with one who seeks the mirage and finds it is not water. Rather, to that is added that he finds with it the Most Wise of judges and the Most Just of the just, glorified and exalted, Who reckons for him what he has of knowledge and action, and pays him in full, down to the weight of an atom. He turns to the deeds he did, hoping for their benefit, and makes them scattered dust (*hab'an manthura*), because they were not sincerely for His sake, nor according to the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ. Those false doubts he thought were beneficial knowledge likewise become scattered dust, and his deeds and knowledge become a source of regret for him.

The *sarab* (mirage) is what appears in vast deserts at midday from the light of the sun, flowing over the surface of the earth as though it were running water. The *qay'ah* and *qa'* are the flat expanse of land with no mountain or valley in it. Thus Allah likened the knowledge and deeds of one who does not take his knowledge from revelation to a mirage which a traveler sees in the intense heat, so he heads toward it, his expectation is disappointed, and he finds it to be a blazing fire. Likewise, the knowledge and deeds of the people of falsehood, when people are gathered and thirst afflicts them severely, appear to them like a mirage, so they take it for water. When they come to it, they find Allah there, and the angels of punishment seize them and drag them to the blazing Hell, and they are given boiling water to drink, which cuts their intestines. That water they are given is the very knowledge that does not benefit. The deeds which were done for other than Allah the Exalted, Allah makes into boiling water, which He gives them to drink. Likewise their food is *dari'* (a bitter thorny plant) which neither nourishes nor relieves hunger. That is the knowledge and deeds of falsehood which they had in this world, and likewise they neither nourish nor relieve hunger. These are the ones concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who are the greatest losers in their deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 103]. They are the ones referred to in His words: ﴿And We will turn to the deeds they did, and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. And they are the ones referred to in His words: ﴿Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them, and they will not come out of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 167].

**[The People of Darkness]**

The second kind within this category: the people of darkness, who are immersed in ignorance to the point that it has encompassed them from every side. They are like cattle, nay, they are even further astray in the way. As for these, their deeds, which they performed without insight, but merely through imitation and following their forefathers without light from Allah the Exalted, are like *zulumat* (darknesses), the plural of *zulmah* (darkness).
