These are: the darkness of ignorance, the darkness of disbelief, the darkness of wrongdoing and following desire, the darkness of doubt and suspicion, and the darkness of turning away from the truth that Allah the Exalted sent His messengers with, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and the light that He sent down with them to bring people out of darkness into light. The one who turns away from what Allah the Exalted sent Muhammad ﷺ with of guidance and the religion of truth moves about within five darknesses: his speech is darkness, his action is darkness, his entrance is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his destination is darkness. His heart is dark, his face is dark, his speech is dark, and his state is dark. When his bat-like insight (*basirah khuffashiyyah*) confronts the light that Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with, he strives hard to flee from it, and its light almost snatches away his sight, so he flees to the darkness of opinions, which are more fitting and suitable for him, as has been said:

*Bats whom the day has blinded with its light,*
*and who are joined by pieces of the dark night.*

When he comes upon the refuse of thoughts and the scrapings of minds, he roams and leaps about, he brings forth and repeats, he clatters and crashes. But when the light of revelation rises and the sun of prophethood shines forth, he retreats into the holes of insects.

**[Section: On the Interpretation of His Words, "in a deep sea, covered by waves..." (the verse)]**

As for His words, ﴿in a deep sea﴾ [al-Nur: 40], *al-lujji* means deep, ascribed to *lujjat al-bahr*, which is its main depth. His words, ﴿covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds﴾ [al-Nur: 40], are a depiction of the state of the one who turns away from His revelation. He likened the clashing of the waves of doubt and falsehood in his breast to the clashing of the waves of that sea, and that they are waves, some above others. The first pronoun in His words *yaghshahu* (covers it) refers to the sea, and the second pronoun in His words *min fawqihi* (above it) refers to the wave. Then those waves are covered by clouds. Thus there are darknesses here: the darkness of the deep sea, the darkness of the wave above it, and the darkness of the cloud above all of that. If one who is in this sea stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it.

**[Discussion of the Word *Kada* (Almost/Hardly)]**

There has been disagreement concerning the meaning of this. Many grammarians (*nuhat*) said: it is a negation of the approach of seeing it, and this is more emphatic than a negation of seeing, for the occurrence of a thing may be negated while its approach is not negated. So it is as if He said: he did not approach seeing it in any way.

These said: *kada* is one of the verbs of approximation (*af'al al-muqarabah*), and it has the same rule as the other verbs regarding negation and affirmation. So when it is said *kada yaf'alu* (he almost does), it is an affirmation of the approach of the action, and when it is said *lam yakad yaf'alu* (he hardly does), it is a negation of the approach of the action.

Another group said: rather, this indicates that he sees it only after great effort, and in that is an affirmation of seeing it after extreme hardship, because of those darknesses. They said: *kada* has a status that no other verb has, for when it affirms it negates, and when it negates it affirms. So when you say *ma kidtu asilu ilayka* (I could hardly reach you), its meaning is: I reached you after effort and hardship. This is an affirmation of arrival. And when you say *kada Zaydun yaqumu* (Zayd almost stands), it is a negation of his standing, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost crowded upon him﴾ [al-Jinn: 19]. From this is His saying: ﴿And indeed those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes...﴾ [al-Qalam: 51], to the end of the verse. Some of them recited in this regard a riddle:

*Is this grammarian of our age, the word that is used*
*in the tongues of Jurhum and Thamud?*

*When it is used in the form of negation, it is affirmed,*
*and when affirmed, it takes the place of denial.*

A third group said, among them Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Malik and others: its affirmative usage requires the negation of its predicate, as in your saying *kada Zaydun yaqumu* (Zayd almost stands), and its negative usage requires its negation by way of priority. So it, according to him, negates the predicate whether it is negative or affirmative. *Lam yakad Zaydun yaqumu* (Zayd hardly stands) is, according to him, more emphatic in negation than *lam yaqum* (he did not stand). He argued that when it is negated while being a verb of approximation, it negates the approach of the action, which is more emphatic than negating the action itself, and when it is used affirmatively, it requires the approach of its subject to its predicate, which indicates the non-occurrence of the action. He answered the like of His words: ﴿So they slaughtered it, and they hardly did it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 71], to the end of the verse. And the like of the saying: *wasiltu ilayka wa ma kidtu asil* (I reached you, and I could hardly reach), *wa salimtu wa ma kidtu aslam* (I was safe, and I could hardly be safe). He said these are two distinct statements, meaning: I did such and such after I had not been approaching it. The first implies the existence of the action, and the second implies that he was not approaching it but was rather despairing of it. Thus they are two statements with two different purposes.

A fourth group went to distinguish between its past and future forms: when it is affirmative, it indicates the approach of the action whether in the past or future form, and when it is in the negative, if it is in the future form it negates the action and its approach, such as His saying: ﴿he can hardly see it﴾ [al-Nur: 40], and if it is in the past form, it requires affirmation, such as His saying: ﴿So they slaughtered it, and they hardly did it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 71].

These are four approaches of the grammarians to this word. The correct view is that it is a verb which requires approach, and it has the rule of other verbs. The negation of the predicate is not derived from its wording or its lexical form, for it was not coined for negation. Rather, it is derived from the necessary implications of its meaning. For when it requires the approach of the action, the action has not occurred, so it is negated by necessity. As for when it is used in negative form: if it is in a single statement, it negates the approach, as when you say: *la yakadu al-batal yuflih* (the idler hardly succeeds), *wa la yakadu al-bakhil yasud* (the miser hardly leads), *wa la yakadu al-jaban yafrah* (the coward hardly rejoices), and the like. If it is in two statements, it requires the occurrence of the action after it had not been approaching, as Ibn Malik said. This is the verification of its matter. The purpose is that His words ﴿he can hardly see it﴾ [al-Nur: 40] either indicate that he does not even approach seeing it because of the intensity of the darkness, which is the most apparent meaning, and if he does not approach seeing it, how could he see it?

Dhu al-Rummah said:

*When distance has changed the lovers, the trace of love for Mayya does not hardly depart,*
that is: it did not approach departing, so how could it depart?

Thus Allah the Glorified likened their deeds, first, in their failure to benefit and their causing harm to them, to a deceptive mirage which deceives its beholder from afar. When he comes to it, he finds the opposite of what he hoped and expected. And He likened them, second, in their darkness and blackness, because they are false and empty of the light of faith, to layers of darkness in the depths of a sea whose waves clash, over which clouds have covered. How wondrous is this comparison, how brilliant and how precisely matching the condition of the people of innovation and error, and the condition of one who worships Allah, glorified and exalted, contrary to what His Messenger ﷺ was sent with and what His Book sent down.

This comparison of theirs, of their deeds that are false, is by direct correspondence and explicit statement, and of their corrupt knowledge and beliefs by implication. Each of the mirage and the darknesses is an image for the whole of their knowledge and deeds. Their deeds are a mirage with no outcome, and their knowledge is darkness with no light in it.

This is the reverse of the likenesses of the believer's deeds and knowledge, which he received from the niche of prophethood (*mishkat al-nubuwwah*). These are like the rain by which the lands and the servants live, and like the light by which the people of this world and the Hereafter benefit.

For this reason, Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions these two likenesses in the Qur'an in more than one place, for His friends and for His enemies. He mentioned them in Surat al-Baqarah in His words: ﴿Their likeness is like that of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing. Deaf, dumb, blind, so they will not return.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17]

He said in *A'lam al-Muwaqqi'in*:

Allah mentioned two likenesses for the disbelievers: a likeness of a mirage, and a likeness of layered darknesses. This is because those who turn away from guidance and truth are of two kinds.

The first: one who thinks he is upon something, but when the realities are uncovered, it becomes clear to him that it was the opposite of what he supposed. This is the state of the people of ignorance and the people of innovation (*ahl al-bid'ah*) and of desires, who think they are upon guidance and knowledge. When the realities are uncovered, it becomes clear to them that they were not upon anything, and that their beliefs and the deeds built upon them were like a mirage in a barren plain, which the viewer sees as water though there is no reality to it. Likewise are the deeds done for other than Allah and not in accordance with His command: the doer thinks they benefit him, but they do not. These are the deeds about which Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]

Consider Allah's making the mirage be in a *qi'ah*, which is a barren land empty of buildings, trees, plants, and living things. The place of the mirage is a barren land with nothing in it, and the mirage has no reality. That matches their deeds and their hearts, which have become barren of faith and guidance.

Consider also what lies under His words: ﴿The thirsty one thinks it to be water﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. The thirsty one whose thirst has grown intense sees the mirage and supposes it to be water, so he follows it, but he finds nothing. Rather, it betrays him at the time he most needs it. So it is with these people: since their deeds were not in obedience to the Messenger and were for other than Allah, they were made like the mirage. It raised for them what they were most thirsty for and most in need of, but they found nothing. They found Allah there, so He repaid them for their deeds and paid them their account in full.

In the *Sahih*, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith of the manifestation on the Day of Resurrection: "Then Hell will be brought forward, displayed as if it were a mirage. It will be said to the Jews: 'What did you used to worship?' They will say: 'We used to worship 'Uzayr the son of Allah.' It will be said: 'You lie. Allah had no consort or son. So what do you want?' They will say: 'We want You to give us drink.' It will be said: 'Drink,' and they will fall into Hell. Then it will be said to the Christians: 'What did you used to worship?' They will say: 'We used to worship the Messiah the son of Allah.' It will be said to them: 'You lie. Allah had no consort or son. So what do you want?' They will say: 'We want You to give us drink.' It will be said to them: 'Drink,' and they will fall..." and he mentioned the hadith.

This is the state of every possessor of falsehood: his falsehood betrays him at the time he most needs it. Falsehood has no reality; it is, like its name, false. When the belief is not in accordance with the truth and is not right, its object is false. Likewise, when the ultimate aim of a deed is false, like doing a deed for other than Allah or not in accordance with His command, the deed becomes void because its aim is void. Its doer is harmed by that voidness, and by the arrival of the opposite of what he was hoping for. His deed and belief do not vanish without effect for him or against him; rather, he becomes punished by the loss of the benefit and by the arrival of the opposite of benefit. Therefore He, exalted, said: ﴿and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. This is the likeness of the astray one who thinks he is upon guidance.

(Section)

The second kind: those whose likeness is layered darknesses. They are those who knew the truth and guidance but preferred over it the darknesses of falsehood and misguidance. So there accumulated upon them the darkness of the nature (*al-tab'*), the darkness of the self, and the darkness of ignorance, since they did not act upon their knowledge and so became ignorant. And there is the darkness of following error and desire. Their state is like that of one in a deep sea with no shore, covered by a wave, and above that wave another wave, and above it a dark cloud. He is in the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the wave, and the darkness of the cloud. This is the counterpart of what they are in of darknesses, from which Allah has not brought them out into the light of faith.

These two likenesses, of the mirage that he took to be the substance of life, which is water, and of the darknesses opposed to light, are the counterpart of the two likenesses Allah struck for the hypocrites and the believers: the watery likeness and the fiery likeness. He made the share of the believers from them life and illumination, and the share of the hypocrites from them the darkness opposed to light and the death opposed to life. Likewise the disbelievers in these two likenesses: their share of the water is the mirage, which deceives the viewer and has no reality, and their share is the layered darknesses. This may mean the state of every group of the disbelievers, that they lost the substance of life and illumination by turning away from revelation; in that case the two likenesses are two attributes of one described subject. It may also mean a diversity of the states of the disbelievers: that the people of the first likeness are those who acted without knowledge or insight, but upon ignorance and a good opinion of their predecessors, so they thought they were doing good; and the people of the second likeness are those who preferred error over guidance, chose falsehood over truth, became blind to it after they had seen it, and denied it after they had recognized it. This is the state of those who earned anger, and the first is the state of those who went astray. The state of both groups is contrary to the state of those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, mentioned in His words: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp...﴾ [al-Nur: 35], to His words: ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty; and Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 38]. The verses comprised the descriptions of the three groups: those upon whom favor was bestowed, who are the people of light; the astray, who are the people of the mirage; and those who earned anger, who are the people of the layered darknesses. And Allah knows best.

So the first of the two likenesses is for the people of the false deed that does not benefit, and the second is for the people of the knowledge that does not benefit and of false beliefs. Both are opposed to guidance and the religion of truth. For this reason, He described the state of the second group by the turbulence of waves of doubts, suspicions, and corrupt knowledge in their hearts, with the turbulence of the waves of the sea, and that these are layered waves with a dark cloud above them. Likewise are the waves of doubts and suspicions in their dark hearts, upon which the clouds of error, desire, and falsehood have accumulated. So let the discerning person reflect upon the states of the two groups, and let him match between them and the two likenesses. He will know the greatness and sublimity of the Qur'an, and that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.

He, exalted, informed that the cause of this is that He did not place light for them, but left them in the darkness in which they were created, and did not bring them out from it into the light. Indeed, He, glorified, is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light. In the *Musnad* from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, and cast upon them some of His light. Whoever is struck by some of that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray." Therefore I say: the pen has dried upon the knowledge of Allah. Allah created the creation in darkness. Whoever He wills to guide, He places for him an existing light by which He gives life to his heart and his spirit, just as He gives life to his body by the spirit that He breathes into it. So there are two lives: the life of the body by the spirit, and the life of the spirit and the heart by the light. For this reason, Allah, glorified, named revelation a spirit, because true life depends upon it, as He said: ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-Nahl: 2]. And He said: ﴿He casts the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. And He, exalted, said: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. So He made His revelation a spirit and a light. Whoever is not given life by this spirit is dead, and whoever has not been given light from Him is in the darknesses, having no light at all.

These are the ones concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who are the greatest losers in their deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think they are doing good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 103]. They are the ones referred to in His words: ﴿And We will turn to the deeds they did, and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. And they are the ones referred to in His words: ﴿Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets for them, and they will not come out of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 167].

**[The People of Darkness]**

The second kind within this category: the people of darkness, who are immersed in ignorance to the point that it has encompassed them from every side. They are like cattle, nay, they are even further astray in the way. As for these, their deeds, which they performed without insight, but merely through imitation and following their forefathers without light from Allah the Exalted, are like *zulumat* (darknesses), the plural of *zulmah* (darkness). These are: the darkness of ignorance, the darkness of disbelief, the darkness of wrongdoing and following desire, the darkness of doubt and suspicion, and the darkness of turning away from the truth that Allah the Exalted sent His messengers with, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and the light that He sent down with them to bring people out of darkness into light. The one who turns away from what Allah the Exalted sent Muhammad ﷺ with of guidance and the religion of truth moves about within five darknesses: his speech is darkness, his action is darkness, his entrance is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his destination is darkness. His heart is dark, his face is dark, his speech is dark, and his state is dark. When his bat-like insight (*basirah khuffashiyyah*) confronts the light that Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with, he strives hard to flee from it, and its light almost snatches away his sight, so he flees to the darkness of opinions, which are more fitting and suitable for him, as has been said:

*Bats whom the day has blinded with its light,*
*and who are joined by pieces of the dark night.*

When he comes upon the refuse of thoughts and the scrapings of minds, he roams and leaps about, he brings forth and repeats, he clatters and crashes. But when the light of revelation rises and the sun of prophethood shines forth, he retreats into the holes of insects.

**[Section: On the Interpretation of His Words, "in a deep sea, covered by waves..." (the verse)]**

As for His words, ﴿in a deep sea﴾ [al-Nur: 40], *al-lujji* means deep, ascribed to *lujjat al-bahr*, which is its main depth. His words, ﴿covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds﴾ [al-Nur: 40], are a depiction of the state of the one who turns away from His revelation. He likened the clashing of the waves of doubt and falsehood in his breast to the clashing of the waves of that sea, and that they are waves, some above others. The first pronoun in His words *yaghshahu* (covers it) refers to the sea, and the second pronoun in His words *min fawqihi* (above it) refers to the wave. Then those waves are covered by clouds. Thus there are darknesses here: the darkness of the deep sea, the darkness of the wave above it, and the darkness of the cloud above all of that. If one who is in this sea stretches out his hand, he can hardly see it.

**[Discussion of the Word *Kada* (Almost/Hardly)]**

There has been disagreement concerning the meaning of this. Many grammarians (*nuhat*) said: it is a negation of the approach of seeing it, and this is more emphatic than a negation of seeing, for the occurrence of a thing may be negated while its approach is not negated. So it is as if He said: he did not approach seeing it in any way.

These said: *kada* is one of the verbs of approximation (*af'al al-muqarabah*), and it has the same rule as the other verbs regarding negation and affirmation. So when it is said *kada yaf'alu* (he almost does), it is an affirmation of the approach of the action, and when it is said *lam yakad yaf'alu* (he hardly does), it is a negation of the approach of the action.

Another group said: rather, this indicates that he sees it only after great effort, and in that is an affirmation of seeing it after extreme hardship, because of those darknesses. They said: *kada* has a status that no other verb has, for when it affirms it negates, and when it negates it affirms. So when you say *ma kidtu asilu ilayka* (I could hardly reach you), its meaning is: I reached you after effort and hardship. This is an affirmation of arrival. And when you say *kada Zaydun yaqumu* (Zayd almost stands), it is a negation of his standing, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost crowded upon him﴾ [al-Jinn: 19]. From this is His saying: ﴿And indeed those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes...﴾ [al-Qalam: 51], to the end of the verse. Some of them recited in this regard a riddle:

*Is this grammarian of our age, the word that is used*
*in the tongues of Jurhum and Thamud?*

*When it is used in the form of negation, it is affirmed,*
*and when affirmed, it takes the place of denial.*

A third group said, among them Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Malik and others: its affirmative usage requires the negation of its predicate, as in your saying *kada Zaydun yaqumu* (Zayd almost stands), and its negative usage requires its negation by way of priority. So it, according to him, negates the predicate whether it is negative or affirmative. *Lam yakad Zaydun yaqumu* (Zayd hardly stands) is, according to him, more emphatic in negation than *lam yaqum* (he did not stand). He argued that when it is negated while being a verb of approximation, it negates the approach of the action, which is more emphatic than negating the action itself, and when it is used affirmatively, it requires the approach of its subject to its predicate, which indicates the non-occurrence of the action. He answered the like of His words: ﴿So they slaughtered it, and they hardly did it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 71], to the end of the verse. And the like of the saying: *wasiltu ilayka wa ma kidtu asil* (I reached you, and I could hardly reach), *wa salimtu wa ma kidtu aslam* (I was safe, and I could hardly be safe). He said these are two distinct statements, meaning: I did such and such after I had not been approaching it. The first implies the existence of the action, and the second implies that he was not approaching it but was rather despairing of it. Thus they are two statements with two different purposes.

A fourth group went to distinguish between its past and future forms: when it is affirmative, it indicates the approach of the action whether in the past or future form, and when it is in the negative, if it is in the future form it negates the action and its approach, such as His saying: ﴿he can hardly see it﴾ [al-Nur: 40], and if it is in the past form, it requires affirmation, such as His saying: ﴿So they slaughtered it, and they hardly did it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 71].

These are four approaches of the grammarians to this word. The correct view is that it is a verb which requires approach, and it has the rule of other verbs. The negation of the predicate is not derived from its wording or its lexical form, for it was not coined for negation. Rather, it is derived from the necessary implications of its meaning. For when it requires the approach of the action, the action has not occurred, so it is negated by necessity. As for when it is used in negative form: if it is in a single statement, it negates the approach, as when you say: *la yakadu al-batal yuflih* (the idler hardly succeeds), *wa la yakadu al-bakhil yasud* (the miser hardly leads), *wa la yakadu al-jaban yafrah* (the coward hardly rejoices), and the like. If it is in two statements, it requires the occurrence of the action after it had not been approaching, as Ibn Malik said. This is the verification of its matter. The purpose is that His words ﴿he can hardly see it﴾ [al-Nur: 40] either indicate that he does not even approach seeing it because of the intensity of the darkness, which is the most apparent meaning, and if he does not approach seeing it, how could he see it?

Dhu al-Rummah said:

*When distance has changed the lovers, the trace of love for Mayya does not hardly depart,*
that is: it did not approach departing, so how could it depart?

Thus Allah the Glorified likened their deeds, first, in their failure to benefit and their causing harm to them, to a deceptive mirage which deceives its beholder from afar. When he comes to it, he finds the opposite of what he hoped and expected. And He likened them, second, in their darkness and blackness, because they are false and empty of the light of faith, to layers of darkness in the depths of a sea whose waves clash, over which clouds have covered. How wondrous is this comparison, how brilliant and how precisely matching the condition of the people of innovation and error, and the condition of one who worships Allah, glorified and exalted, contrary to what His Messenger ﷺ was sent with and what His Book sent down.

This comparison of theirs, of their deeds that are false, is by direct correspondence and explicit statement, and of their corrupt knowledge and beliefs by implication. Each of the mirage and the darknesses is an image for the whole of their knowledge and deeds. Their deeds are a mirage with no outcome, and their knowledge is darkness with no light in it.

This is the reverse of the likenesses of the believer's deeds and knowledge, which he received from the niche of prophethood (*mishkat al-nubuwwah*). These are like the rain by which the lands and the servants live, and like the light by which the people of this world and the Hereafter benefit.

For this reason, Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions these two likenesses in the Qur'an in more than one place, for His friends and for His enemies. He mentioned them in Surat al-Baqarah in His words: ﴿Their likeness is like that of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing. Deaf, dumb, blind, so they will not return.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17]

He said in *A'lam al-Muwaqqi'in*:

Allah mentioned two likenesses for the disbelievers: a likeness of a mirage, and a likeness of layered darknesses. This is because those who turn away from guidance and truth are of two kinds.

The first: one who thinks he is upon something, but when the realities are uncovered, it becomes clear to him that it was the opposite of what he supposed. This is the state of the people of ignorance and the people of innovation (*ahl al-bid'ah*) and of desires, who think they are upon guidance and knowledge. When the realities are uncovered, it becomes clear to them that they were not upon anything, and that their beliefs and the deeds built upon them were like a mirage in a barren plain, which the viewer sees as water though there is no reality to it. Likewise are the deeds done for other than Allah and not in accordance with His command: the doer thinks they benefit him, but they do not. These are the deeds about which Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]

Consider Allah's making the mirage be in a *qi'ah*, which is a barren land empty of buildings, trees, plants, and living things. The place of the mirage is a barren land with nothing in it, and the mirage has no reality. That matches their deeds and their hearts, which have become barren of faith and guidance.

Consider also what lies under His words: ﴿The thirsty one thinks it to be water﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. The thirsty one whose thirst has grown intense sees the mirage and supposes it to be water, so he follows it, but he finds nothing. Rather, it betrays him at the time he most needs it. So it is with these people: since their deeds were not in obedience to the Messenger and were for other than Allah, they were made like the mirage. It raised for them what they were most thirsty for and most in need of, but they found nothing. They found Allah there, so He repaid them for their deeds and paid them their account in full.

In the *Sahih*, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith of the manifestation on the Day of Resurrection: "Then Hell will be brought forward, displayed as if it were a mirage. It will be said to the Jews: 'What did you used to worship?' They will say: 'We used to worship 'Uzayr the son of Allah.' It will be said: 'You lie. Allah had no consort or son. So what do you want?' They will say: 'We want You to give us drink.' It will be said: 'Drink,' and they will fall into Hell. Then it will be said to the Christians: 'What did you used to worship?' They will say: 'We used to worship the Messiah the son of Allah.' It will be said to them: 'You lie. Allah had no consort or son. So what do you want?' They will say: 'We want You to give us drink.' It will be said to them: 'Drink,' and they will fall..." and he mentioned the hadith.

This is the state of every possessor of falsehood: his falsehood betrays him at the time he most needs it. Falsehood has no reality; it is, like its name, false. When the belief is not in accordance with the truth and is not right, its object is false. Likewise, when the ultimate aim of a deed is false, like doing a deed for other than Allah or not in accordance with His command, the deed becomes void because its aim is void. Its doer is harmed by that voidness, and by the arrival of the opposite of what he was hoping for. His deed and belief do not vanish without effect for him or against him; rather, he becomes punished by the loss of the benefit and by the arrival of the opposite of benefit. Therefore He, exalted, said: ﴿and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. This is the likeness of the astray one who thinks he is upon guidance.

(Section)

The second kind: those whose likeness is layered darknesses. They are those who knew the truth and guidance but preferred over it the darknesses of falsehood and misguidance. So there accumulated upon them the darkness of the nature (*al-tab'*), the darkness of the self, and the darkness of ignorance, since they did not act upon their knowledge and so became ignorant. And there is the darkness of following error and desire. Their state is like that of one in a deep sea with no shore, covered by a wave, and above that wave another wave, and above it a dark cloud. He is in the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the wave, and the darkness of the cloud. This is the counterpart of what they are in of darknesses, from which Allah has not brought them out into the light of faith.

These two likenesses, of the mirage that he took to be the substance of life, which is water, and of the darknesses opposed to light, are the counterpart of the two likenesses Allah struck for the hypocrites and the believers: the watery likeness and the fiery likeness. He made the share of the believers from them life and illumination, and the share of the hypocrites from them the darkness opposed to light and the death opposed to life. Likewise the disbelievers in these two likenesses: their share of the water is the mirage, which deceives the viewer and has no reality, and their share is the layered darknesses. This may mean the state of every group of the disbelievers, that they lost the substance of life and illumination by turning away from revelation; in that case the two likenesses are two attributes of one described subject. It may also mean a diversity of the states of the disbelievers: that the people of the first likeness are those who acted without knowledge or insight, but upon ignorance and a good opinion of their predecessors, so they thought they were doing good; and the people of the second likeness are those who preferred error over guidance, chose falsehood over truth, became blind to it after they had seen it, and denied it after they had recognized it. This is the state of those who earned anger, and the first is the state of those who went astray. The state of both groups is contrary to the state of those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, mentioned in His words: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp...﴾ [al-Nur: 35], to His words: ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty; and Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 38]. The verses comprised the descriptions of the three groups: those upon whom favor was bestowed, who are the people of light; the astray, who are the people of the mirage; and those who earned anger, who are the people of the layered darknesses. And Allah knows best.

So the first of the two likenesses is for the people of the false deed that does not benefit, and the second is for the people of the knowledge that does not benefit and of false beliefs. Both are opposed to guidance and the religion of truth. For this reason, He described the state of the second group by the turbulence of waves of doubts, suspicions, and corrupt knowledge in their hearts, with the turbulence of the waves of the sea, and that these are layered waves with a dark cloud above them. Likewise are the waves of doubts and suspicions in their dark hearts, upon which the clouds of error, desire, and falsehood have accumulated. So let the discerning person reflect upon the states of the two groups, and let him match between them and the two likenesses. He will know the greatness and sublimity of the Qur'an, and that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.

He, exalted, informed that the cause of this is that He did not place light for them, but left them in the darkness in which they were created, and did not bring them out from it into the light. Indeed, He, glorified, is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light. In the *Musnad* from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, and cast upon them some of His light. Whoever is struck by some of that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray." Therefore I say: the pen has dried upon the knowledge of Allah. Allah created the creation in darkness. Whoever He wills to guide, He places for him an existing light by which He gives life to his heart and his spirit, just as He gives life to his body by the spirit that He breathes into it. So there are two lives: the life of the body by the spirit, and the life of the spirit and the heart by the light. For this reason, Allah, glorified, named revelation a spirit, because true life depends upon it, as He said: ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-Nahl: 2]. And He said: ﴿He casts the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. And He, exalted, said: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. So He made His revelation a spirit and a light. Whoever is not given life by this spirit is dead, and whoever has not been given light from Him is in the darknesses, having no light at all.

(Section)

Imam Ahmad said: Those who argue that the dog is pure cite the words of Allah Almighty: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water﴾.

The unrestricted application of "water" implies purity.

It was also said: There is nothing to prevent Allah from transforming its substance into impurity, as with grape juice that turns into wine, or water that turns into urine.

(Section)

The words of Allah Almighty: ﴿Of them is one that walks on its belly﴾, and likewise ﴿on four﴾, indicate the use of (man, "who" or "whoever") for those who do not reason.

On this there are two views.

The first: the opening of the verse is the words of Allah Almighty: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water﴾, so all moving creatures are gathered together, including the rational ones such as humans and the non-rational ones such as beasts.

The rule is: when the rational and the non-rational are gathered together, the rational takes precedence. Since the division that follows is a division of rational beings only.

The second view: it corresponds to "walks" in His words: ﴿Of them is one that walks on two legs﴾, so it departs from the original usage for the sake of the required correspondence.

It was also said that (ma, "what") is also used for rational beings, as in His words: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾.

It was answered that (ma) here is a verbal-noun particle, its meaning being: nor are you worshippers of my worship, nor am I a worshipper of your worship. So (ma) is used only for what does not reason.

They gave the same answer regarding His words: ﴿And a soul and Him who fashioned it﴾. However, a difficulty arose for them concerning the pronoun in His words: ﴿Then He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety﴾, since the verbal-noun (ma) is a particle to which pronouns do not refer.

Some of them accepted that the pronoun refers back to it, meaning the verbal-noun (ma).

And this is weak.

(Section)

These inanimate things and animals of differing shapes, sizes, attributes, benefits, powers, foods, and plants, which are likewise, contain such wisdom and benefits that the nations have greatly described them and tested them over the passing ages, yet they have reached from them only the most trivial and least of things. Indeed, even if all the nations were to agree, they would not comprehend the knowledge of all the wisdom and interests deposited in a single one of these kinds. Besides this, there is in them the lesson and the clear indication of the existence of the Creator, His will, His choice, His knowledge, His power and His wisdom. For a single substance by itself cannot bear this strange form, these varied shapes, benefits and attributes, nor if it were combined with others; nor is the coming into being of these kinds and forms by the mere act of combination, nor does combination bestow it. Thus the occurrence of this diversity, variation and difference in animals and plants is among the greatest signs of the Lord, the Exalted, and proofs of His lordship, power, wisdom and knowledge, and that He is the doer of what He wills by choice and will. So the diversifying of His creatures and their coming into being one after another is among the most manifest proofs. Consider how the Qur'an guided to this in more than one place, such as His words: ﴿And in the earth are neighbouring tracts, and gardens of vines, and crops, and palm trees, some multiple and some single, watered with one water; yet We make some of them excel others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships that run in the sea with what benefits people, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, and dispersing in it every kind of moving creature, and the directing of the winds and the clouds made subservient between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who reason﴾.

And His words: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your tongues and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those who know﴾. And His words: ﴿It is He who sent down from the sky water, from which you have drink and from which grow trees in which you pasture your herds. By it He causes to grow for you crops, olives, palm trees, vines and all kinds of fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾.

And His words, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water. Of them is one that walks on its belly, and of them is one that walks on two legs, and of them is one that walks on four. Allah creates what He wills; indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾. So consider how, by the difference of animals in walking, while they share one substance, He, glorified be He, drew attention to the difference in what lies beyond that: their organs, shapes, powers, actions, foods and dwellings. Thus He pointed to both the commonality and the difference, indicating a small part of it. All birds share feathers and wings, yet differ enormously beyond that.

Solid-hoofed animals share the hoof, such as the horse, the donkey and the mule, and differ beyond that.

Cloven-hoofed animals share the cloven hoof and differ in other respects.

Horned animals share horns and differ in creation, benefits and shapes.

Aquatic animals share being swimmers in which they dwell and are formed, and differ with the greatest difference, which humans have until now been unable to enumerate.

Wild beasts share distance from people and remoteness from them and their dwellings, and differ in their attributes, shapes, natures and actions with a difference beyond human ability to count.

Those among them that walk on the belly share this, and their kinds differ.

Those that walk on two legs share this, and their kinds differ with the greatest difference. Each of these kinds has knowledge, perception and cunning to bring about its benefits and repel its harms, and many of them outdo the human kind in this. Among the greatest wisdoms is the clear indication of knowing the one Creator who, by His power, might and wisdom, dominates all of this, such that all of them came obedient, submissive and driven toward what He created them for, in accordance with His will and wisdom. This is the most telling evidence of His overpowering strength, His profound wisdom and His all-encompassing knowledge. Thus one knows the comprehensiveness of one power, one knowledge and one wisdom, namely, by the kind, from one Capable, one Wise, over all these kinds and their multiples, which human reason does not know, as He said: ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾.

And He said: ﴿So I swear by what you see and what you do not see﴾.

He gathers the ends of His action, the wisdom of His creation and His command into one end, which is the ultimate of ends, namely the true divinity, all other divinity besides which is falsehood and impossibility. It is the end of ends. Then He descends from it to other ends, which are means in relation to it and ends in relation to what is below them: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final goal﴾. Beyond Him there is no known, sought or mentioned thing except pure nothingness. In existence there is only Allah and His effects, which are the traces of His actions, and His actions are traces of His attributes, and His attributes subsist in Him as necessary consequences of His essence.

The point is that the sought ends are knowledge, by the comprehensive knowledge of one Knower, of one action from one Agent, of one power from one Capable, and of one wisdom from one Wise, of all that is in it despite its differences, and that the ends of His action and command converge on one end. This is among the clearest proofs of the oneness of divinity, just as all things began from one Creator, one Capable and one Lord. The two matters, namely the oneness of lordship and the oneness of divinity, are indicated by the single order and the comprehensive wisdom that gathers diverse kinds together with their opposites and their differing, and by the dependence of some of them on others, their interweaving with one another, their mutual assistance and their connection to one another, which show that they are the handiwork of one Maker and one Lord. For had there been with Him other gods and lords, the kings of this world would not be content for the slave of one of them to need the slave of another like him, because of the deficiency and defect this entails, contrary to perfect power and self-sufficiency. The orderly arrangement of their existence, their standing in their stability, their difference, and their being in the most perfect and finest of forms, also indicates that they all terminate in one end and one sought object, namely their true God and their supreme Worshipped, besides whom they have no god and no one worshipped by them.

Consider, then, how the difference of existing things, their stability, their gathering in what they share, and their separation in what they differ, point to one God and one Lord, and point to the attributes of His perfection and the qualities of His majesty.

(Section)

Then consider first the quadrupeds among animals: how you see them following their mothers, independent in themselves, not needing to be carried and nurtured as human children need. Because their mothers do not have what human mothers have of nurture, tenderness, gentleness and detached and attached instruments, the Subtle, the All-Aware gave them the ability to rise and stand on their own soon after birth. For this reason you see the chicks of many birds, such as hens, partridges and the fatha, moving about and pecking as soon as they come out of the egg. And those with weak standing, like the chicks of pigeons and doves, He, glorified be He, gave their mothers, out of His bounty, tenderness, compassion and affection, so that they regurgitate food from their crops into the chicks' mouths, storing it in the most precious place within them and then driving it from their mouths into the chicks' beaks.

They keep doing this until the chick rises and stands on its own. All this is from their share and portion, which reached them from the one mercy out of a hundred. Then when it stands on its own and is able to fly, the two parents keep treating it with the most complete and gentlest care, until it flies from its nest and seeks its own provision, and eats from where they eat, as though they had never known it and it had never known them. Indeed they drive it away from the nest, and do not leave it, though their sustenance is between them, but they say to it in a language it understands: "Make for yourself a nest and food, for you have no nest or food with us."

So ask the one who denies the Creator: Is all this mere neglect? Who inspired them to do this? Who inclined them toward the chicks when they were small and most in need of them, and then withdrew this from them when the chicks became self-sufficient, out of mercy toward the parents, who would otherwise strive for their own interests? For had this continued for them, it would have harmed them and distracted them from their livelihood, especially given how much their offspring need food. So He placed in them mercy, altruism and tenderness out of mercy toward the chicks, and removed it when they became self-sufficient, out of mercy toward the parents. Could all this occur without a wise Governor, without care and kindness from Him, glorified and exalted be He? The proofs of His lordship, the evidences of His divinity, the signs of His wisdom and the signs of His power have been established. So the intellect cannot deny them, except as mere arrogance on the tongue, of every ungrateful denier: ﴿Is there doubt about Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾

Doubt arises only regarding what its indications are obscure and its proofs unclear. As for one who has in every perceptible or intelligible thing a sign, indeed signs, conveying from Him and bearing witness to Him that He is Allah, there is no god but Him, Lord of the worlds, how could there be doubt about Him?

(Section)

Then consider the profound wisdom in the limbs of animals: how it required that they be paired, not single, either two or four, so that walking and moving would be possible for them and their welfare be complete. For if they were single, it would not suit them for this, because the walker moves with some of its limbs and relies on others. The two-legged moves one and relies on the other, and the four-legged moves two and relies on two, in alternation. For if it moved two limbs from one side and relied on two from the other side, its limbs would not stay firm on the ground during its movement, and its walking would be a hopping like the hopping of a bird. That would harm it and exhaust it, as it would move its body, unlike the bird. This is why when a human walks like that for a short while, it exhausts and tires him, unlike the natural gait which is proper to him. So wisdom required the advancing of the right of the hands together with the left of the feet, and keeping the left of the hands and the right of the feet, and then moving the other two in the same way. This is the easiest and lightest kind of walking for animals.

(Section)

Then consider the striking wisdom in the face of the beast: how you see its two eyes fixed forward so that it can see what is before it more fully than other creatures, because it guards itself and its rider, and avoids striking a wall or falling into a pit. Its eyes were made like the eyes of an upright creature, because it is a sentinel. Its mouth was made split at the bottom of the snout so that it can bite and grasp fodder. For if it were above, at the front of the snout as it is in a human at the front of the chin, it could not take anything from the ground.

Do you not see that a human does not take food with his mouth but with his hand? Since the beast does not take its food with its paw, its snout was made split at its lower part so that it can place it on the fodder, then crop it. It was assisted with the upper lip, which for it is like the lip for the human, to gather what is near and far.

The benefit of the tail has been unclear to some people, and they have not been guided to it, though it has several benefits. Among them: it serves as a cover over the anus, a veil that conceals and covers the two orifices.

Among them: between the anus and the lower belly of the beast there is a place where flies and mosquitoes gather and harm the beast, so its tails serve as fly-whisks and fans to drive that away.

Among them: the beast finds rest in moving its tail from side to side. For since its standing is on four limbs with its whole body, and its legs are occupied with bearing the body and cannot shift and turn, the moving of the tail gives it relief.

Perhaps there are other wisdoms in it which the understandings of creatures fall short of, and which the hearer would belittle if they were presented to him, for he does not know their place except at the time of need. Among these: when the beast sinks down into mud, nothing helps more in lifting it than taking hold of its tail.

**[Section: The Servants' Absolute Need to Know the Messenger]**

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after a lengthy discussion:

From this you learn that the servants' need, above every other need, is to know the Messenger and what he brought, to affirm what he reported, and to obey what he commanded. There is no path to happiness and success, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, except through the hands of the Messengers. There is no way to know the good from the bad in detail except through them. The pleasure of Allah is never attained except through them. Therefore, the good in deeds, words, and character is nothing but their guidance and what they brought. They are the sound balance by which words, character, and deeds are weighed, and by following them the people of guidance are distinguished from the people of misguidance. The need for them is greater than the body's need for its soul, the eye's need for its light, and the soul's need for its life.

Whatever necessity or need is imagined, the servant's necessity and need for the Messengers exceeds it by far.

And consider the one who, if his guidance and what he brought were absent from you for the blink of an eye, your heart would become corrupt, and you would become like the fish when it leaves the water and is placed in the frying pan. The condition of the servant when his heart is separated from what the Messengers brought is like this condition, rather worse. But only a living heart feels this, and:

*"The wounded feel no pain when they are dead."*

Since the servant's happiness in both abodes is tied to the guidance of the Prophet (ﷺ), it is obligatory upon everyone who counsels his own soul and loves its salvation and happiness to know, from his guidance, his conduct, and his affairs, that which takes him out of the ranks of those ignorant of him, and enters him among his followers, his partisans, and his party. People in this matter are divided into those who are content with little, those who strive for much, and those who are deprived. Bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of tremendous bounty.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 24, verse 58:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not reached puberty among you ask permission of you three times﴾ — the verse.

He, exalted is He, commanded the believing slaves, and those among them who have not reached puberty, to seek permission to enter upon them at these three times, lest their entering unannounced, without permission, at these times become a means of their glimpsing their private parts (ʿawrāt) at the time of removing their clothes, at the midday rest (qāʾilah), at sleep, and upon waking. He did not command them to seek permission at other times, even though avoiding this harm was possible, because such occurrences are rare and rarely lead to it; so those other times were treated as a preliminary (muqaddimah).

[Section: The permission of slaves and those who have not reached puberty during the three private times]

As for the permission which God commanded of the slaves and of those who have not reached puberty during the three private times — before the dawn prayer, at midday, and at sleep — Ibn ʿAbbās used to command it and would say: "People have abandoned acting upon it." A group said: the verse is abrogated (mansūkhah), but they did not bring any proof.

Another group said: it is a command of recommendation (nadb) and guidance (irshād), not a binding decree (ḥatm) and obligation (ījāb), and there is nothing with it that indicates diverting the command from its apparent meaning.

Another group said: the one commanded in this is women specifically, while men seek permission at all times. This is clearly invalid, for the plural "alladhīna" is not specific to the feminine, although it may be applied to them along with males by way of precedence (taghlīb).

Another group said the opposite: that the one commanded in this is men, not women, looking at the word "alladhīna" in both places; but the context of the verse rejects this, so reflect upon it.

Another group said: the command to seek permission at that time was for a need, and then that need ceased; and a ruling which is established by a reason ends when that reason ends. Abū Dāwūd related in his Sunan that some men from the people of Iraq said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "O Ibn ʿAbbās! How do you view this verse, in which we were commanded what we were commanded, and yet no one acts upon it: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾ — the verse."

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Indeed God is Wise and Merciful to the believers, He loves concealment (sitr). People did not have curtains or screens for their houses, so a servant, or a child, or a man's orphan girl might enter while the man was with his family. So God commanded them to seek permission at those private times. Then God brought them curtains and goodness, and I have not seen anyone acting upon it since."

Some have denied the authenticity of this report from Ibn ʿAbbās, and criticised ʿIkrimah, and it did not benefit them. They also criticised ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, client of al-Muṭṭalib, though both authors of the Ṣaḥīḥ relied upon him; so denying this is obstinacy and improbable assumption with no basis.

Another group said: the verse is muḥkam (definitive), general, with no opposing or repelling evidence, and acting upon it is obligatory, even if most people abandon it.

The sound view is this: if there is something which takes the place of seeking permission, such as opening a door whose opening is a sign of entering, or lifting a curtain, or the coming and going of those inside and outside and the like, then that suffices in place of seeking permission. But if there is nothing that takes its place, then it is necessary. The ruling is linked to a reason (muʿallal) which the verse has indicated; so when the reason is present, the ruling is present, and when it is absent, the ruling is absent. And God knows best.

(A Note of Subtlety)

He did not mention the houses of the children, because they are included within their own houses (i.e., the houses of the believers themselves). So he sufficed with mentioning those and not these; otherwise, their houses are closer than the houses of those mentioned in the verse.

[Section: The Sickness of the Bodies]

As for the sickness of the bodies, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, [for them to eat from your houses]﴾ [al-Nur: 61].

He mentioned the sickness of the body in connection with the Hajj, the fasting, and the ablution, for a wondrous secret which shows you the greatness of the Qur'an, and the sufficiency of it for whoever understands and comprehends it, without anything else. That is because the rules of the medicine of the bodies are three: preserving health, protecting oneself from what harms, and expelling corrupt humours. So He, glorified is He, mentioned these three principles in these three places.

He said, in the verse of fasting: ﴿So whoever among you is sick or on a journey, then [prescribed is] a number of other days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 184].

So He permitted breaking the fast for the sick because of the excuse of illness, and for the traveller, seeking the preservation of his health and strength, lest fasting during travel should take them away, due to the combination of intense movement, what it necessitates of dissolution, and the lack of nourishment that would replace what has dissolved, so that strength weakens and declines. Thus He permitted the traveller to break the fast, preserving his health and strength from what weakens them.

And He said, in the verse of Hajj: ﴿So whoever among you is sick or has an ailment of the head, then an expiation of fasting or charity or a sacrifice﴾ [al-Baqarah: 196].

So He permitted the sick, and whoever has an ailment of the head such as lice or itching or other than these, to shave his head while in the state of ihram, as an expulsion of the matter of the corrupt vapours which had caused him harm in his head by their being confined beneath the hair. When he shaves his head, the pores open, and those vapours come out of them. This expulsion is analogous to every expulsion whose confinement causes harm.

The things whose confinement and resistance cause harm are ten: blood when it agitates, semen when it becomes excessive, urine, faeces, wind, vomiting, sneezing, sleep, hunger, and thirst.

Each one of these ten, its confinement necessitates a disease of the diseases according to its measure.

Allah, glorified is He, has alerted by the expulsion of the lowest of them, which is the vapour confined in the head, to the expulsion of what is more difficult than it, as is the method of the Qur'an: alerting by the lower to the higher.

As for protection (al-himyah): Allah the Exalted said in the verse of ablution: ﴿And if you are sick or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾ [al-Nisa: 43].

So He permitted the sick to turn from water to dust, as a protection for him from his body being touched by what harms him. This is an alert to protection from every harm to him, from within or from without. Indeed, He, glorified is He, guided His servants to the principles of medicine and the essentials of its rules. We will mention the guidance of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in this, and show that his guidance in it is the most perfect guidance.

As for the medicine of the hearts, it is entrusted to the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, and there is no way to attain it except from them and through them. The soundness of hearts is that they know their Lord and their Creator, His names, attributes, acts and rulings, and that they prefer His pleasure and what He loves, avoiding what He forbids and what angers Him. There is no health for them and no life whatsoever except by this, and there is no way to receive it except from the Messengers. What is assumed of attaining soundness of the heart without following them is an error on the part of whoever assumes it; rather, that is the life and health and strength of the bestial, appetitive soul, and the life, health and strength of the heart are far removed from that. Whoever does not distinguish between this and that, let him weep over the life of his heart, for he is among the dead, and over its light, for he is immersed in seas of darkness.

[Section: The Medicine of the Bodies]

As for the medicine of the bodies: it is of two kinds.

One kind is that which Allah has instinctively placed in animals, both rational and brute. This does not require the treatment of a physician, such as the remedy for hunger, thirst, cold and fatigue, by their opposites and what removes them.

The second is that which requires thought and reflection, such as the repelling of similar diseases that arise in the temperament so that it departs from balance, either towards heat, cold, dryness, or moisture, or what is composed of two of these. These are of two kinds: either material or qualitative; that is, either by the pouring of a matter, or by the occurrence of a quality. The difference between them is that qualitative diseases occur after the removal of the matters which caused them, so their matters disappear and their effect remains as a quality in the temperament.

As for material diseases, their causes remain with them and sustain them; when the cause of the disease is present with it, consideration of the cause must come first, then of the disease second, then of the remedy third. Or the instrumental diseases, which are those that take an organ out of its form, either in shape, cavity, passage, roughness, smoothness, number, bone, or position; for these organs, when they are joined together and the body is composed of them, their joining is called connection, and departure from balance in it is called dissolution of connection. Or the general diseases which affect both the similar and the instrumental.

The similar diseases are those by which the temperament departs from balance, and this departure is called a disease once it harms in fact, with perceptible harm.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 24, verse 63:

He, glorified is He, commanded that His Messenger not be called in the manner in which people call one another, but rather it should be said: "O Messenger of Allah."

He should not be called "O Muhammad." Rather, he would be named by his name only when addressed by the disbelievers.

As for the Muslims, they would address him as "O Messenger of Allah." And if this is the case in addressing him directly, then likewise in his absence it is not fitting to treat what is used to call him as being of the same kind as what we use to call one another. Rather, he should be invoked with the most noble form of supplication, which is salutation upon him (ﷺ). It is well known that mercy is invoked for every Muslim, and even for non-human animals, as in the prayer for rain: "O Allah, have mercy on Your servants, Your lands, and Your livestock."

He said in al-Madarij (Madarij al-Salikin):

Among the etiquette with him is that one should not make his supplication like the supplication of others.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like your calling of one another﴾.

Regarding this, there are two opinions among the exegetes (mufassirun).

The first: that you should not call him by his name, as some of you call others, but rather say: "O Messenger of Allah" and "O Prophet of Allah." According to this, the verbal noun (masdar) is in the genitive construction with its object, meaning: your calling of the Messenger.

The second: that the meaning is: do not make his calling of you equivalent to your calling of one another. If he wills, he responds, and if he wills, he leaves it; rather, when he calls you, there is no escape for you from responding to him, and you have no leeway to hold back from it at all. According to this, the verbal noun is in the genitive construction with its agent, meaning: his calling of you.
